name: Object Between the Lines
blueprint: Full-viewport section, min-height 100svh, padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem) clamp(1rem, 5vw, 4rem). Headline is an h1 with two block spans: line one top-aligned, line two bottom-aligned, size clamp(3rem, 10vw, 10rem), line-height 0.9. Between them a gap element whose height is a CSS variable --gap, starting at 0.4em and opening to clamp(14rem, 34vw, 30rem). A WebGL canvas (the product: bottle, sneaker, speaker) is absolutely centred in that gap at z-index 1; the headline spans sit at z-index 2 but never overlap the object footprint. Below line two: one-sentence deck at clamp(1rem, 1.4vw, 1.25rem), primary CTA and price chip. States: idle (lines parted, object slowly turning), hover on canvas (object faces cursor up to 12deg), in-view, done (gap fully open, CTA focusable).
motion: Load: lines start almost touching, then part over 900ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) while the object scales from 0.6 to 1 into the opening. Scroll progress 0-40%: object rotates 0 to 120deg on Y. 40-80%: lines drift a further 6vh apart and the object tilts to show its underside. 80-100%: object settles at three-quarter view, a soft floor shadow sharpens, CTA lifts 8px into place.
still_check: At 50% both headline lines are fully set and readable above and below a fully lit product, no letters cut by the canvas, CTA visible. 25% shows the object front-on with a tighter gap; 75% shows it tilted with wider spacing.
mobile: At 375px the gap opens to 62vw and the object renders as a pre-rendered poster image unless the device reports good GPU memory. Scroll rotation is replaced by a single 1.2s turntable on first view. Lines drop to clamp(2.6rem, 13vw, 3.4rem).
a11y: h1 is one element read as a single sentence; the canvas is aria-hidden with an adjacent visually hidden product description. Reduced motion: lines start parted, object static at three-quarter view. CTA keeps a 3px focus-visible ring with 3:1 contrast against the backdrop.
avoid: Object drifting over letters, gap collapsing into an empty band before the model loads (show a poster image first), layout shift when --gap animates (reserve final height), scroll hijack that pins longer than one viewport.

stack_notes.css: Lines as grid rows; gap row height animated with animation-timeline: view() on a registered @property --gap. Poster image sits in the gap with a CSS rotateY via view() timeline for the turn. IntersectionObserver adds an in-view class where scroll timelines are unsupported.
stack_notes.js: three.js or raw WebGL renders the model into a canvas sized to the gap rect, measured with ResizeObserver. rAF reads section progress 0..1 from getBoundingClientRect and maps it to rotation and gap height. Pause rendering when out of view; dispose geometry, textures and the renderer on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Seam-Split Headline
blueprint: One-line headline at clamp(3.5rem, 12vw, 12rem), weight 800, centred in a 100svh section with padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). The real h1 carries the text. Two aria-hidden copies are stacked exactly over it: the top copy in ink A (paper colour on black band) clipped to the upper half with clip-path inset(0 0 50% 0), the bottom copy in ink B (accent on paper) clipped to the lower half. A diagonal ribbon 4px tall, rotated -4deg, runs across the full width along the seam, carrying a tiny marquee of the studio's services at 0.75rem. Background splits in the same two inks. States: idle, hover on headline (seam angle eases to 0deg), in-view, done.
motion: Load: seam draws across left to right in 700ms ease-out, then the halves separate vertically by 0.08em. Scroll progress 0-50%: seam angle rotates from -4deg to +4deg, re-cutting letters so each moment shows a different split. 50-100%: halves slide horizontally opposite each other by up to 0.3em, then re-register flush at 100%. Ribbon marquee runs at a constant 40s loop.
still_check: At 50% the headline reads as one word in two inks with the seam level, both halves aligned enough to read. 25% shows a downward-tilted seam, 75% shows the halves offset sideways, both still legible.
mobile: At 375px the headline breaks onto two lines and each line gets its own seam; horizontal slip is capped at 0.12em. The ribbon marquee becomes a static line of services. Tap on the headline toggles seam angle instead of hover.
a11y: Only the base h1 is exposed; both clipped copies and the ribbon duplicate are aria-hidden. Each ink pair meets 4.5:1 against its own background. Reduced motion: seam level, halves flush, marquee stopped and shown as a static list.
avoid: Halves offset far enough to make the word unreadable, a seam that hides the x-height of every letter, mismatched copies that ghost at sub-pixel offsets, colour pairs failing contrast on one side of the split.

stack_notes.css: Stack three spans in one grid cell. Animate a registered @property --seam angle and --slip length with animation-timeline: view(), feeding clip-path polygon() points and translate. The ribbon is a rotated flex row with a CSS keyframe marquee.
stack_notes.js: rAF maps section progress to seam angle and slip, writing CSS variables on the wrapper so the copies share one source of truth. WAAPI plays the load-in seam draw. Remove listeners and cancel animations on unmount; re-measure on font load. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Headline on a Ribbon Path
blueprint: Section 100svh, padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). A real h1 sits in normal flow at the top left, clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5.5rem), fully readable. Behind and around it a full-width SVG ribbon: a wide S-curve band 9vw tall in accent colour, carrying the same headline repeated on a textPath at clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3.5rem) in the paper colour. The ribbon threads through a central portrait or work image (clamp(16rem, 30vw, 26rem) wide), passing behind it on the left and in front on the right using two path segments at different z-index. Below: name, role line, two links. States: idle, hover on ribbon (letter-spacing widens 0.02em), in-view, done.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% moves startOffset of the textPath from 0% to -60%, so the words travel along the curve like a conveyor. 0-30%: ribbon unrolls via stroke-dashoffset from left. 30-70%: travel. 70-100%: travel slows on an ease-out mapping and the ribbon curvature relaxes 15% flatter. Load: image fades up 400ms.
still_check: At 50% the DOM h1 is fully readable, the ribbon fully drawn, its text mid-travel with whole words visible, the image framed by the ribbon passing behind and in front. 25% shows the ribbon partly unrolled; 75% shows flatter curvature.
mobile: At 375px the ribbon becomes a single gentle arc above the image, the path text shrinks to clamp(1rem, 5vw, 1.4rem) and travel distance halves. Image goes full width under the h1. No scroll pinning.
a11y: The SVG ribbon is aria-hidden because the h1 carries the same words in the DOM, selectable and translatable. Reduced motion: ribbon fully drawn, text static at offset 0. Links get visible focus-visible outlines offset 3px.
avoid: Making the ribbon text the only copy of the headline, ribbon crossing the h1 or the image subject's face, letters bunching on tight curve radii, scroll-velocity-driven speed changes, an empty first frame before the ribbon draws.

stack_notes.css: Inline SVG with textPath; animate startOffset is not CSS-animatable, so the CSS path animates the ribbon group translate along x with animation-timeline: view() and draws the band with stroke-dashoffset. Split the band into two paths at different z-index around the image.
stack_notes.js: rAF reads section progress and sets the textPath startOffset attribute and the band dashoffset. Recompute path length with getTotalLength on resize. Cancel rAF when the section leaves view via IntersectionObserver and on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.

name: Ridge in Front, Ridge Behind
blueprint: Section 100svh, overflow hidden. Three stacked layers in one grid cell: back layer is the sky and far ridge photo, middle layer is the h1 at clamp(4rem, 14vw, 14rem), weight 900, letters spanning the width, bottom edge sitting low; front layer is a cut-out PNG or AVIF of the near ridge, peak or landmark with a transparent sky, so the subject stands in front of the lower parts of some letters and behind others are clear. Subhead and CTA sit in a frosted strip at the bottom, padding clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2rem). z-order: back 0, h1 1, cut-out 2, strip 3. States: idle, in-view, done; no hover dependence.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% drives depth: back layer moves 4vh, h1 moves 12vh upward, cut-out moves 0. 0-40%: the cut-out covers about 30% of letter height. 40-100%: the h1 rises until letters clear the peaks almost entirely, revealing the full word. Load: h1 letters rise 0.2em with 40ms stagger, 600ms ease-out.
still_check: At 50% the word is recognisable with the peak overlapping only the lower third of two or three letters, strip readable. 25% shows deeper occlusion; 75% shows letters mostly clear above the ridge.
mobile: At 375px the h1 breaks into two stacked lines at clamp(3rem, 18vw, 4.5rem), the cut-out is a portrait crop, and parallax distances halve. Occlusion is capped at 20% of letter height so short words still read.
a11y: The h1 is live DOM text and its full word is available to assistive tech regardless of occlusion; the cut-out has an empty alt because the back image carries the descriptive alt. Reduced motion: final state, letters mostly clear. Strip text meets 4.5:1.
avoid: Occlusion that hides letters needed to read the word, cut-out edges with halos, layer drift causing horizontal overflow, parallax so strong it induces nausea, empty sky above the type at the start.

stack_notes.css: Grid stack of three layers; translate each with animation-timeline: view() and different keyframe distances. A tight cut-out mask image keeps edges crisp. IntersectionObserver toggles an in-view class for the letter stagger fallback. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: rAF maps progress to translateY per layer via CSS variables; a light WebGL depth-map displacement is optional where the project already uses it. Observe visibility to stop updates, and remove listeners on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.

name: Headline Wrapped Around the Specimen
blueprint: Two-thirds width text column inside a max-width 78rem container, padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem) clamp(1rem, 5vw, 4rem). A cut-out object image (a ceramic pill bottle, an anatomical model, a seed pod) floats right at clamp(14rem, 32vw, 28rem) with shape-outside: url(object.png) and shape-margin 1.2rem, so the h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 6.5vw, 6rem) and the 2-sentence lede wrap tightly along the object's silhouette. A small caption with a hairline leader points to one detail of the object. CTA pair below. States: idle, in-view (caption leader drawn), hover on caption (object detail outline highlights), done.
motion: On entering view the object fades from 0 to 1 opacity and rises 12px over 600ms ease-out; the caption hairline draws in 400ms after a 300ms delay. Scroll progress 0-100% rotates the object by only 3deg, never changing the wrap outline enough to reflow text.
still_check: At 50% the headline lines visibly hug the object contour with no awkward single-word lines, caption and CTA readable. 25% and 75% differ only in a slight object rotation and the caption leader state.
mobile: At 375px shape-outside is removed; the object sits above the headline at 70vw width, and the caption becomes a numbered note under the lede. Headline uses clamp(2.25rem, 10vw, 2.8rem).
a11y: Object image has descriptive alt; the caption is a figcaption tied to the figure. Reduced motion: object and leader shown at final state immediately. Reading order is headline, lede, CTA; the float does not reorder focus.
avoid: Shape images with loose alpha that make text wrap around invisible pixels, ragged one-word lines, rotating the object enough to reflow text mid-scroll, caption only revealed on hover.

stack_notes.css: float right plus shape-outside using the same alpha PNG, shape-image-threshold 0.4, shape-margin. Use @starting-style for the fade-in and animation-timeline: view() for the tiny rotation. text-wrap: balance on the h1.
stack_notes.js: Only an IntersectionObserver that adds an in-view class for the caption leader draw in browsers without scroll timelines. Any library the project uses can run the fade; no layout measurement needed.

name: Letters as Windows
blueprint: Section 100svh with a flat dough-coloured background. The h1, one or two short words at clamp(5rem, 18vw, 18rem), weight 900, tight tracking, is filled with a muted looping video of the trade (bread in the oven, a barber's chair, kiln glow) using background-clip: text on a wrapper, or an SVG mask where video clip is needed. A thin outline stroke keeps letter edges defined. Beneath: opening hours chip, address line, and a Order or Book button. A small aria-hidden caption reads what the video shows. States: idle, hover on h1 (video playback rate 1 to 0.6), in-view, done.
motion: Scroll progress 0-50%: the mask letters scale from 1.0 to 1.6 from the centre, enlarging the windows onto the footage. 50-80%: the background outside the letters fades to 15% opacity, letting the full video show. 80-100%: it fades back to solid and letters return to 1.15, setting up the next section.
still_check: At 50% the word is crisply readable as large letters full of moving footage, edges outlined, hours chip visible. 25% shows smaller letters on solid ground; 75% shows the video spilling beyond the letters at low opacity.
mobile: At 375px the video is replaced by a still poster unless the user has not opted into data saving; scale range is 1.0 to 1.25. Words stack on two lines. Hours chip and button sit in a sticky bottom bar.
a11y: The visible word remains a real h1; the video is muted, aria-hidden, and has a pause control reachable by keyboard. Reduced motion: still poster in letters, no scaling. Outline stroke guarantees letter shapes when footage is dark.
avoid: Footage too busy for letters to read, autoplaying sound, letters scaling past the viewport so the word breaks, a blank frame before the video loads (use poster), relying on background-clip in browsers lacking it.

stack_notes.css: Wrapper with background video replaced by background-clip: text on an animated image, or an SVG mask with text element over a video element. Scale and outer fade via animation-timeline: view(). Provide @supports fallback to solid text.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver plays and pauses the video only when visible; rAF maps progress to mask scale for browsers without scroll timelines. Honour Save-Data and matchMedia reduced motion; release the video source on unmount.

name: The Object Is the Word
blueprint: Centred h1 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 9rem) reading, for example, Built like a [object] for your desk. The bracketed word is a real span with the word in it, but its visible box is an inline canvas sized 1.6em wide by 1.1em tall holding a rotating 3D model of the product, baseline-aligned so the line reads continuously. The span's text is visually hidden yet present for screen readers and selection. Below: deck at clamp(1rem, 1.4vw, 1.25rem), swatch dots that change the model finish, Buy CTA. States: idle (slow spin), hover on object (spins toward cursor), swatch active, in-view, done.
motion: Load: the word briefly shows as text for 500ms, then the letters fall away 300ms as the model scales into the same slot. Scroll progress 0-60%: the inline model grows from 1.6em to 3.2em wide and the line reflows smoothly around it. 60-100%: model rotates to hero angle and swatch dots stagger in at 60ms each.
still_check: At 50% the full sentence reads with the model clearly occupying the word slot, other words intact on either side, no overlap. 25% shows a smaller model; 75% shows the larger model at hero angle with swatches visible.
mobile: At 375px the object slot moves to its own line at 2.4em, the model uses a lower poly variant, and growth on scroll is disabled. Swatches become 44px tap targets in a row below the deck.
a11y: The span keeps the real word in DOM text with a visually hidden class; the canvas is aria-hidden. Swatches are radio inputs in a fieldset with a legend. Reduced motion: model static at hero angle, no letter fall, no growth.
avoid: Removing the word from DOM, inline slot height changing line-height and causing jumps, model failing to load leaving a hole (show a poster image), swatches only changing colour without a text label.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: span contains a looping image sequence or a CSS 3D layered image with rotateY keyframes; width grows via animation-timeline: view() on a registered --slot length. Visually hidden text with clip-path inset(50%).
stack_notes.js: three.js or WebGL renders into the inline canvas measured by ResizeObserver; rAF maps progress to slot width and rotation. Swatch change swaps a material uniform. Pause when offscreen and dispose renderer, geometry and textures on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Odometer Inside the Sentence
blueprint: Full-width h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5.75rem), max 18ch, on the page grid's left edge with nothing beside it. The sentence contains a live figure, e.g. We have paid out 41,208,550 to members. The figure is a set of digit windows: each digit is a 1em-tall, overflow-hidden slot with a vertical strip of 0-9 in tabular figures, framed by hairline borders like a mechanical counter, set inline on the baseline. A small source line under the headline states as-of date and source. Beneath it a 4rem-tall hairline sparkline strip runs the full container width, plotting the same figure's history with the as-of point marked. States: idle, in-view (digits roll), done (final value settled).
motion: On first view the digits roll from a lower value to the real figure over 1.4s, least significant digits spinning more turns, ease cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.1,1), settling right to left with 40ms stagger. No scroll-driven motion beyond a 2% opacity shift on the hairlines; after settling it stays still.
still_check: At 50% the headline shows the final figure fully settled and readable, source line visible, sparkline drawn. 25% and 75% look identical in content; only the hairline tone differs subtly, which is acceptable for a calm hero.
mobile: At 375px the figure moves onto its own line at clamp(2.5rem, 12vw, 3.5rem), digit windows keep tabular width, and the sparkline strip keeps the full width at 3rem tall under the source line.
a11y: Figure has a visually hidden text span with the final value; the digit strips are aria-hidden. Reduced motion: final digits shown immediately. Source line is real text linked to methodology. Contrast of digits and hairlines meets AA.
avoid: Screen readers reading every strip digit, rolling to a made-up number, proportional figures that wobble width, re-rolling every time the user scrolls back, values without as-of date.

stack_notes.css: Each slot holds a column of digits translated by a CSS variable --d times -1em; transition on translate with per-slot delay. A tiny IntersectionObserver sets the final values once. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
stack_notes.js: Fetch the real figure, compute target digits, then animate each strip with WAAPI. Observe once and unobserve after the roll. Format with Intl.NumberFormat for locale grouping; update the hidden text span at the same time.

name: Working Product Fragment
blueprint: Split grid 5/7 inside max-width 80rem, padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem) clamp(1rem, 4vw, 3rem). Left: h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 5.5vw, 5rem), lede, CTA pair, and a one-line hint Try it: type a customer name. Right: a real, working fragment of the product in a framed window: a search input, three filter chips, and an 8-row table of sample records that genuinely filters and sorts. A live counter reads 8 of 8 rows. Window chrome is minimal: title bar with workspace name. States: idle (a ghost cursor types a demo query once), user focus (ghost stops), filtered, empty-result (helpful message), done.
motion: Load: window rises 16px with 500ms ease-out. After 1.2s idle, a ghost typing demo enters a query at 70ms per character, rows filter with a 180ms height and opacity transition, then clears. User interaction cancels the demo permanently. Scroll progress only tilts the window from 2deg to 0deg over 0-40%.
still_check: At 50% the headline and the full fragment are visible with all rows legible and controls clearly interactive. 25% shows a slight window tilt; 75% shows it flat, possibly mid-demo with a filtered row set, never empty.
mobile: At 375px the fragment stacks below the copy, the table becomes a card list of 5 records, chips scroll horizontally in one row, and the ghost demo is skipped. Input is 16px font to avoid zoom.
a11y: Real input with label, chips as toggle buttons with aria-pressed, table as a semantic table with sortable header buttons and aria-sort. Result count in a polite live region. Reduced motion: no ghost typing, no tilt.
avoid: A screenshot pretending to be interactive, ghost demo fighting the user's typing, filter producing an empty table with no message, fake data that looks like real personal data, heavy app bundle loaded just for the hero.

stack_notes.css: Rows marked with data attributes; :has() on the fieldset with checked chip inputs hides non-matching rows, giving a no-JS filter. Tilt via animation-timeline: view(). Row exit uses transition on grid-template-rows for smooth collapse.
stack_notes.js: Small vanilla module: input event filters an in-memory array and re-renders rows, sort toggles by column. Ghost demo uses a cancellable timer chain. Clean up timers and listeners on unmount; lazy-load nothing beyond this module. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.

name: Shoppable Still Life
blueprint: Full-bleed art-directed photograph of a styled table or shelf, aspect 16/9 on desktop, with the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4.5rem) set in a quiet corner of negative space. Five to seven numbered hotspots (28px circles with a 1px ring) sit on real products in the photo, positioned with percentage coordinates. Each opens a small card: thumbnail, name, price, swatch count, Add to bag button. A right-edge index lists the same items in order as a plain list. States: idle (hotspots gently pulse once), hover or focus on hotspot (card opens), active (card pinned), done.
motion: On view, hotspots appear in numeric order with 80ms stagger and a single 1.2s ring pulse each, then stay still. Cards open with 180ms opacity and 6px translate. Scroll progress 0-100% shifts the photo 3% scale for a gentle settle; nothing else moves.
still_check: At 50% the photo is sharp, headline readable, all hotspots visible, index list present. 25% and 75% differ only by the slight photo scale; no card should be half-open in a static capture.
mobile: At 375px the photo crops to 4/5 around the products, hotspots stay but cards open as a bottom sheet. The index list becomes a horizontal swipe row of product chips below the photo; tap replaces hover.
a11y: Hotspots are buttons labelled with the product name and price; the card is a popover tied with aria-controls. The index list mirrors all products for non-visual users. Reduced motion: no pulse or scale. Focus ring visible on the photo.
avoid: Product info available only on hover, hotspots covering the product itself, cards spilling off-screen, more than seven hotspots, headline set over a busy part of the photo without a scrim.

stack_notes.css: Hotspots as buttons with popovertarget opening popover cards, positioned with anchor positioning where supported or fixed offsets otherwise. Stagger via animation-delay with @starting-style; scale via animation-timeline: view().
stack_notes.js: A small module adds focus-trap-free card toggling, closes on Escape and outside click, and flips card side when near edges using getBoundingClientRect. Add to bag posts to the existing cart API. Remove listeners on unmount.

name: Tonight's menu, set as the page
blueprint: Split hero inside max-width 76rem, padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem) clamp(1rem, 4vw, 3rem), on the restaurant's flat paper tone (no texture image). Start column 5/12: a single photograph of tonight's signature dish or the room at 4:5, square-cornered. End column 7/12: the menu typeset as live text, upright, no rotation and no shadow: the date line at 0.875rem small caps, the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4.25rem) with text-wrap: balance (Thursday supper), then 5 courses each as name at 1.125rem, one-line description at 0.9375rem in the muted ink and price in tabular figures right-aligned on a 1px dotted leader, then one line for the wine of the night under a hairline. Under the list: Book a table button 3rem tall with 4px corners and a plain walk-in line. States: idle, course hover (leader line darkens to full ink), button hover (fill darkens 8%), focus (2px ring offset 2px).
motion: On view the courses fade up 8px in a 60ms stagger over 400ms total; the photo holds still. No rotation, no parallax. Button press depresses 1px in 120ms.
still_check: At 50% the date headline, every course name and price are readable on the card, slip visible, CTA present. 25% and 75% differ only by the small card-to-slip offset; no blank card.
mobile: At 375px the card spans 92vw with rotation 0.5deg, the h1 stays the card's top line at clamp(2rem, 9vw, 2.75rem), the slip tucks under the card bottom edge, and Book becomes a sticky bottom button with the walk-in note.
a11y: Menu is a real list of courses with prices as text, not an image. Date uses a time element. Reduced motion: card placed at rest without slide. Dotted leaders are decorative and aria-hidden. Serif body meets 4.5:1 on paper.
avoid: Tilted cards, linen or paper textures, drop shadows, script fonts, scanned menu images, stale dates (render from data), prices without tabular figures, or more than 6 courses in the hero.

stack_notes.css: Card is an article with a CSS paper gradient and box-shadow; course rows use a flex row with a dotted border filler for leaders. Entry via @starting-style transitions; parallax via animation-timeline: view(). Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: Render courses from a small JSON or CMS feed by date; IntersectionObserver adds an in-view class for older browsers that lack @starting-style. No animation library required; the menu data feed is the only script worth shipping here.

name: Today, at a Glance
blueprint: Calm signed-in hero inside the app shell, padding clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem). Top row: greeting h1 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem) with the date and one sentence summarising the day (3 things need you, all else on track). Below, a row of three to four meters: a ring for daily goal, a slim bar for budget used, a stepped bar for tasks done, each with a large tabular number, label and delta. Under the meters, one prominent Next up item with a single action button. States: idle, in-view (meters fill), hover on meter (tooltip with breakdown, also visible on focus), done.
motion: On load meters fill from 0 to their values over 800ms ease-out with 100ms stagger, numbers count with them. Afterwards everything stays still. Live data changes animate only the changed meter over 400ms with the same easing, and its number crossfades. Hover or focus tooltips fade in over 150ms. No scroll-linked motion at all.
still_check: At 50% scroll the greeting, summary sentence, every meter value and the Next up item are fully visible and filled. 25% and 75% show the same composition; the only allowed difference is a live data update.
mobile: At 375px meters become a 2x2 grid with rings at 64px, the summary sentence stays under the greeting, and Next up becomes a full-width card with a 48px action button.
a11y: Each meter is a meter or progressbar element with aria-valuenow, min and max, plus a visible text value. Breakdowns are reachable by focus, not hover-only. Reduced motion: values appear filled. Status uses text plus colour, never colour alone.
avoid: Wall of KPIs, alarming red for normal states, meters without numbers, counts that re-animate on every re-render, breakdown data hidden behind hover only.

stack_notes.css: Rings via conic-gradient driven by a registered @property --pct with a transition; bars via scaleX on a pseudo-element. @starting-style sets 0 for the first fill. Container queries switch meter layout.
stack_notes.js: Framework component sets --pct from data; Intl.NumberFormat for values. Live updates arrive via existing data hooks; diff old and new values so only changed meters transition. No animation library. Cancel any polling or subscriptions on unmount.

name: Issue Cover Zoom-In
blueprint: Section height 220svh with a sticky 100svh stage. The stage shows a magazine cover at aspect 3/4, height 82svh, centred: masthead across the top, issue number large in the corner (No. 14 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem)), cover line h1 at clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 4rem), three secondary cover lines with page numbers, barcode and date. Cover lines are real links to the stories. Around the cover, desk space with the table of contents peeking from the right. States: idle, in-view, zooming, done (zoomed into the lead story's image with its standfirst readable).
motion: Scroll progress 0-30%: cover sits at full size, cover lines stagger in. 30-80%: the cover scales from 1 to 2.6 with transform-origin on the lead story image, masthead sliding out of frame. 80-100%: the lead image fills the stage and the story standfirst fades in on a scrim; the sticky releases.
still_check: At 50% the cover is mid-zoom but the cover line h1 and issue number remain inside the frame and legible. 25% shows the full cover; 75% shows the lead image dominant with standfirst appearing, still readable.
mobile: At 375px sticky length shortens to 150svh, cover fills 92vw width, zoom maxes at 1.8, and the table of contents becomes a link list below. Cover lines remain tappable links.
a11y: Cover lines are a list of links with page numbers as text; issue number is in the h1 context via a visually hidden prefix. Reduced motion: no zoom, show the full cover then the lead story card beneath. Focus jumps do not trap inside the sticky.
avoid: Zoom that crops the h1 mid-word, a sticky range much longer than the content, cover rendered as one flat image, scaled text going blurry (scale the container, keep text crisp via final layout swap).

stack_notes.css: position: sticky stage with animation-timeline: view() on the section driving scale and transform-origin on the cover. Standfirst opacity keyed to the 80-100% range with animation-range. Masthead slide via translate keyframes.
stack_notes.js: rAF maps sticky progress 0..1 to scale with a swap to a sharp final layout at 100%. IntersectionObserver fallback simply shows cover then story card. Remove scroll listeners on unmount.

name: Floor Plan That Draws Itself
blueprint: Split grid 5/7, padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem). Left: address line, h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4.5rem) such as Three bedrooms, west light, a facts row (sqm, beds, baths, price) in tabular figures, and Book a viewing CTA. Right: an SVG floor plan of the actual property at max 44rem wide on a blueprint-paper ground. Walls are strokes, doors are arcs, each room is a labelled path with area. A small north arrow and scale bar. Hovering or focusing a room fills it with a pale tint and shows a photo thumbnail beside the plan. States: idle, in-view (walls draw), room active, done.
motion: Scroll progress 0-50%: exterior walls draw via stroke-dashoffset, then interior walls. 50-75%: door arcs swing in and room labels fade in by room. 75-100%: a sun-angle wedge sweeps across west-facing rooms showing evening light, then holds. Room hover or focus tint fades in over 160ms ease and the thumbnail crossfades in 200ms.
still_check: At 50% all walls are drawn, labels starting to appear, headline and facts fully readable. 25% shows exterior walls only with a clear outline; 75% shows labels complete and the light wedge on the west rooms.
mobile: At 375px the plan sits above the facts at full width, draw range shortens, rooms are tapped to open a bottom sheet with photo and dimensions. The light wedge is a static overlay.
a11y: The SVG has a title and the room list is duplicated as a real list of rooms with areas. Rooms are focusable with role button and aria-label. Reduced motion: plan fully drawn, labels visible, wedge static.
avoid: Half-drawn plan in the first frame with no outline, labels too small to read, photo previews only on hover, a generic plan not matching the property, plan pushing facts below the fold.

stack_notes.css: Paths with pathLength 1 and stroke-dasharray 1; animate stroke-dashoffset with animation-timeline: view() and staggered animation-range per layer. Room tint via :hover and :focus-visible fill transitions.
stack_notes.js: rAF maps section progress to per-layer draw values; room focus swaps the thumbnail src and preloads neighbours. IntersectionObserver fallback triggers a timed 1.2s draw instead. Remove listeners on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.

name: Route Line Across the Land
blueprint: Section 250svh with a sticky 100svh stage. Background is a WebGL terrain or globe quadrant with muted relief. Overlay at z-index 2: h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6.5rem) top left, trip name and dates; bottom left a stop card (place name, day number, one line, photo thumb). A glowing route line traces the itinerary across the terrain with stop pins. Right edge: a vertical day index of the 7 to 10 stops as links. States: idle, in-view, travelling (camera follows route), stop active, done (whole route visible from above).
motion: Scroll progress 0-10%: camera high, route undrawn, headline in. 10-85%: route draws to each stop in sequence, camera eases along, the stop card swaps at each pin with 200ms crossfade. 85-100%: camera pulls up to show the entire route lit, Book this trip CTA appears.
still_check: At 50% the route is drawn to roughly the middle stop, its card readable, headline still present, terrain lit. 25% shows the early stops; 75% shows later stops with different terrain and card.
mobile: At 375px the terrain becomes a static illustrated map image with an SVG route drawn by scroll, sticky length shortens to 160svh, stop card becomes a bottom sheet, and the day index becomes a horizontal chip row.
a11y: The itinerary is a real ordered list of stops linked from the index; the canvas is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: overview camera with the full route drawn and all stops listed. Keyboard focus on a stop scrolls to its position.
avoid: Camera spins that cause motion sickness, an undrawn empty map at 50%, stop cards covering the line, heavy terrain loading blocking the headline, scroll pinning longer than the content justifies.

stack_notes.css: Static map image with an inline SVG route path; stroke-dashoffset tied to animation-timeline: view() on the sticky section, pins revealed with staggered animation-range. Stop cards stack and swap by range.
stack_notes.js: WebGL terrain or three.js scene with a route tube geometry; rAF maps progress to the drawn fraction and a camera path. Any map library the project already uses can supply tiles. Dispose scene and stop rAF on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: One Dot per Family
blueprint: Section 200svh with a sticky 100svh stage. A canvas field fills the stage behind the copy. One real number anchors it: e.g. 12,480 families housed since 2019, stated as the h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5.5rem). Each dot equals one family; the field holds exactly that many dots, 2-3px each, in a warm neutral. Bottom bar: source and as-of date, Donate CTA, and a sentence explaining what one dot is. A single highlighted dot carries a small label with one real family's story excerpt link. States: idle, in-view, filling, done (all dots placed, one highlighted).
motion: Scroll progress 0-20%: one dot alone, centred, labelled. 20-80%: dots pour in by year, each year a slightly different tone, a small year label ticking 2019 to 2026. 80-100%: dots settle into a dense shape (a house silhouette or map), the highlighted dot stays visible, CTA rises.
still_check: At 50% the h1 with the real number is fully readable, roughly half the dots placed with a visible year label, the single highlighted dot distinguishable. 25% shows a sparse field; 75% shows the shape forming.
mobile: At 375px dot count stays truthful but dots render at 1px with a Canvas2D path, sticky shortens to 140svh, the h1 stacks above the field and the story label becomes a tappable card below.
a11y: The number and source are DOM text; the canvas is aria-hidden with a text summary of growth per year in a details element. Reduced motion: final shape shown immediately. Donate button keeps a visible focus ring.
avoid: Fake or rounded-up numbers, dots that do not equal the stated unit, a blank field at 50%, contrast loss behind the h1 (add a scrim), unexplained colour changes by year.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: pre-rendered stages as images layered in the sticky stage, crossfaded via animation-timeline: view() ranges; the year label uses a stepped counter with @property integer animation.
stack_notes.js: WebGL point sprites or Canvas2D draw N dots with precomputed target positions; rAF maps progress to how many are placed and eased toward targets. Stop rendering offscreen and free buffers on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Ticket Stub Tear-Off
blueprint: Section 100svh, padding clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem). Centre: an oversized ticket clamp(20rem, 70vw, 60rem) wide, aspect 2.4/1, with a notched perforation 72% along. Main body: event name as h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6.5vw, 6rem), date, venue, doors and lineup in a ticket grid. Stub: seat-style admit label, price from, a QR-like decorative pattern, and Get tickets button. Background is a paper-coloured board. States: idle, hover on stub (perforation wiggles 1deg), in-view, torn (stub separates), done.
motion: Load: ticket feeds up from a slot at the bottom edge over 900ms with a stepped ease mimicking a printer. Scroll progress 0-60%: ticket rests. 60-100%: the stub tears along the perforation, rotating 6deg and sliding 4vw right, revealing the price and CTA in full beside the body. Click on CTA does not depend on tear state.
still_check: At 50% the whole ticket is printed and still intact with event name, date, venue and the stub's CTA readable. 25% looks the same but newly settled; 75% shows the stub partly torn away with a ragged perforation edge.
mobile: At 375px the ticket rotates to portrait, perforation runs horizontally, the stub sits below the body, and the tear is a short 150ms animation on first view instead of scroll-linked.
a11y: Ticket is an article with a heading and a description list for date, venue and doors. The decorative QR pattern is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: printed and intact, no tear. CTA is a real link with visible focus ring.
avoid: CTA only reachable after tearing, printer effect so slow the headline arrives late, a fake QR that looks scannable, ragged edge clipping text, ticket overflowing narrow screens.

stack_notes.css: Ticket built from two grid areas with a mask of radial-gradient notches for perforation; the tear uses translate and rotate keyed to animation-timeline: view() with animation-range 60% 100%. Printer feed via steps() keyframes.
stack_notes.js: rAF maps progress to tear rotation and offset; WAAPI plays the feed on load. A clip-path polygon with jittered points draws the ragged edge, computed once on resize. Clean up on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Search-First Docs Front Door
blueprint: Compact hero, padding clamp(3rem, 7vw, 6rem) clamp(1rem, 4vw, 3rem), max width 52rem centred. Small h1 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem) naming the product docs, one line of version and changelog link. Then the star: a wide search field 3.5rem tall with a keyboard shortcut hint, and below it six popular starting points as a 3x2 list (Install, Quickstart, Auth, API reference, Errors, Migrate). Under that, a quiet row of version selector and status. States: idle, focus on search (the rest of the page dims to 40% and results drop below), typing (live results grouped by section), done.
motion: Focus: surrounding content fades to 40% opacity over 200ms ease-out and the search field expands 4px with a subtle shadow. Results list appears with 120ms fade. Arrow-key movement through results slides the highlight bar in 100ms. Blur or Escape returns everything to full opacity in 160ms. No scroll-linked motion.
still_check: At 50% the h1, search field with shortcut hint and all six starting points are readable at full opacity. 25% and 75% show the same composition; only an active focus state may differ.
mobile: At 375px the search field becomes full width and sticky at the top on scroll, starting points become a single-column list of 48px rows, and the shortcut hint is hidden.
a11y: Search uses role search landmark with a labelled input and a combobox pattern for results with aria-activedescendant. Shortcut hint is a kbd element. Dimming never applies to the focused region. Reduced motion: instant dim without transition.
avoid: Marketing illustration pushing search below the fold, dimming so strong the page looks disabled, results only via mouse, shortcut that conflicts with browser find, missing empty-results guidance.

stack_notes.css: body:has(.docs-search input:focus) dims siblings with an opacity transition. Starting points are a grid list. Results area shown with :focus-within and @starting-style for its first appearance.
stack_notes.js: Hook the existing search index (local JSON or the docs platform API), debounce input 120ms, render grouped results, handle arrow keys and Enter, and register the slash shortcut. Remove key listeners on unmount.

name: Terminal Session Replay
blueprint: One stacked column inside max-width 64rem, padding clamp(4rem, 8vw, 7rem) clamp(1rem, 4vw, 3rem). Top: h1 at clamp(2.4rem, 5vw, 4.6rem), a one-sentence lede and an install command in a 3.25rem copyable pill (npx your-tool init) with a Copy button. Below, at the full container width: a terminal pane in 0.95rem monospace showing a real recorded session as DOM lines: the prompt, the command, 6-10 output lines (resolved config, files written, a pass/fail summary) and the final result the product promises. Lines are grouped into 3 steps; the step rail (01 install, 02 run, 03 result) runs along the pane's title bar. States: replaying, paused by the user, finished (full transcript), copy confirmed.
motion: Scroll progress 0-60% of the hero range reveals the transcript one step at a time: step 1 lines are present at 0%, step 2 at 30%, step 3 at 60%; each new line slides 6px and fades in over 160ms with a 40ms stagger. The step rail fills in sync. No typing jitter, no fake cursor delay beyond a 2-frame caret blink.
still_check: At 50% the headline, the install pill and at least steps 1 and 2 of the transcript are fully legible as real text; 25% shows step 1 only, 75% shows all three steps with the result line visible. No screenshot shows a half-typed command.
mobile: At 375px lines wrap with a hanging indent instead of scrolling sideways, the step rail becomes 3 small labels in the title bar, and the full transcript shows without scroll-linked reveal.
a11y: Transcript is a pre/code block in DOM order, so screen readers get the whole session at once; the reveal is visual only. Copy is a real button with a polite live region (Copied). Reduced motion: full transcript shown at once, caret static.
avoid: A fake command that does not exist, output nobody can verify, typing animation that hides the install command, a screenshot image of a terminal, horizontal scroll at 375px, and colour-only success or failure markers.

stack_notes.css: Lines carry data-step; animation-timeline: view() with animation-range drives opacity and translate per step group. Caret is a ::after with steps(2) blink. Copy pill uses user-select: all as a no-JS fallback.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver plus a scroll progress read in rAF toggles data-shown on step groups for browsers without scroll timelines. navigator.clipboard.writeText for Copy with a fallback selection. Remove listeners and cancel rAF on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Recipe card with ticking steps
blueprint: A single cream index card centred in the section, max-width min(44rem, 92vw), padding clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3rem), section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). Card header: dish-style title clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem), a serves / time / difficulty row in small caps. Left column (30%): ingredient list as a real ul with hairline rules. Right column: an ordered list of 4-6 method steps, each with a 1.25rem square checkbox glyph, step text at 1.0625rem, and a margin timestamp ('min 12'). A thin vertical progress rule in the card gutter fills as steps tick. States: idle step = ink 70%; in-view step = box ticks, text full ink; done = tick plus faint strikethrough on the matching ingredient.
motion: Each step owns its own view() range. 0-40% of a step entering: checkbox stroke draws in (stroke-dashoffset), 40-60%: tick snaps with a 120ms ease-out scale 0.8 to 1, 60-100%: linked ingredient gets a 1px strike that draws left to right. The gutter rule height maps 0..1 to section progress. No card movement at all; only ink and ticks.
still_check: At 50% the card is fully readable with roughly half the steps ticked, gutter rule half full, and matching ingredients struck. At 25% only one or two ticks show; at 75% most are ticked and the final step is next.
mobile: Card goes full width minus 16px gutters; ingredients collapse into a details summary above the method so steps stay the focus. Step ranges shorten to the step's own height, and the gutter rule moves to the left edge.
a11y: Steps are an ol; ticks are aria-hidden decoration, so no fake checkboxes. Under prefers-reduced-motion all ticks and strikes render in their done state immediately. If steps are interactive, use real input type checkbox with labels and a visible focus ring.
avoid: Striking text so heavily it becomes unreadable, faking checkboxes that look clickable but are not, ticking all steps before the user reaches them, or making the card scroll inside itself.

stack_notes.css: animation-timeline: view() on each li with animation-range entry 20% cover 50%; tick via stroke-dashoffset keyframes on an inline SVG; ingredient strike via a background-size gradient keyed by a shared custom property. Gutter rule uses scroll-timeline on the section. @supports fallback adds a done class via IntersectionObserver.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver with thresholds per step toggles data-done; WAAPI plays the stroke draw and strike. Optionally let users tap to tick, storing state in sessionStorage. Any library the project already uses can drive the same attributes.

name: Pinned workbench assembly
blueprint: Section height 400vh with a sticky 100vh stage. Stage grid: left 38% text rail, right 62% WebGL canvas showing a workbench top-down at three-quarter angle. The product (lamp, shoe, speaker) starts as exploded parts laid out like a parts tray. Text rail holds 5 steps as an ol, step label clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3rem), body 1rem, with part names matching parts on the bench. A part tag (small DOM label, absolutely positioned via projected coordinates) follows each active part. States: inactive step = 40% ink; active = full ink plus its part glowing; done = part seated, label greyed with a small check.
motion: Progress 0-15%: camera settles on the full tray. 15-80%: each step's 13% slice lifts one part, rotates it on an arc and seats it into the assembly with a soft overshoot; screws spin in. 80-100%: camera orbits 30 degrees to a hero beauty angle, rim light sweeps the finished object, and the step list collapses into a single 'assembled in 5 steps' line.
still_check: At 50% the object is visibly half assembled, one part mid-flight but clearly identifiable, its step text fully legible and active. At 25% most parts still lie on the tray; at 75% only the last part remains loose.
mobile: Unpin and stack: a short 60vh canvas above the step list, each step tap or scroll-snap advancing the assembly one stage with a 600ms tween. Drop the orbit, keep a fixed camera, and halve geometry detail.
a11y: Step list is a real ol and carries all content; canvas is aria-hidden with a short alt description. Reduced motion shows five static rendered frames beside each step. Keyboard users can Tab through steps, and focusing a step jumps the assembly to that stage.
avoid: Parts flying over the text rail, step text that only exists in the canvas, a blank canvas while the model loads (show a poster render), scroll lock, and assembly stages that feel random rather than mechanically plausible.

stack_notes.css: Fallback without WebGL: five pre-rendered PNG or AVIF frames stacked in the sticky stage, each crossfaded by animation-timeline: view() on its matching step, with position: sticky for the stage. Still reads as assembly, just stepped.
stack_notes.js: three.js or raw WebGL scene; rAF loop reads section progress from getBoundingClientRect and lerps each part along a precomputed bezier with a damped spring. Project part anchors to screen for DOM labels. Dispose geometry, textures and listeners on unmount; pause when off-screen.

name: Build stages inked onto a plan
blueprint: Section 250vh, sticky stage 100vh on blueprint-blue paper with a faint 24px grid. Centre: an inline SVG floor plan, width min(56rem, 70vw). Around it, four step callouts (Survey, Plan, Build, Handover) pinned to the plan corners with leader lines, each callout a DOM block: number, title clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), 2-line body. Dimension annotations sit as DOM text on the plan. States: pending step = dashed outline only; active = its walls ink in and its callout lifts to full contrast; done = plan section gets a soft fill and room labels appear.
motion: 0-25%: survey dots and dimension ticks appear around the plot boundary. 25-50%: exterior walls draw via stroke-dashoffset in drafting order. 50-75%: interior walls, doors (quarter-arc swings) and windows draw. 75-100%: rooms fill with a light wash, room names and areas fade up, and a keys icon drops at the entrance for Handover.
still_check: At 50% exterior walls are complete, interior walls just starting, two callouts at full contrast and readable. At 25% only the boundary and survey ticks exist; at 75% rooms are walled and doors drawn but not yet filled.
mobile: Unpin; plan scales to 100% width at the top of each step block, and each step block shows the plan at its own stage (four small static states) with the current one drawn as it enters view.
a11y: Steps are an ol in DOM order; the SVG has role img with a title summarising the plan. Room labels are DOM text, not paths. Reduced motion shows the completed, filled plan with all callouts visible.
avoid: Strokes drawing so thin they vanish on low-DPI screens, leader lines crossing callout text, a blank grid at section start, and hiding step copy until its walls finish drawing.

stack_notes.css: SVG paths with pathLength=1 and stroke-dasharray 1; stroke-dashoffset keyframes bound to animation-timeline: scroll() on the section via timeline-scope, each group with its own animation-range. IntersectionObserver adds stage classes where scroll timelines are unsupported.
stack_notes.js: Compute section progress in a rAF-throttled scroll handler and set a --p custom property; map ranges per path group. Optionally measure path lengths with getTotalLength for non-normalised paths. Works with any tween library already present.

name: Building directory index
blueprint: Two-column grid 4/12 and 8/12 inside max-width 80rem, section padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem). Start column: a sticky directory set like a well-made lobby directory in the brand's own type, not felt: each service as one row at 1rem with a floor or section number in tabular figures at inline-start, rows 2.5rem tall separated by 1px hairlines, the whole list never taller than 70svh. End column: one entry per service, each with the title at clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3rem) with text-wrap: balance, a 3-line description at 1.0625rem with text-wrap: pretty, duration and price in tabular figures and a Book this link with an underline 1px offset 3px. A 1px rule separates entries; entries size to their content with padding-block clamp(3rem, 6vw, 5rem). States: the directory row for the entry in view shows full ink and a 2px bar at inline-start; others sit at the muted ink (still 4.5:1).
motion: As an entry crosses the viewport centre, its directory row's bar grows from 0 to full height in 180ms ease-out and the ink shifts in 150ms. Nothing else moves.
still_check: At 50% the board shows the middle service highlighted with its arrow, and the right column shows that service's full text. At 25% and 75% a different row is lit and a different entry fills the right.
mobile: Board becomes a horizontal scrolling chip strip pinned under the header; the active chip scrolls into view. Entries shorten to content height with 3rem gaps.
a11y: Board is a nav with a list of in-page anchor links; the active one gets aria-current location. Focus ring on each link is clearly visible against felt. Reduced motion removes the arrow slide but keeps the highlight swap.
avoid: Felt-board or lobby-sign textures, letters settling animations, entries padded to 70vh of empty space, a directory taller than the viewport, highlight lag, or dim rows below 4.5:1.

stack_notes.css: position: sticky board; each entry defines view-timeline-name, hoisted with timeline-scope on the section so board rows animate against their entry's view timeline (range contain). Fallback: IntersectionObserver with rootMargin -50% 0 sets aria-current.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver on entries with a centre band rootMargin toggles a data-active attribute; scrollIntoView with block nearest keeps mobile chips aligned. Clicking a row uses native smooth anchor scrolling, respecting reduced motion.

name: Triage board that reshuffles
blueprint: Top: a question line clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3rem) such as 'What brings you in?' followed by a wrap of 6-8 need chips (pill buttons, min 44px tall). Below: a board of service tiles in a masonry-like 12-column grid with tiles of three sizes; each tile shows service name, who it is for, wait time and a coloured urgency stripe. States: idle = all tiles at equal weight; chip selected = matching tiles grow to the large size and move to the top, non-matching shrink to compact rows at the bottom; tile hover/focus = lifts 2px and reveals its book link.
motion: On chip toggle, tiles reflow with a FLIP animation: 420ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), matching tiles scale up and slide to the top while others compress, staggered 30ms. Urgency stripes widen on matching tiles. A small count line ('3 services match') ticks to its new number.
still_check: Not scroll-driven: any screenshot must show a chosen or default chip state with every tile readable. Default state shows a balanced board; with a chip selected, matched tiles clearly lead and unmatched remain listed below.
mobile: Chips become a horizontal scroll strip; board collapses to one column where matching services sort to the top and unmatched collapse into a details 'Other services' group.
a11y: Chips are toggle buttons with aria-pressed; board is a list; the match count is an aria-live polite region. Reduced motion swaps FLIP for instant reorder. Never hide non-matching services entirely, keep them reachable.
avoid: Tiles disappearing so users think a service does not exist, layout jumping without animation causing lost place, chips that look like decorative tags, and reflow that shifts the chip row itself.

stack_notes.css: Use :has() on the section, e.g. section:has(#need-back:checked) .tile[data-need~=back], to set order and grid-span with radio or checkbox inputs styled as chips; transitions on size only. Order changes jump without JS, which is acceptable.
stack_notes.js: FLIP: record getBoundingClientRect, apply new order, invert with transforms, play with WAAPI. Or document.startViewTransition with a view-transition-name per tile. Update the live count text after sort.

name: Contact sheet with loupe
blueprint: Section 300vh, sticky 100vh stage on near-black. A horizontal film strip contact sheet: 3 rows of 35mm frames, each frame 18vw wide with sprocket holes and edge numbers ('14A') as DOM text. Grease-pencil circles mark chosen frames. A circular loupe, diameter clamp(10rem, 22vw, 18rem), sits fixed at stage centre and magnifies 2.5x whatever passes under it. Below the loupe, a caption block shows the frame's project, client and year at 1rem. States: frame under loupe = sharp and captioned; circled frames under loupe add a red grease mark and a 'View case' link.
motion: Section progress 0..1 translates the sheet horizontally from 0 to minus its overflow width, so frames slide under the fixed loupe. The loupe's inner image is the same sheet scaled 2.5x and offset to match. Caption swaps with a 160ms crossfade when a new frame centre passes the loupe. A slight 1 degree loupe tilt follows progress, never velocity.
still_check: At 50% a frame sits squarely in the loupe with its caption readable and neighbouring frames visible around it. At 25% and 75% different frames and captions are in the loupe, and the sheet edge numbers differ.
mobile: Unpin; the sheet becomes a native horizontal scroll-snap strip, and the loupe becomes a tap: tapping a frame opens it full width with its caption in a dialog.
a11y: Frames are a list of links with real alt text and captions; the magnified duplicate is aria-hidden. Keyboard focus on a frame scrolls it under the loupe. Reduced motion presents the sheet as a static grid with captions visible.
avoid: Loupe content misaligned with the sheet beneath, captions only visible in the loupe, an empty loupe between frames, and horizontal motion driven by wheel hijacking instead of normal vertical scroll.

stack_notes.css: Sticky stage plus a scroll() timeline translating the track; loupe uses a second copy of the track inside a circle clip-path, scaled with transform and bound to the same timeline. Captions switch via per-frame view() timelines on the horizontal axis where supported.
stack_notes.js: Measure track overflow on resize, map progress to translateX in rAF, compute which frame centre is nearest the loupe to set the caption. A Canvas2D loupe can sample a pre-drawn sheet for sharper magnification. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Filing drawer case files
blueprint: Section 350vh with a sticky stage. A manila filing drawer seen from slightly above; 5 case folders stand in it with staggered tabs labelled by client in typewriter face. As each case activates, its folder rises out and lays flat in front, opening to show a cover sheet: project title clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem), brief, three outcome figures, a paper-clipped photo. Previous folders slide back into the drawer with their tab now stamped 'Closed'. States: in drawer, lifting, open, filed.
motion: Each case owns 20% of progress. 0-30% of its slice: folder lifts out with a 3D rotateX from 70 to 0 degrees. 30-80%: folder open and still so the sheet reads. 80-100%: folder slides back down while the next tab starts rising. Paper clip photo has a 2 degree settle on open.
still_check: At 50% case three is fully open and flat with all text legible; drawer behind shows two stamped tabs and two waiting. At 25% case two is open; at 75% case four is open and three is stamped.
mobile: Unpin; drawer becomes a row of tabs at the top, and each case renders as a stacked open folder in normal flow with a sticky tab header while it is in view.
a11y: Each case is an article with a heading; the tab strip is a nav of anchors. Typewriter face only for labels, body in a readable text face. Reduced motion shows all folders open in sequence without 3D lifts.
avoid: Folders that are mid-rotation when text should be read, rotateX making text blurry, stacked folders occluding the active sheet, and more than 6 cases making the section endless.

stack_notes.css: position: sticky stage with perspective; each folder animated by a view() timeline of an invisible spacer block in the scroll column, using animation-range for lift, hold and file phases. Fallback: IntersectionObserver toggles data-state with transitions.
stack_notes.js: Compute section progress, derive active index and local t, set transforms per folder in rAF. Use will-change only during the section and remove it after. Any tween library already in the project may replace the manual mapping. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Index with shader dissolve stage
blueprint: Section 400vh, sticky 100vh stage. Left 40%: a numbered project index as a large typographic list, item size clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4.5rem), year and discipline in small caps. Right 60%: a full-bleed WebGL plane showing project imagery. Between projects, the image doesn't fade but melts through a displacement shader shaped by that project's own motif (ink bleed, pixel sort, liquid ripple). States: inactive list item = outline-free dim 40% ink; active = solid ink plus a thin rule extending toward the stage; done = 60% ink with a small index tick.
motion: Progress splits into equal slices per project. In each slice 0-70% the image holds with a slow 4% scale drift; 70-100% the shader uniform mix goes 0 to 1 dissolving into the next project using a noise texture. The list rule extends with progress inside the slice, acting as a timer toward the next case.
still_check: At 50% one project image is crisp and its list item active and legible; dissolves happen only in the last 30% of each slice. At 25% and 75% a different project is active with a different image.
mobile: Unpin; each project becomes a block with its image as a plain img and the shader used only as a brief on-enter ripple. Index list collapses to a sticky count ('03 / 06').
a11y: Index is an ol of links to case pages; canvas aria-hidden, each image duplicated as an img with alt for screen readers. Reduced motion replaces dissolves with instant cuts and stops drift. Focus on an item jumps the stage to it.
avoid: Showing mush during dissolves at common screenshot points, dissolves tied to scroll speed, a WebGL failure leaving a black panel (render img fallback), and list items using outline-only type.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: stacked img elements with mask-image driven by a scroll() timeline using a noise PNG mask whose mask-size grows, giving a dissolve-like wipe. Sticky stage and active list styling through view() timelines on spacers.
stack_notes.js: WebGL fragment shader with uniforms texA, texB, noise, mix; rAF reads progress and sets mix with smoothstep in each slice. Lazy-load textures one project ahead; dispose textures and context on unmount; pause rendering when the section is off-screen. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Slider-driven receipt printer
blueprint: Two-column grid 1fr 1fr, section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). Left: configuration controls, a large seats slider, a usage slider and 3 add-on toggles, each with label and current value in tabular figures. Right: a receipt printer slot (dark bar 2rem tall) from which a thermal-paper receipt hangs, width clamp(18rem, 30vw, 24rem), monospace 0.9375rem. Receipt lines: plan, seats x unit price, add-ons, discount, a dashed total line, total at 2rem, and a barcode footer. States: idle default config; adjusting = lines update; new line added = it prints in; removed line = torn off and drops.
motion: When a toggle adds a line, the receipt grows downward by one line height over 260ms steps(6) to mimic stepped printing, with a faint 1px jitter. Changed numbers roll digit by digit over 300ms. Removing an add-on clips its line out with a tear edge and a 200ms drop. Total updates last, with a quick highlight.
still_check: Interaction-driven: any screenshot shows a complete receipt with plan, at least two lines, and total readable; no line half-printed at rest. Default and adjusted states differ in line count and total.
mobile: Stack: receipt first (sticky at top, max 45vh, scrollable inside only if needed), controls below. Sliders get 48px thumbs. Printing animation shortens to 160ms. The total also appears in a sticky bottom bar.
a11y: Controls are native input range and checkbox with labels; receipt is a table with a caption; total in an aria-live polite region. Reduced motion updates instantly. Never rely on colour alone for discounts, include a text label.
avoid: Receipt height changes that shift the controls column, numbers rolling so long they misreport the price, hidden fees appearing only on the receipt, and sliders with no visible value.

stack_notes.css: Native inputs plus :has() to show or hide add-on rows; line entry via @starting-style height and translate transitions; totals require JS unless pre-computed per state. Use steps() timing for the stepped print.
stack_notes.js: Compute totals in a small pure function; render rows with keyed DOM; WAAPI for print-in and tear-off; number roll via per-digit translateY spans. Format with Intl.NumberFormat for currency. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.

name: Hairline ledger with column lock
blueprint: A full-width accountant's ledger: real table with 3-4 plan columns, rows for price, limits and key inclusions, hairline 1px rules, alternating faint rows, tabular figures throughout. Header row has plan name clamp(1.25rem, 2.5vw, 1.75rem) and price clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.5rem). Above: a monthly / annual segmented control. A pencil-mark tick column on the far left. States: hover or focus on a column = it gets a soft highlight band and its tick marks darken; selected plan (radio) = column locked with a double rule under its total like a closed ledger line.
motion: Billing toggle: prices roll vertically digit by digit over 280ms ease-out, the 'save 2 months' note writes in with a 200ms clip. In-view: the hairlines extend from left to right once over 600ms, staggered 40ms per row, so the ledger appears ruled before figures fade in.
still_check: Any screenshot shows a complete ruled table with every price and row label legible. Before and after toggling, prices and the savings note differ; with a plan chosen, its column shows the double rule.
mobile: Table becomes a plan selector (segmented) with a single column of rows for the chosen plan, keeping the ledger rules; a 'compare all' details reveals the full table with horizontal scroll inside a labelled region.
a11y: Use table, th scope col/row, caption. Billing toggle is a radio group. Price changes announced via aria-live polite. Reduced motion skips the rule draw and digit roll. Column highlight must not be the only selection cue.
avoid: Fake tables made of divs, prices that jump layout width when toggling (use tabular figures and fixed widths), hover-only details, and greyed rows dropping below 4.5:1.

stack_notes.css: :has(input[value=annual]:checked) swaps price spans; :has(td:nth-child(3):hover) highlights a column via a shared class trick or col elements; rules draw with scaleX transitions under @starting-style or an in-view view() timeline. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.
stack_notes.js: Minimal: a click handler on the billing toggle to update prices and the live region; IntersectionObserver adds a ruled class once. Optional per-digit roll with spans translated by WAAPI.

name: Audit trail log
blueprint: A terminal-like but light panel, max-width 60rem, monospace 0.9375rem, line height 1.7. Header: 'What happened last quarter' clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3rem) in the display face above the panel. Each log line: ISO timestamp, actor (named customer or system), event ('migrated 1.2M rows, 0 errors'), and a short verification chip (commit hash or invoice id) that links to evidence. 12-16 lines, grouped by month with sticky month headers inside the panel. Right gutter: a running tally of uptime and incidents. States: older lines 70% ink; in-view line full ink; hovered chip shows source tooltip and underline.
motion: Lines appear as their row enters view: 0-50% of entry, a caret blinks once at line start; 50-100%, the line opacity eases 0.35 to 1 and the chip slides 6px in. The gutter tally numbers tick as their month header passes. Nothing moves after entry.
still_check: At 50% two months of entries are fully visible with timestamps, events and chips readable, plus a tally partially counted. At 25% only the first month is in; at 75% the incidents total and later months show.
mobile: Drop the gutter tally into a summary row above the log; wrap long events below the timestamp; chips go on their own line with 44px tap height.
a11y: Log is an ol with time elements; chips are links with descriptive names, not raw hashes only. Tooltips are also available on focus. Reduced motion shows all lines at full ink. Avoid role=log since content is static.
avoid: Invented evidence, unclickable verification chips, lines too faint before entry, auto-typing every character, and a scrolling panel inside the page.

stack_notes.css: Each li gets animation-timeline: view() with animation-range entry 0% entry 100%; caret is a pseudo-element with a single blink keyframe. Month headers use position: sticky inside the panel. IntersectionObserver fallback adds a seen class.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver per line toggles data-seen; requestAnimationFrame counter for the tally using an ease-out over 900ms, started once. Pull lines from a JSON feed of real events if available.

name: Before and after with measurements
blueprint: Grid of 1 large compare frame (aspect 3/2, width min(64rem, 92vw)) plus a row of 3 thumbnail jobs below. The frame stacks before and after photos; a vertical handle with a 44px grip splits them. Annotations are DOM pins with measured facts tied to each side ('damp reading 28%' on before, '9%' on after; 'room 14m2' constant). Below the frame: job card with address area, date, crew size and cost range. States: handle default at 50%; dragging moves the split; pins belonging to the hidden side fade to 0.3; thumbnail selection swaps the job.
motion: On first in-view, the handle eases from 70% to 50% once over 900ms to hint it is draggable. During drag, pins crossfade by side with 150ms. Job swap crossfades photos over 250ms. No scroll-driven motion beyond the one-time hint. Pins scale from 0.9 to 1 when their side becomes dominant.
still_check: Any screenshot shows both halves with the handle visible, at least two measurement pins readable, and the job facts below. At 25% and 75% handle positions, different pins dominate.
mobile: Frame full width; handle grip enlarges to 56px; pins collapse into a two-column before / after fact list under the frame so the image stays uncluttered.
a11y: Handle is a native input range labelled 'Reveal after photo' with arrow-key support. Both images have alt text describing the state. Pins are a dl in DOM order. Reduced motion skips the hint animation.
avoid: Mismatched camera angles, pins over faces or key details, measurement claims without units or dates, and a drag area that blocks page scroll on touch.

stack_notes.css: Overlay the after img with clip-path: inset(0 0 0 var(--split)); a transparent input range across the frame updates --split via a tiny oninput or via @property registered value with a range selector (needs JS to write the var). Pins use :has() based on a data-side state.
stack_notes.js: Pointer events with setPointerCapture for dragging; update --split in rAF; sync the range input value for keyboard. touch-action pan-y on the frame so vertical scroll still works.

name: Before and after diff
blueprint: Section max-width 76rem, padding clamp(3.5rem, 7vw, 6rem) clamp(1rem, 4vw, 3rem). A heading names the change in plain words, then a unified diff panel min(70rem, 100%) wide at 0.9rem monospace: file name header, 12-20 real lines with removed lines on a muted red ground and added lines on a muted green ground, each also prefixed with - or + so meaning never rests on colour. To the right a 16rem rail lists 3 measured outcomes of the change (tests 41 to 58 passing, bundle 212 kB to 148 kB, 3 warnings to 0). Tabs above the panel switch between 2-3 example files. States: default file, other file selected, expanded hunk.
motion: On entering view the panel draws its hunks top to bottom once: each changed line's background sweeps from 0 to full width over 220ms with a 30ms stagger, then rests. Tab switch crossfades the panel over 180ms. Nothing else moves.
still_check: Any screenshot after first view shows the file header, at least 8 diff lines with readable +/- prefixes and all 3 measured outcomes. Mid-sweep, every line's text is already fully visible; only its background tint is animating.
mobile: At 375px the outcome rail moves above the panel as a 3-row list, diff lines wrap with the +/- gutter kept fixed, and tabs become a native select.
a11y: Diff is a pre block; removed and added lines use del and ins elements so assistive tech announces them. Tabs follow the ARIA tabs pattern with arrow keys. Reduced motion: tints present immediately, no sweep.
avoid: A diff of invented code that would not compile, colour-only change markers, tiny 11px code, outcome numbers without a unit or baseline, and a horizontal scrollbar inside the panel on desktop.

stack_notes.css: Line tint is a background-size transition from 0% 100% to 100% 100% triggered by animation-timeline: view() with animation-range entry; :has() on the tablist radio inputs swaps panels without JS. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: Only for roving tabindex on the tabs and copying a hunk. No runtime syntax highlighter: pre-render tokens at build time. Clean up keyboard listeners on unmount.

name: Chart that builds with annotated stills
blueprint: Section 400vh. Sticky 100vh stage holds an SVG line chart, width min(70rem, 94vw), height 60vh, with real DOM axis labels. Scrolling text cards (max-width 24rem, 1.0625rem) pass on the left, each tied to one annotation frame: a year range, a callout label, a shaded band. Headline above chart clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3rem) changes per frame. States: frame inactive; frame active = band shaded, callout pinned to a data point with a leader line, line drawn up to that date; final = full series plus comparison series in a second hue.
motion: 0-20%: axes and first decade draw. 20-45%: line extends to the first event, band shades, callout appears. 45-70%: line continues, previous callout shrinks into a small numbered marker. 70-90%: second series draws in. 90-100%: y-axis rescales smoothly to show the full range and markers align into a footnote list.
still_check: At 50% the line reaches the second event with that callout fully readable and earlier markers visible; chart never empty. At 25% only the first event is annotated; at 75% both series appear.
mobile: Unpin and render each annotation frame as its own static chart snapshot inline after its text card, with the active segment drawn on entry. Labels move below the chart.
a11y: Provide a data table in a details element and a text summary. Chart SVG role img with title. Callouts are DOM text. Reduced motion shows the final annotated chart with all numbered markers and the footnote list.
avoid: Axes rescaling mid-read with no cue, callouts overlapping the line, cards scrolling over the chart, colours that fail in greyscale, and frames where the line is mid-stroke at the screenshot point.

stack_notes.css: Path with pathLength=1 and dashoffset bound to a scroll() timeline; bands and callouts per card via view() timelines hoisted with timeline-scope. Rescale is not practical in CSS, so pre-render the final axis and crossfade.
stack_notes.js: Compute scales, generate the path, and in rAF clip the path to the date for progress via a clipPath rect width. Animate scale domain changes with an interpolated domain. Works with any charting code the project already uses.

name: Every dot is a person
blueprint: Section 500vh, sticky canvas stage 100vh. One dot represents a real unit (100 people, 1,000 meals); legend chip states the unit in the corner. Stages: a loose crowd field; dots sort into a waffle grid of total reach; split into colour-coded bars by region; a slice drifts off to show the unmet need; final, dots form the year's figure as a large numeral.
