A DOM caption column on the left (max 26rem) changes per stage, headline clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 3.5rem) with the key number. States per stage: forming, settled, labelled.
motion: Each of 5 stages takes 20% of progress: first 40% of a stage dots travel to targets with eased interpolation and slight per-dot delay; next 60% they hold settled while DOM labels for that formation fade in. Final numeral stage arranges dots into digit outlines with the DOM number overlaid exactly.
still_check: At 50% dots sit settled as labelled regional bars, caption and DOM labels readable, no dots mid-flight. At 25% the waffle grid shows; at 75% the unmet-need slice has separated.
mobile: Halve dot count with each dot meaning double units and state it in the legend; unpin and render each stage as a short 100vh block with its own settle animation; labels stack below the canvas.
a11y: Each stage has a DOM caption and a data table fallback; canvas aria-hidden. Reduced motion shows each stage's settled frame as a static image beside its caption. Unit legend is always visible text.
avoid: Dots that never settle during readable windows, numbers baked only into the canvas, misleading units, frame drops on low-end devices (cap at around 20k points), and a black canvas while initializing.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: five pre-rendered SVG or AVIF frames in a sticky stage, crossfaded by view() timelines on caption blocks. Waffle and bars can be pure CSS grid of small spans if counts are under a few hundred.
stack_notes.js: WebGL points with per-vertex start and target attributes; vertex shader mixes positions by a uniform eased t per stage. Precompute targets with layout functions. Canvas2D works below 5k dots. Dispose buffers and stop rAF when off-screen. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Feature list that crops the screen
blueprint: Grid 5fr 7fr, section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). Right: a sticky product screenshot in a frame, width 100%, aspect 16/10. Left: 5 feature entries, each min-height 60vh, title clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), 2-line body and a keyboard hint. The frame holds one large UI image; per feature, a CSS crop window (object-position plus scale) zooms to the relevant UI region and a soft dim vignette darkens everything else. States: in-view feature = text full ink and frame cropped to its area; others 45% ink.
motion: When a feature crosses the centre, the screenshot pans and scales to its region over 500ms cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1); the vignette mask moves with it. Non-active feature text fades to 45% over 200ms. That is the entire choreography. A thin outline ring draws around the target region after the pan settles, over 250ms.
still_check: At 50% the third feature's text is full ink and the screenshot is zoomed to the matching panel, readable and not mid-pan. At 25% and 75% a different region and feature are active.
mobile: Unstick; each feature shows its own pre-cropped screenshot directly under its text, no pan, so nothing is too small at 375px. Each crop gets a small caption naming the UI area.
a11y: Features are a list with headings; screenshot img has alt describing the whole UI, crops are visual only. Reduced motion jumps to crops without panning. Dimmed text stays above 4.5:1.
avoid: Crops that blur because the source image is low resolution, dimming text below contrast, pans tied to scroll so it judders, and sticky frames taller than the viewport.

stack_notes.css: Sticky frame; each feature declares a view-timeline-name, hoisted with timeline-scope; or simpler, use :has() with scroll-state or IntersectionObserver adding data-active to the section and selecting transforms per value via attribute selectors with transitions. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver on entries with a centre band sets data-active; CSS handles the transform transitions. Use a 2x source image and transform scale on a wrapper rather than resizing the image.

name: Press the key to see the feature
blueprint: Top: a rendered keyboard, width min(62rem, 94vw), with real key caps as buttons; 6 feature keys are coloured and labelled with the feature ('K Search', 'D Duplicate'). Below: a demo window aspect 16/9 showing a looping short clip or live mini-UI for the active feature, with a caption title clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem) and one line of body. States: idle = first feature active; key hover = cap lifts 2px; key pressed (click or real keypress while section focused) = cap depresses 3px with shadow collapse and the demo switches; visited keys get a small dot.
motion: Key press: translateY 3px and shadow shrink over 70ms, release over 120ms. Demo window crossfades with a 220ms clip-path wipe from the key's direction. On first in-view, three feature keys auto-press in sequence 600ms apart as a hint, then stop.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the full keyboard with legible caps and one active feature demo with caption. Different active keys show different demos and captions; never an empty demo window.
mobile: Keyboard shrinks to just the 6 feature keys in a 3x2 grid of 64px caps; demo sits above them. Physical keypress listening is disabled on touch devices.
a11y: Implement as a tablist of tab buttons with aria-controls; arrow keys move between tabs. Real keypress shortcuts only when the section has focus and never override typing in inputs. Reduced motion removes depress and wipe, and the auto hint.
avoid: Global key listeners hijacking browser shortcuts, decorative keys that look clickable, demos that autoplay sound, and the keyboard rendered as an image with no real buttons.

stack_notes.css: Radio inputs styled as key caps with labels; :has(#key-k:checked) shows the matching panel. :active gives depress styling. Wipe via clip-path transition. Works fully without JS except physical keypress.
stack_notes.js: Tablist pattern with roving tabindex; keydown handler scoped to the section maps letters to tabs. WAAPI for the wipe; IntersectionObserver triggers the one-time hint and pauses demo videos off-screen.

name: Sign-in sheet roster
blueprint: A lined sign-in sheet on paper: table with columns Name, Role, Since, Ask me about. Name column in a handwritten-feeling display face at clamp(1.25rem, 2.5vw, 1.75rem), other columns in a text face. A fixed portrait slot (aspect 4/5, width clamp(12rem, 20vw, 18rem)) sits pinned in the right margin like a clipped Polaroid. States: idle = slot shows a group photo; row hover or focus = row gets a highlighter swipe and the slot swaps to that person's portrait with their name caption; leaving restores the group photo.
motion: Highlighter swipe: background-size 0 to 100% over 220ms ease-out. Portrait swap: crossfade 180ms with a 1.5 degree tilt settle, like a photo being re-clipped. On in-view, rows' rules draw left to right once with a 30ms stagger. Hovering a name also nudges its pen underline 2px right over 160ms.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the full sheet with all names and roles readable and a photo in the slot. Hovered and idle states differ only in highlight and photo, never in hidden text.
mobile: Portrait slot moves inline: each row becomes a compact card with a small 56px portrait beside the name, and the sheet columns stack under the name. No hover required.
a11y: Real table with th headers or a list if few columns. Each row is focusable via a link to the person's bio so keyboard users trigger the swap. Portraits have alt with names. Reduced motion disables swipe and tilt.
avoid: Portraits that only appear on hover with no other way to see them, handwriting faces for body text, rows that shift height on hover, and fake signatures.

stack_notes.css: Portrait slot stacks all portraits absolutely; section:has(tr:nth-child(3):is(:hover, :focus-within)) .portrait:nth-child(3) shows it. Highlighter via linear-gradient background-size transition. Sticky slot with position: sticky. Preload portraits with loading eager only for the first few rows.
stack_notes.js: Optional: pointerenter and focusin set data-person on the section; preload portraits after idle with requestIdleCallback. On touch devices, tapping a row toggles the portrait instead.

name: Tape measure timeline
blueprint: Section 350vh, sticky stage. A yellow steel tape measure extends horizontally across the stage, 6rem tall, with year ticks as real DOM labels every year and minor ticks for months. The tape case sits fixed at the left edge. Milestone tags hang from the tape on short strings: year clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem), title, one sentence, optional photo. A fixed reading notch at 40% of the stage width marks 'now reading'. States: tag before notch = settled; at notch = enlarged 1.1x, full ink; after = waiting, 70% ink.
motion: Progress 0..1 pulls the tape out of the case: track translateX from 0 to minus overflow, tick labels sliding under the notch. Tags swing gently on their strings with rotation mapped to their distance from the notch (max 4 degrees), not velocity. At 100% the tape locks with a small detent.
still_check: At 50% the notch sits on a mid-history year with that tag enlarged and readable, neighbouring tags visible. At 25% and 75% different years sit under the notch and more tape has extended from the case.
mobile: Rotate the axis: the tape runs vertically down the left edge, tags stack on the right in normal flow, and the notch becomes a sticky year badge at the top. No pinning.
a11y: Milestones are an ol with time elements; the tape graphic and ticks are aria-hidden except the milestone years. Reduced motion shows the static vertical layout. Keyboard focus on a tag scrolls the track to it.
avoid: Tags overlapping each other at dense years, tick labels too small to read, horizontal scroll hijack from wheel events, and swing animations that make text wobble at read time.

stack_notes.css: Sticky stage with a scroll() timeline translating the track; tag rotation via view() timeline with inline axis where supported. Fallback is the vertical layout for all browsers without scroll timelines via @supports.
stack_notes.js: Measure overflow, map progress to translateX in rAF; compute each tag's distance to the notch to set rotation and scale. Recompute on resize via ResizeObserver.

name: Founding letter on stacked paper
blueprint: A letter on a cream sheet, max-width 40rem, padding clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem), body serif 1.125rem line height 1.75, signed at the bottom. Behind it, two offset sheets peek out (rotated -2 and 1.5 degrees) holding an old photo and a handwritten recipe or first invoice. Margin notes in a second colour sit in the left margin at 0.875rem, each tied to a sentence. Section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). States: in-view = sheets fan slightly open; margin notes appear as their sentence passes centre; done = signature visible.
motion: Across the section's view range, back sheets rotate from 0 to their resting angles and translate 12-24px outward, so the stack fans gradually as you read. Margin notes fade from 0 to 1 over their sentence's entry range. Signature stroke draws in over the last 15% of the range.
still_check: At 50% the letter is fully legible, sheets are half fanned, and the first two margin notes are visible. At 25% sheets are nearly closed with one note; at 75% sheets are fully fanned and the signature starts.
mobile: Back sheets become a single peeking sheet above the letter with the photo; margin notes become inline indented asides after their sentence. Fan angles halve.
a11y: Letter is an article with a heading and signature as text; margin notes are aside elements in reading order. Photo has alt text. Reduced motion shows the fully fanned state and signature at once.
avoid: Paper textures that reduce text contrast, notes covering letter text, cursive body copy, and rotating the main letter itself so lines tilt.

stack_notes.css: animation-timeline: view() on the section drives back-sheet transforms; per-note view() timelines for fades; signature SVG stroke-dashoffset with animation-range exit. IntersectionObserver fallback adds fanned class. Use transform-origin at the bottom corner of each sheet.
stack_notes.js: Only needed for fallback: IntersectionObserver with multiple thresholds sets a --p custom property; CSS maps --p to rotations. No other script. Disconnect the observer once fully fanned and on unmount.

name: Walk-through hallway gallery
blueprint: Section 500vh, sticky stage with perspective 900px. A CSS 3D hallway: two side walls built from rotated planes plus floor and ceiling, each wall holding 4-5 framed images at rotateY 90 and -90 degrees. A placard below each frame gives title, place and date as DOM text at 0.9375rem. The far end wall holds a hero image and a call link. Section headline clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem) sits on the end wall. States: frame approaching = lit by a soft spotlight gradient; frame passing = spotlight fades; end = camera stops facing the end wall.
motion: Progress 0..1 dollies the camera: hallway container translateZ from 0 to the hallway length. 0-85% travel past the frames, with the nearest frame's spotlight brightening as it gets within range. At points matching each frame, the camera turns 12 degrees toward it for readability, easing back. 85-100%: camera halts at the end wall; headline and link fully lit.
still_check: At 50% two framed images and their placards sit at a readable angle, the end wall visible but distant; no blank corridor. At 25% the first frames dominate; at 75% the end wall is large and later frames pass.
mobile: Drop 3D: convert to a vertical scroll of full-width framed images with placards, each sliding in with a slight perspective tilt on entry, and the end wall becoming the final block.
a11y: Frames are a list of figures with figcaption placards in DOM order. Reduced motion renders the flat mobile layout on all sizes. Keyboard focus on a frame jumps progress so that frame faces the camera.
avoid: Placards rotated so steeply they become unreadable, camera passing through frames, nausea-inducing turns, images loading as blank walls, and long 500vh runs with no visible progress cue.

stack_notes.css: transform-style: preserve-3d stage; hallway translateZ bound to a scroll() timeline on the section with position: sticky. Spotlights via view() timeline is not possible inside 3D, so use opacity keyframes on the same scroll timeline at offsets.
stack_notes.js: Compute progress, set translateZ and small rotateY in rAF with damping; per-frame distance drives spotlight opacity. three.js can replace CSS 3D for real lighting if already in the project. Lazy-load images two frames ahead. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Chalkboard day-part board
blueprint: A framed slate panel, max-width 72rem, dark green-black ground with a 1.25rem wooden frame border and faint chalk-dust noise texture. Top edge carries three hand-lettered day-part tabs (Breakfast, Lunch, Supper) as radio inputs styled like chalk labels, font-size clamp(1.1rem, 2vw, 1.5rem). Below, a two-column dish list: dish name in a chalk script at clamp(1.25rem, 2.6vw, 1.9rem), one-line description, price right-aligned. A small smudged eraser mark sits behind the active tab. The current day-part is preselected from the local clock. Section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 8rem). States: idle (slate rests), active tab (underline chalk stroke), switching (old list wiped, new list written), done.
motion: On tab change the outgoing list fades to 0 opacity with a 6px horizontal smear over 220ms ease-in, like an eraser pass; the incoming list draws in with a left-to-right clip-path inset reveal over 420ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), staggered 40ms per dish. The chalk underline under the active tab scales from 0 to 1 on the x axis over 300ms. No scroll-linked motion.
still_check: At 50% the slate is fully visible with one day-part list complete and its tab underlined; all prices legible. 25% and 75% differ only in framing: top tabs entering versus full list and frame bottom with the specials note visible.
mobile: At 375px the slate drops the frame to 0.5rem, tabs become a horizontally scrollable segmented row pinned at the top of the slate, and the dish list collapses to one column with prices on the same line as names.
a11y: Tabs are a real radio group inside a fieldset with a legend, so arrow keys switch day-parts. Panels use hidden states, not opacity alone. Reduced motion swaps the eraser and write-in for an instant swap. Chalk text keeps at least 7:1 contrast on the slate.
avoid: Chalk script fonts that are illegible at small sizes, texture so heavy it lowers contrast, prices baked into an image, defaulting to breakfast at 8pm, or layout jump when lists of different lengths swap.

stack_notes.css: Radio inputs plus :has(#lunch:checked) toggle panel visibility; @starting-style gives the write-in clip-path entry; a grid-template-areas stack keeps all panels in one cell so height is the max of the three and nothing shifts.
stack_notes.js: A few lines read new Date().getHours() to preselect the day-part; optional WAAPI animates clip-path for older engines. Any framework tab component works if it renders all three lists in the DOM and only toggles visibility.

name: Printed card with allergen toggles
blueprint: A cream card-stock panel, max-width 46rem, centred on a darker linen ground, with a 1px inset rule 1rem from the edge like a printed menu. Course headings in small caps at clamp(0.85rem, 1.4vw, 1rem) with wide tracking. Each dish row: name, a dotted leader line filling the gap, and the price, using a flex row with the leader as a border-bottom dotted spacer. Allergen codes (G, D, N, S) sit as tiny superscript letters. Above the card, a row of toggle chips labelled No gluten, No dairy, No nuts, Vegan. Section padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem). States: idle, filter active (non-matching rows dim to 30% and get a hairline strike), all clear.
motion: Toggling a chip dims non-matching rows over 200ms ease-out and draws a hairline strike through them from left to right over 260ms; matching rows stay in place so the card never reflows. The chip fills with ink colour over 150ms. A count line under the chips updates its number with a short 120ms crossfade.
still_check: At 50% the full printed card is visible with course headings, dotted leaders and prices aligned; if a filter is on, dimmed rows remain readable. At 25% the chips and first course show; at 75% the last course and allergen key show.
mobile: At 375px the card loses its outer linen margin, leaders shrink to a minimum 1.5rem, long dish names wrap above the leader and price, and chips become a two-by-two grid sitting sticky above the card while it scrolls.
a11y: Chips are checkbox inputs with visible focus rings. Filtered rows get a visually hidden note saying contains nuts rather than being removed. The allergen key is a definition list. Reduced motion skips the strike draw. A live region announces the matching dish count.
avoid: Removing filtered dishes so the card jumps, relying on colour alone for allergens, leaders that break onto two lines, tiny superscripts below 0.7rem, or chips that claim safety without a kitchen note about cross-contact.

stack_notes.css: Checkboxes plus :has() selectors such as .menu:has(#nuts:checked) .dish[data-n] apply the dim and strike; the strike is a pseudo-element scaled on the x axis with a transition; leaders use flex-grow and a dotted border-bottom.
stack_notes.js: Optional: a tiny script counts visible matches into an aria-live element and syncs chips to the URL hash. Data can come from any CMS as dish rows with allergen data attributes; no library required.

name: Swatch book fan-out
blueprint: Products sold in colourways (paint, fabric, tiles) shown as a physical swatch book. Left column 5/12: product name at clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem), material notes, price, add button. Right column 7/12: a stack of 8-12 tall swatch strips, each 9rem by 26rem with a rounded top, colour name and code printed at the bottom like a paint chip, pivoting from a shared rivet at the bottom-left. Section is pinned for 200vh. States: closed (strips stacked), fanning (strips rotate apart), open (full arc of 70 degrees), selected (one strip lifts 2rem and the left column updates to that colourway).
motion: 0-20%: stack sits closed with the top swatch name readable. 20-70%: strips rotate about the rivet from 0 to their slot angle, each offset by index times 7 degrees, eased with progress squared. 70-100%: the arc holds open and the swatch nearest the centre line lifts and becomes selected. Clicking a strip selects it with a 260ms lift transition.
still_check: At 50% the fan is half open with at least five colour names legible and the left product copy complete. At 25% only two or three strips have separated; at 75% the full arc is open with one strip lifted and its name in the left column.
mobile: At 375px the pin is removed; the fan becomes a horizontal scroll-snap row of swatch strips at 6rem wide below the product copy, with the selected strip raised and its name shown in a sticky bar with the add button.
a11y: Swatches are a radio group of buttons with colour name and code as text, so selection works by keyboard alone. Reduced motion renders the open arc statically. Focus raises the strip like hover. Colour names never rely on the chip colour itself.
avoid: Strips overlapping the colour name text, a closed stack at mid-scroll that looks empty, scroll hijack that traps the page, selecting by scroll position only, or colour chips that misrepresent the real product shade.

stack_notes.css: Scroll-driven path: each strip gets a custom property --i and an animation keyed to animation-timeline: view() on a tall wrapper, rotating to calc(var(--i) * 7deg); position: sticky pins the stage; IntersectionObserver toggles a fallback open class.
stack_notes.js: rAF reads wrapper progress from getBoundingClientRect and sets --p on the stack; WAAPI handles the click lift. Selected colourway swaps the product image and price; any project animation library can drive the same --p variable. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Turntable with jeweller's loupe
blueprint: One hero product per row in a short catalogue of 3-5 crafted items (watches, ceramics, shoes). Grid: 7/12 stage on the left with a WebGL canvas showing the product on a turntable, 5/12 spec column on the right: maker mark, name at clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3.25rem), a materials ledger, price, add button. A circular loupe, clamp(8rem, 16vw, 12rem) wide with a brass rim, follows the pointer over the stage and shows a 3x magnified render with a small caption naming the detail under it (hand-stitched welt, 18k crown). Stage sits beneath the loupe; spec text never overlaps the stage. States: idle, rotating with progress, loupe active, detail pinned.
motion: As the row scrolls from 0 to 100% the turntable rotates the product 0 to 300 degrees on the y axis, so each still shows a different face. Hotspot dots fade in at 30%, 55% and 80% of the rotation. The loupe follows the pointer with a 90ms lerp and scales in from 0.6 over 180ms on enter. Clicking a hotspot pins the loupe there.
still_check: At 50% the product is fully lit at roughly 150 degrees with at least one hotspot visible and the spec column complete. At 25% the front face shows; at 75% the back detail and a different hotspot caption show.
mobile: At 375px the stage stacks above the specs at 80vw tall; the loupe becomes tap-to-inspect on hotspot dots, opening a fixed circular detail view near the bottom of the stage; rotation is a drag gesture plus the scroll progress, shortened to 180 degrees.
a11y: Every hotspot is a button with its detail caption as text, listed again in the spec ledger. Canvas is aria-hidden with a poster image fallback. Reduced motion freezes rotation at the hero angle and replaces the follow loupe with static magnified crops.
avoid: Heavy GLB files that delay LCP, a loupe that covers the price or add button, hotspot copy that only exists inside the canvas, uninitialised black canvas frames, or rotation tied to wheel velocity.

stack_notes.css: CSS fallback: a sequence of 12 product photos swapped by a scroll-driven steps() animation on a background-position sprite, and the loupe as a circular element using a second high-resolution background positioned from pointer custom properties.
stack_notes.js: WebGL path with three.js or raw WebGL: load a compressed GLB lazily via IntersectionObserver, map section progress to rotation.y, render the loupe as a second camera with narrower fov to a circular scissor region. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Aisle shelf with hanging signs
blueprint: A shop-floor shelf, pinned for 300vh, translating horizontally. Above the shelf, hanging aisle signs (Pantry, Dairy, Bakery, Household) clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.4rem) on short strings mark category boundaries. The shelf is a long row of products standing on a 0.75rem wooden ledge, each with a shelf-edge price label: product name, unit price per 100g, big price at clamp(1.25rem, 2.4vw, 1.75rem), and a small barcode stripe. A fixed aisle indicator at bottom-left reads Aisle 2 of 4. Section padding top clamp(3rem, 7vw, 6rem). States: idle, travelling, sign passing centre (sign swings slightly), item hover (label lifts, quick add appears).
motion: 0-100% progress translates the shelf track from 0 to minus its overflow width, linear with scroll. Each hanging sign rotates from minus 4 to plus 4 degrees as it crosses the viewport centre, mapped to its own local progress. The aisle indicator number updates when a sign passes centre, with a 160ms vertical slide. Hover lifts a label 4px over 150ms.
still_check: At 50% the shelf is mid-aisle with one hanging sign readable, at least five full price labels legible, and no empty shelf gaps. At 25% the Pantry and Dairy signs show; at 75% Bakery to Household with a different indicator number.
mobile: At 375px the pin is dropped; each aisle becomes its own native horizontal scroll-snap row with its sign as a sticky left label, products at 9rem wide, and the quick add always visible on the label rather than on hover.
a11y: The shelf is a list of products grouped by headings for each aisle, so screen readers get categories. Native scroll stays available; arrow keys move focus product to product. Reduced motion shows aisles as stacked rows. Price labels meet 4.5:1 contrast.
avoid: Track widths measured before images load causing jumps, products cut in half at the end, labels that only appear on hover, scroll hijack that blocks vertical skimming, or a final frame with an empty shelf.

stack_notes.css: position: sticky stage with a tall wrapper; the track uses animation-timeline: view() with a translateX keyframe to a calc of the overflow width stored in a custom property set once; signs use their own view() timelines on the inline axis.
stack_notes.js: Measure track scrollWidth on load and resize with ResizeObserver, map wrapper progress to translateX in rAF, and update the aisle indicator from IntersectionObserver on signs. Any existing scroll library can drive the same progress. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Index-card file drawer
blueprint: Questions filed as index cards in an open card-catalogue drawer, max-width 52rem. Each card is a details element: the summary is the card's top strip with a coloured filing tab offset per category (Booking, Payment, Policies) at clamp(0.75rem, 1.2vw, 0.9rem), question text at clamp(1.05rem, 1.8vw, 1.3rem) on a ruled card with a red top rule. Cards overlap by 0.75rem like a drawer of cards seen from above at a slight angle. Opening a card lifts it out of the row, revealing the full ruled answer area with a stamped reviewed-on date. Drawer front with brass label holder titled Questions, A to Z. States: filed, hover (card rises 6px), open (card fully pulled), closed.
motion: Hover raises a card 6px over 160ms ease-out. Open uses interpolate-size so the card height grows from the summary strip to full content over 320ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) while its shadow deepens. Cards below slide down naturally with the height change. The reviewed stamp fades and rotates from minus 8 to minus 4 degrees in 200ms.
still_check: At 50% the drawer shows a run of filed cards with all question strips legible and one card opened with complete answer text. At 25% the drawer front label and top cards show; at 75% the final category tabs and a contact note show.
mobile: At 375px the slight perspective is removed, overlap reduces to 0.4rem, category tabs move to the left edge of each strip as a coloured bar with a text label, and cards take full width with 1rem gutters.
a11y: Native details and summary give keyboard toggling and state. Category is text, not just tab colour. Reduced motion opens instantly. Focus ring outlines the whole card strip. Questions sit under an h2 with categories as h3 for navigation.
avoid: Overlap that hides question text, a closed card showing a half answer, colour-only categories, fixed heights that clip long answers, or every card opening at once on load.

stack_notes.css: details elements with interpolate-size: allow-keywords on the root and a transition on block-size for ::details-content; :has(details[open]) adjusts sibling overlap; the paper look is linear-gradient ruling plus a box-shadow stack.
stack_notes.js: For engines without interpolate-size, a small script measures scrollHeight and animates height with WAAPI on toggle events, then resets to auto. Optional: deep link to a card via hash and open it on load.

name: Two-sided contact card
blueprint: One card, aspect-ratio 3 / 2, max-width 52rem, upright on the page ground with a 1px border in the line colour and 4px corners (no tilt, no desk texture). Front: a photograph of the place at the card's full size with the business name at 1.25rem on a solid band at block-end. Back (the default side, so contact details are never hidden): start half holds a 2 to 3 sentence note from the owner at clamp(1.0625rem, 1.6vw, 1.25rem) in the reading face with text-wrap: pretty and their name and role; a 1px vertical rule; end half holds address, today's hours, phone and email at 1rem in a definition list, each a working link. A text button Show the place at block-end flips to the front and back. States: idle, button hover (underline thickens to 2px), flipped, focus (2px ring offset 2px on the button).
motion: The flip rotates the card 180deg on Y over 520ms cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1) with backface hidden; nothing else animates.
still_check: At 50% the message side faces up with all contact lines, the stamp and postmark legible, no partial flip. At 25% the card top and note show; at 75% the full card plus a line below with directions link.
mobile: At 375px the card drops its aspect ratio and stacks: stamp and postmark row on top, address lines next, note last, at full width with 1rem gutters; the tilt is removed and Turn over becomes a simple link to the photo.
a11y: Address uses the address element with tel and mailto links. Both card faces are real DOM and the hidden face gets inert. Reduced motion swaps the flip for a crossfade. Turn over is a button with aria-pressed and a visible focus ring.
avoid: Postage stamps, postmarks, handwriting fonts, tilted cards, shadows, contact details only on the hidden side, or a flip that leaves focus on an invisible face.

stack_notes.css: transform-style: preserve-3d with backface-visibility: hidden on two faces; :has(button[aria-pressed=true]) or a checkbox toggles rotateY(180deg); the hover flatten is a transition on rotate; entry via @starting-style. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.
stack_notes.js: A few lines toggle aria-pressed and inert on faces; optional pointer tilt with a 6 degree maximum using pointermove and custom properties, skipped when reduced motion is set. Date in the postmark generated with Intl.DateTimeFormat.

name: Routing panel by department
blueprint: Contact section inside max-width 72rem: h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem) with text-wrap: balance, then a two-column panel 4/12 and 8/12 with a 1px border and 4px corners. Start column: a list of 4 to 6 departments (Sales, Support, Billing, Press, Security) as rows 3.25rem tall, each with the name at 1rem and the promised response time at 0.875rem in tabular figures, the selected row in full ink with a 2px bar at inline-start. End column: the routing card for the selected department: who answers (name, role, 2.5rem photo), the response promise, direct email and phone as links, and one line on what to include in your message. Under the panel, one line with the general address for anyone unsure. Works as tabs (role tablist) with the first department selected on load, so details are never hidden. States: idle, row hover (background tint 4%), selected, focus (2px ring offset -2px inside the row).
motion: Switching departments crossfades the routing card over 180ms with a 6px rise; the bar moves to the new row in 200ms ease-out. No cables, no lamps.
still_check: At 50% the panel shows all five labelled sockets, one patched, and its routing card complete with email and response time. At 25% the heading and panel top show; at 75% the routing card and a fallback general address show.
mobile: At 375px sockets become a vertical list of rows, each with lamp, department, and extension; the cable is replaced by a short lit connector bar on the selected row, and the routing card opens directly under that row.
a11y: Sockets are a radio group with visible labels; the cable SVG is aria-hidden. Dimmed options stay at 4.5:1 contrast. Reduced motion shows the cable fully drawn instantly. The routing card is an output region announced politely on change.
avoid: Switchboard, brass or enamel skeuomorphs, patch-cable animations, all details hidden until a choice, more than 6 departments, or no general fallback address.

stack_notes.css: Radio inputs with :has(#billing:checked) to dim siblings, show the matching card, and set --path on the cable; the SVG path per socket animates stroke-dashoffset via transition; lamps are radial-gradient pseudo-elements.
stack_notes.js: Optional script preselects a department from a query string such as from a pricing page link, and updates the cable path with getBoundingClientRect when sockets reflow. Any form library can attach to the routing card if a form is needed.

name: Counter-slip footer
blueprint: Footer as a narrow, precisely set counter slip for a shop or cafe: a single column max-width 26rem at inline-start of the footer grid (not centred on a ground patch), monospace or the brand's tabular text face at 0.9375rem, line-height 1.6. Top: business name at 1.25rem caps with 0.06em tracking, address and phone. Then three short groups under small caps labels (Visit, Order, About) whose rows are real links with today's relevant fact at inline-end on a 1px dotted leader (Order online ... until 21:00; Visit ... open now). Last row, under a double 1px rule: opening hours for today in tabular figures. Beside it on wide screens, the rest of the footer (newsletter field with visible label, legal line) sits in a quiet second column. States: row hover (leader turns full ink, label underlines), focus (2px ring offset 2px), today's row in full ink.
motion: None on entry. Row hover transitions the leader colour over 120ms.
still_check: At 50% of the footer range the receipt is printed past the link groups with header and items fully legible, and no line sliced through mid-glyph thanks to stepped reveal. At 25% only the header shows; at 75% the total and barcode show.
mobile: At 375px the receipt takes full width minus 1rem gutters, monospace size holds at 0.9rem, link groups remain stacked, and the print reveal range shortens so the whole receipt prints within one screen of scroll.
a11y: Content is a nav with lists under headings, not a table. The barcode is aria-hidden. Reduced motion shows the receipt fully printed. Links have clear focus outlines and 44px tall rows. Newsletter input has a real label.
avoid: Torn zigzag edges, CSS barcodes, fake quantities or prices beside links, print-out reveal animations, thermal-grey low-contrast text, or centring the slip on an empty band.

stack_notes.css: animation-timeline: view() with animation-range entry 0% to cover 40%, using steps(12) on clip-path inset; the zigzag edge is a mask-image of a repeating conic or linear gradient; dotted spacers via flex and border-bottom.
stack_notes.js: Fallback: IntersectionObserver adds a printing class that runs a CSS keyframe once. Short pages where the footer is already in view get printed state immediately. No library needed.

name: Colophon with the cropped wordmark
blueprint: A dark footer that ends the page, padding-top clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem). Top band on a 12-column grid: a 4-column contact block (studio email at clamp(1.25rem, 2vw, 1.75rem), phone, address), 2 columns each for Work, Studio and Social links at 0.9375rem, and a 2-column colophon (typefaces, built by, year) at 0.8125rem in the muted ink; all text 4.5:1 on the dark ground. A 1px rule at 15% opacity. Bottom band: the wordmark in the display face fitted to the full content width (font-size computed so the ink spans edge to edge), solid in the light ink, its baseline sitting on the viewport bottom so the descender area crops cleanly. Legal links at 0.75rem sit above the wordmark at inline-end. States: link hover (underline draws from inline-start in 180ms), focus (2px ring offset 3px).
motion: As the footer enters, the wordmark rises 4vh into place over its view range 0 to 50% with a mask from its baseline; once set it never moves. Links do not animate on entry.
still_check: At 50% the colophon and sitemap are fully legible and the wordmark is at least 60% revealed with crisp edges, not a blurred smear. At 25% the wordmark is a low sliver; at 75% it is fully risen with the fill image settled.
mobile: At 375px the wordmark size drops to clamp(3.5rem, 24vw, 6rem) and may break onto two lines; sitemap becomes a two-column list, and the hover image swap becomes a static single fill.
a11y: The wordmark is a real text element, aria-hidden only if the brand name already appears as text in the footer. Reduced motion shows it fully risen with a flat colour fill. Fill images keep the letters above 3:1 contrast against the ground.
avoid: Video or image strips inside the letters, a wordmark that crops above mid-x-height, footers padded to 90vh, colophon text below 4.5:1, or the wordmark used without the brand's real name.

stack_notes.css: mask-image linear-gradient with mask-position animated by animation-timeline: view(); background-clip: text with a background-image per state toggled by :has(a[data-work=x]:hover) on the footer; translate the background on the same timeline. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver fallback adds a risen class with a 900ms transition. Optional WAAPI or any existing library can scrub the mask position by measured progress for engines without scroll timelines.

name: From the station, on foot
blueprint: Split 6/6 grid. Left: an illustrated SVG street map in two inks with the nearest transit stop, three landmarks, and the shop marked by a door icon, inside a rounded frame clamp(20rem, 45vw, 34rem) tall. Right: numbered walking steps written as real directions (Exit the station by the north stairs, Pass the green bakery awning, Our door is the blue one next to the pharmacy), each with a landmark thumbnail and distance, plus a summary line: 4 min walk, step-free route. Section padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem). States: idle, step active (its path segment and landmark highlight), done (full route drawn, door pulses once).
motion: Scroll progress through the section draws the route line with stroke-dashoffset from 0 to 100% of its length; each step activates when progress passes its segment threshold (0-25%, 25-55%, 55-85%), highlighting the landmark with a 200ms ring scale. 85-100%: route complete, door icon pulses once over 600ms.
still_check: At 50% the route is drawn past the second landmark, step 2 is active, all step text is legible, and the map is never blank. At 25% the first segment and step 1 show; at 75% step 3 and most of the route show.
mobile: At 375px the map stacks above the steps at 70vw height, becomes sticky at the top while steps scroll beneath it, and the route draws per step entry; a button opens the address in the device map app.
a11y: Steps are an ordered list and include accessibility notes such as step-free. The SVG map has a title and aria-describedby pointing to the list. Reduced motion shows the full route with all landmarks labelled. The map app link is a normal anchor.
avoid: Embedding a heavy third-party map iframe above the fold, directions that only exist as map art, a route that animates by time and is blank when scrolled fast, or tiny landmark labels on mobile.

stack_notes.css: SVG path with pathLength set to 1 and stroke-dashoffset animated by animation-timeline: view(); steps highlight with their own view() timelines; position: sticky keeps the map in view on mobile.
stack_notes.js: Compute section progress with getBoundingClientRect in rAF and set stroke-dashoffset; IntersectionObserver per step sets the active landmark. A mapping library already in the project can replace the SVG while keeping the ordered list. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Festival timetable with playhead
blueprint: A multi-stage festival timetable. Columns are stages (Main, Tent, Garden, Club) with sticky colour headers; rows are 15-minute slots from 12:00 to 00:00 with a sticky time gutter clamp(3rem, 6vw, 4.5rem) wide. Each act is a block whose height equals its set length, showing artist, start and end, and a star button to add to My day. A horizontal playhead line labelled with a time marker crosses all stages. Day tabs (Fri, Sat, Sun) above. A clash badge appears when two starred sets overlap. Section padding clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem). States: idle, playhead moving, act under playhead (highlighted as on now), starred, clash.
motion: During the event the playhead sits at the real time. Before or after, scroll progress through the grid maps 0-100% to 12:00-00:00 and moves the playhead down; acts it crosses lift with a 2px outline and an on now tag over 150ms. Starring fills the star with a 200ms scale pop and recounts My day.
still_check: At 50% the playhead sits near 18:00 across all four stages, at least eight act blocks are legible with times, and headers are visible. At 25% early afternoon acts show; at 75% evening headliners show under the playhead.
mobile: At 375px the grid shows one stage at a time as a swipeable column with stage tabs, or a list sorted by time with stage chips; the playhead becomes a sticky now bar at the top of the list.
a11y: Underlying markup is a table per day with stages as column headers and times as row headers, enhanced visually as a grid. Star buttons have aria-pressed. Reduced motion pins the playhead to real time without scroll scrubbing. Stage colours always have text labels.
avoid: A grid wider than the screen with no stage indicator, act names truncated in short slots without a tooltip or detail link, playhead covering text, clash badges by colour only, or time zones not stated.

stack_notes.css: CSS grid with grid-row spans computed from slot indexes in inline custom properties; sticky headers and time gutter via position: sticky; playhead translate driven by animation-timeline: view() on the grid wrapper.
stack_notes.js: Script sets the playhead to the current time with a minute interval when live, stores starred acts in localStorage behind try catch, and detects clashes by comparing start and end values. Any framework renders the blocks from a JSON line-up. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Studio week board
blueprint: A pinboard-style week grid for a yoga, climbing, or cooking studio. Seven day columns with dates, three day-part bands (Morning, Midday, Evening). Each class is a peg tag: time, class name at clamp(0.95rem, 1.5vw, 1.1rem), teacher, level dot with text, and a capacity strip of 12 small pips showing booked versus open. Above: filter chips by class type and a This week or Next week toggle. Today's column has a warm wash and a Today label. Padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem). States: idle, filter active (other tags fade to 25% but keep slots), tag hover (lifts and shows Book a spot), full (tag reads Waitlist).
motion: Filtering fades non-matching tags to 25% opacity over 200ms and scales them to 0.97 so the week keeps its shape. Hover lifts a tag 3px with a 150ms shadow transition. On first view the today column wash grows from 0 to full height over 500ms ease-out. Capacity pips fill on entry with a 30ms stagger.
still_check: At 50% all seven columns and the Morning and Evening bands are visible, tags legible with times and capacity, and today highlighted. At 25% the chips and morning band show; at 75% evening classes and the timezone note show.
mobile: At 375px the grid becomes a day strip of seven date buttons at the top with today selected, and the selected day shows its classes as a vertical list of tags grouped by day-part; filters scroll horizontally.
a11y: Each day is a list under a heading with the date; capacity is text such as 3 of 12 spots left, with pips aria-hidden. Filters are checkboxes. Reduced motion skips lifts and fills. Level uses text, not only coloured dots.
avoid: A seven-column grid squeezed into phone width, hiding filtered classes so days look empty, capacity shown only as pips, buttons that appear only on hover, or stale weeks shown without dates.

stack_notes.css: Grid with seven columns and named rows per day-part; :has() on filter checkboxes dims tags by data type; today wash is a scaled pseudo-element with @starting-style; container queries switch to the day strip layout under 40rem.
stack_notes.js: A small script marks today from the date, switches week data, and fills capacity from a booking API if present. IntersectionObserver triggers the pip stagger. Any calendar backend can supply class rows.

name: Listing told room by room
blueprint: A single property listing told through its floor plan. Pinned stage 220vh. Left 7/12: an architectural SVG plan in thin ink lines, with room labels and square metres as real text positioned over rooms. Right 5/12: a spec ledger (address, price at clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 3rem), beds, baths, total area, energy rating), and a room card that changes as rooms highlight, showing a photo of that room and two facts (south light, original parquet). A north arrow and scale bar sit bottom-left. States: drawing (walls trace), room focus (room fill tint and card swap), complete (whole plan, all labels), hover a room (focus that room).
motion: 0-35%: exterior walls draw with stroke-dashoffset, then interior walls, doors swing in as quarter arcs. 35-90%: rooms take focus in walk-through order (hall, living, kitchen, bedrooms), each tint fading in at 20% opacity and the room card crossfading over 250ms. 90-100%: full plan with every label, ledger fully visible throughout.
still_check: At 50% walls are fully drawn, the living room is tinted, its card shows photo and facts, and the spec ledger is complete. At 25% walls are mid-trace with ledger visible; at 75% a bedroom is focused with a different photo.
mobile: At 375px the pin is removed; the plan sits full-width at top with walls drawn on entry, and rooms are a horizontal scroll-snap row of room cards below; tapping a card tints its room on the plan above.
a11y: Rooms are also an ordered list with areas, so the plan is not the only source. SVG has a title and is labelled as a floor plan. Reduced motion shows the complete plan and lets users pick rooms by button. Price and specs stay real text.
avoid: Room labels inside SVG paths with no DOM copy, a blank plan at the top of the range, card photos loading late and shifting the ledger, scroll lock on mobile, or areas without units.

stack_notes.css: SVG with pathLength 1 on wall groups and stroke-dashoffset animated on a view() timeline; room tints keyed to animation-range segments; sticky stage; :has(.room:hover) highlights a room and its card.
stack_notes.js: rAF maps section progress to wall drawing and to the active room index, swapping the room card with a crossfade; IntersectionObserver lazy-loads room photos ahead of their segment. Plans can come from the agent's CAD export as SVG. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.

name: Departures board of open roles
blueprint: Open jobs listed as a station departures board. A dark panel, max-width 76rem, with yellow-on-black split-flap characters in a monospace at clamp(0.95rem, 1.6vw, 1.25rem). Columns: Departs (start date), Role, Team, Platform (Remote, Berlin, Lisbon), Status (Boarding, On time, Closing). A header row in small caps and a board title Now hiring, clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem). Filter flaps above for team and location. Each row is a link to the job page with an arrow on hover. States: idle, flipping (characters cycle into place), filtered, row hover (row back-lights), closing soon (status flap blinks once).
motion: When the board enters view, each character cell flips through 3 to 6 random glyphs before landing, 40ms per flip, staggered 20ms per column and 60ms per row; total under 1.4s. Filtering re-flips only changed cells. Row hover back-lights over 120ms. After landing, all characters are static.
still_check: At 50% the board shows at least five fully settled rows with roles readable, not mid-flip noise. At 25% the board title and header row show with first rows; at 75% last rows and an Apply anyway row show.
mobile: At 375px the board keeps Role and Platform as the visible flap columns, moving Team and Departs into a second line per row; flap animation runs only on the role text, and rows become 56px tall tap targets.
a11y: The board is a table with real header cells, each role an anchor. Individual flap glyphs are aria-hidden; each cell carries the final text for assistive tech. Reduced motion skips flipping. Status words not colour carry meaning.
avoid: Screen readers hearing random glyphs, flipping that repeats on every scroll, rows unreadable while flipping at screenshot time, fixed character widths that truncate role titles, or yellow on black below contrast at small sizes.

stack_notes.css: Each cell renders the final text with a CSS counter-free fallback; flip faces use two halves with rotateX transitions and backface hidden; @starting-style gives a single settle flip without script; table layout with sticky header.
stack_notes.js: Split final strings into spans and run a short glyph cycle with setTimeout or WAAPI per cell, triggered once by IntersectionObserver; rows rendered from the careers API or a JSON file. No library needed. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Boarding pass itinerary
blueprint: A multi-day trip itinerary. Left 6/12: a sticky illustrated map, height 80vh, with stops as numbered pins and a dashed route. Right 6/12: a stack of day passes styled as boarding passes, each 100% wide with a perforated stub: day number in large type clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.5rem), from and to stops with three-letter codes, departure time, transport mode icon with text, and a short paragraph of what happens; stub side shows stay name and a meal included note. Section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem). States: pass inactive (muted), pass active (full colour, stub stamped), map focused on that leg, final (route complete, total km and nights summary).
motion: As each pass crosses the viewport centre, local progress 0-100% advances the map: the route segment for that leg draws from 0 to full, the map pans and zooms to frame both stops over the same range, and the stub receives a rotated stamp at 60%. Between legs the map holds the previous leg fully drawn.
still_check: At 50% the map shows roughly half the route drawn with the current leg framed, and the active pass is fully legible with codes and times. At 25% early legs are drawn; at 75% the later region is framed with a different active pass.
mobile: At 375px the map becomes a short sticky strip 40vh tall at the top, showing only the active leg, while passes scroll beneath it at full width; the perforated stub folds under the main pass as a second row.
a11y: Days are an ordered list of articles with headings; the map is decorative with aria-hidden and the passes carry all stop names and times. Reduced motion shows the complete route and static active styles. Codes are explained once in an abbr title.
avoid: A map that pans with fixed timing and lands mid-leg, passes overlapping the map on narrow screens, invented airport codes that look real but are wrong, tiny stamp text as the only info, or a blank map before the first pass.

stack_notes.css: Sticky map with an SVG route; each leg path animates stroke-dashoffset on a named view-timeline set on its pass via view-timeline-name and timeline-scope; transform on the map group pans with the same timelines.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver picks the active pass; rAF maps its local progress to route drawing and a viewBox interpolation between leg bounds. A tile-map library the project already uses can replace the SVG, reading the same progress. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Where each gift goes
blueprint: Section padding clamp(4rem, 10vw, 8rem), max width 72rem. Top: h2 at clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 3.5rem) and one line naming last year audited total. Middle: one full-width bar 100% wide, height clamp(3rem, 7vw, 5rem), split into 4 to 6 labelled segments (Field programmes 71%, Training 14%, Fundraising 9%, Running costs 6%); each segment label is DOM text above it with its percentage in tabular figures. Below: a radiogroup of gift amounts (10, 25, 50, 100) styled as chips; the chosen amount shows a sentence card naming what it funds (25 pays two days of a field nurse) and outlines the matching share of each segment. States: idle (all segments solid), chip chosen (outline overlay, sentence swaps), in-view (segments grow to width once).
motion: Entering view (view timeline 0-40% of entry): segments grow from 0 to their width left to right, each starting 60ms after the previous, ease-out, labels fade up with their segment. After that the bar is static. Choosing a gift chip cross-fades the sentence card over 200ms and slides the outline overlay to its new widths over 240ms. No scroll-linked motion after entry.
still_check: At 50% the full bar shows every segment at its final width with every label and percentage readable, and the default gift sentence is visible. At 25% the bar may be mid-growth but labels already sit at final positions.
mobile: At 375px the single bar turns vertical-stacked: one row per segment with a thin bar, label left and percentage right, so no label is squeezed. Gift chips wrap into a 2 by 2 grid with 44px targets; the sentence card sits below them.
a11y: Under reduced motion segments render at final width with no growth. The bar has a visually hidden table (category, percentage) as its accessible source and the graphic is aria-hidden. Gift chips are a native radio group with visible focus rings; the sentence card is an aria-live polite region.
avoid: Segments under 4% with labels crammed inside them, percentages that do not sum to 100, growth that replays on every scroll, colour as the only label, and vague sentences that name no concrete thing a gift buys.

stack_notes.css: Segments are flex children with flex-basis set from a custom property; animation-timeline: view() with animation-range entry 0% entry 40% scales them from scaleX(0) with transform-origin left. Chip state uses :has(input:checked) to swap the sentence and set overlay widths. IntersectionObserver adds an in-view class where view timelines are unsupported. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: Optional: read the allocation from JSON, set custom properties, and update the overlay widths on radio change with WAAPI. Any chart library the project already ships can draw the bar, as long as the hidden table stays the source of truth.

name: Syllabus binder
blueprint: A course syllabus as a ring binder. Pinned stage 240vh. Centre: a stack of 6 module pages, each a paper sheet max-width 44rem with three punched holes on the left and a coloured index tab protruding from the right edge at a different height, labelled Module 1 to 6 with a short title. Each page shows module title at clamp(1.6rem, 3.6vw, 2.6rem), lessons as a checklist with durations, an outcome sentence, and a project brief box. Behind the stack, the binder spine and rings. States: page resting, page lifting (rotates over the rings to the left), page turned (rests as a thin edge on the left), tab clicked (jumps to that page).
motion: Progress is divided into six equal ranges. In each range the current page rotates on the y axis from 0 to minus 165 degrees around its left edge, with a 4% shadow sweep across the page beneath. Turned pages stack on the left as thin edges. Clicking a tab scrolls to that range smoothly over about 500ms.
still_check: At 50% three pages are turned, Module 4 lies flat and fully legible with lessons and durations, and all six tabs remain visible on the right. At 25% Module 2 is readable; at 75% Module 5 is readable.
mobile: At 375px the pin and 3D turn are removed; modules become stacked sheets with their tab as a coloured top strip, and the tab row becomes a sticky horizontal jump bar of six numbered chips.
a11y: Modules are an ordered list of sections with headings; tabs are anchor links to each module. Reduced motion stacks pages flat in order. Turned pages are inert while out of view. Lesson checklists are lists, not checkbox inputs.
avoid: Mid-turn pages at screenshot time with text sheared, tabs covered by turned pages, more than eight modules in one stack, hard-to-read handwriting fonts, or scroll hijack when users only want to read one module.

stack_notes.css: Each page has --i and an animation on a shared view() timeline with animation-range computed from calc(var(--i) * 16.66%), rotating on transform-origin left; perspective on the stage; sticky stage inside a tall wrapper. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.
stack_notes.js: rAF computes progress and sets each page rotation, snapping slightly so pages never rest mid-turn at range ends; tabs call scrollTo with the computed offset. Any existing animation library can consume the same progress.

name: Docs rail with live section ticks
blueprint: Three-column docs layout: left nav 16rem, content max 46rem, right on-this-page rail 14rem. Left nav is a tree of guides with a version picker at the top styled like a package tag (v3.2 stable). The right rail lists h2 and h3 anchors as rows, each with a vertical tick on its left edge; the tick for the section in view is filled, the ones read are half-tone, upcoming are hairlines. A small API status chip and an Edit this page link sit at the rail bottom. Body text at clamp(1rem, 1.1vw, 1.0625rem), line length 68ch. States: idle, section in view (tick fills, label bolds), read, version switched (banner noting changed pages).
motion: Each tick fills from top to bottom as its section scrolls through the viewport, mapped to that section's own progress, so the rail shows exactly how far through the current section you are. Label weight shifts over 150ms. Version switch shows a 240ms banner slide from the top of the content column.
still_check: At 50% of a long page the rail shows earlier ticks half-tone, one tick partly filled, upcoming hairlines, and all labels legible; content text unobscured. At 25% and 75% a different tick is partial.
mobile: At 375px both rails collapse: the left tree moves to a menu button, and the right rail becomes a sticky top bar showing the current section title with a thin fill under it and a drop-down listing all sections.
a11y: The rail is a nav with aria-label On this page and an ordered list of links; the current link gets aria-current location. Reduced motion uses discrete filled or empty ticks. Version picker is a native select with a label.
avoid: Scroll spy that flickers between sections, sticky rails taller than the viewport with no scroll, ticks as the only current indicator, version picker that loses the reader's page, or rails stealing content width on tablets.

stack_notes.css: Each section declares view-timeline-name and the rail sets timeline-scope on the layout root so each tick animates scale on its section's timeline; position: sticky for rails; container queries collapse rails under 64rem.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver with rootMargin marks the current section and sets aria-current; optional progress per section via getBoundingClientRect for engines without timeline-scope. Works with any static docs generator.

name: Admission-ticket call to action
blueprint: For events and festivals: one ticket, max-width 56rem, aspect-ratio about 5 / 2 (auto height below 40rem), centred, flat fill in the event's lead colour with 6px corners and two 0.75rem half-circle notches at the stub line via mask. Main body 70%: event name as h2 at clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.75rem) with text-wrap: balance, date, venue and price from in tabular figures, one line of terms. Stub 30%, after a 1px dashed perforation: the primary button 3.25rem tall with 4px corners (Get tickets), and the number left (412 left) in tabular figures. No serial numbers. States: idle, button hover (fill darkens 8%), pressed (depresses 1px), focus (2px ring offset 2px, never clipped by the mask).
motion: On first view the ticket rises 12px and fades in over 400ms once. Button press depresses 1px in 120ms. No tearing, tilting or delayed navigation.
still_check: At 50% the whole ticket is visible with headline, terms, serial, and stub button readable, stub attached. At 25% the ticket top and headline show; at 75% the ticket plus a secondary link below it show.
mobile: At 375px the ticket rotates its layout: the body stacks on top and the stub sits below a horizontal perforation, full width, with the button 52px tall; the tear motion becomes a short downward shift.
a11y: The stub action is a real link or button with text, not the whole ticket. Reduced motion removes tilt and tear, keeping a colour change. Focus-visible ring sits outside the notched mask so it is not clipped. Serial is decorative and aria-hidden.
avoid: Tilt or tear animations, fake serial numbers, raffle styling, delayed navigation, the mask clipping the focus ring, or using it for anything other than a real ticketed event.

stack_notes.css: mask with radial-gradient notches; :has(.stub a:hover, .stub a:focus-visible) moves the stub via transition; :active triggers the tear transform; entry via @starting-style; perforation as a repeating linear-gradient border.
stack_notes.js: Optional: intercept click, play a WAAPI tear keyframe for 260ms, then follow the href; skip when reduced motion is set or modifier keys are held. No library required; any existing animation tool can run the same keyframes.

name: Card to detail shared-element morph
blueprint: Applies between a listing page and a detail page. On the listing, each item shows an image, title, and price. On the detail page, the same image sits as a large hero clamp(20rem, 60vh, 44rem) tall, the title becomes the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 6vw, 5rem), the price moves to a buy panel. The three elements share view-transition-name values per item id, so the browser morphs position, size, and crop between pages. Other content crossfades. A back navigation reverses the morph into the original card slot. States: listing, morphing, detail, returning.
motion: On navigation, image, title, and price morph from card geometry to detail geometry over 380ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.1,1); the image keeps object-fit cover and its crop eases. Page root crossfades over 200ms. Detail secondary content fades and rises 12px, starting at 180ms. Back navigation uses the same timing in reverse.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. A paused frame mid-transition must show one image and one title, both readable, never doubled ghost text. The listing and detail end states are each complete compositions on their own.
mobile: At 375px the morph still runs but shortens to 300ms; the detail hero is full-bleed at 60vw tall; titles that wrap differently are crossfaded rather than morphed by assigning the name only to the image.
a11y: Reduced motion disables the morph via a media query and uses an instant swap. Focus moves to the detail h1 after navigation. Names never sit on interactive elements that would trap focus. Both pages work without the API.
avoid: Duplicate view-transition-name values on one page, which aborts the transition, text stretched during the morph, morphs over 500ms that feel slow, images loading late at the destination, or animating every card at once.

stack_notes.css: Cross-document: the at-rule view-transition with navigation auto on both pages; set view-transition-name inline per item id on listing and detail; style ::view-transition-group and ::view-transition-old or new for timing and to crossfade titles.
stack_notes.js: Single page apps call document.startViewTransition around the route update, assigning names only to the clicked card just before. Fallback: FLIP with getBoundingClientRect and WAAPI for engines without the API.

name: Ground colour handoff
blueprint: Each section declares its own ground and ink colours as custom properties, for example a bone ground with ink text, then a terracotta ground with cream text, then a deep green with mint. The page body background is not set per section; instead a fixed ground layer behind all content blends between neighbouring section colours based on scroll progress across the boundary zone, the 30vh before and after each seam. Text colour flips at the midpoint of the zone, not during it. States: inside section (stable colour), in seam zone (blending ground), past midpoint (ink swapped).
motion: Across each seam zone, 0-100% progress interpolates the ground from the previous section colour to the next in oklch space, linear with scroll. At 50% the ink colour switches in a 120ms transition, so text never sits mid-blend at low contrast. Outside zones, nothing moves.
still_check: At 50% of a seam, the ground is a mixed colour and all visible text uses whichever ink passes 4.5:1 on that mix. At 25% the ground is near the previous colour; at 75% near the next.
mobile: At 375px seam zones shorten to 20vh so colour changes complete within a thumb flick; the fixed layer stays a single element, avoiding repaint of large backgrounds.
a11y: Each section also sets its own background, so reduced motion or no support shows hard seams with correct contrast. Every colour pair is checked for contrast, including the midpoint mix. Colour carries no meaning on its own.
avoid: Text mid-blend dropping under contrast, ground keyed to scroll speed, images with transparent edges showing a mismatched colour, flashing between saturated hues, or colour changes inside a pinned section that already animates.

stack_notes.css: Register --ground as an at-property color; animate it on each seam element's view() timeline with animation-range cover 30% to 70%; the fixed ground layer reads var(--ground); ink flips with a step at the midpoint. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver with thresholds per seam computes progress and writes color-mix(in oklch) results to the ground layer style; the ink swap is a class at 0.5. Any library can drive the same custom property.

name: Button press ink spread
blueprint: Primary buttons are outlined with a 2px ink border on the page ground, label in ink. A pseudo-element holds an ink blot shaped by an organic blob mask, not a circle, positioned at the press point using pointer custom properties (defaulting to the centre for keyboard). Button height 3rem, padding inline clamp(1.25rem, 3vw, 2rem), radius 999px. States: idle (outline), hover (ink fills 15% as a faint wash), pressed (blot spreads from the press point to fill), released (filled for 200ms, label in ground colour, then settles to hover state or navigates).
motion: Press: the blot scales from 0 to 2.2 over 320ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) from the pointer position, with its blob mask rotating 20 degrees so the edge feels liquid. Label colour swaps at 40% of the spread. Release: blot fades to the hover wash over 260ms. Keyboard activation spreads from the centre.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. Any frame must keep the label legible: the label colour switch happens when the blot covers it, never leaving ink text on ink fill. Idle, hover, and pressed are each distinct at a glance.
mobile: At 375px the spread originates from the touch point using pointer events, runs 260ms, and buttons keep a minimum 48px height; hover wash is skipped on touch devices via hover media queries.
a11y: Uses a native button or link. Focus-visible ring sits 3px outside the outline. Reduced motion replaces the spread with an instant fill. The label stays the accessible name; the blot is a pseudo-element only.
avoid: Ink text on ink fill mid-press, blots overflowing the radius, delaying navigation for the animation, circular Material-like ripples that look stock, or rerunning on every hover.

stack_notes.css: Pseudo-element with mask-image of an inline SVG blob, transform-origin set from --x and --y; :active triggers scale with transition; label colour via :active plus a short transition-delay.
stack_notes.js: A pointerdown listener writes offsetX and offsetY to --x and --y; WAAPI can animate the blot for finer control and is cancelled on pointerleave. Listeners attach once with event delegation.

name: Underline that traces the word
blueprint: Inline text links in body copy. Idle: a hairline underline at 1px, 30% ink, with text-underline-offset 0.2em. Hover or focus: a second 2px line draws left to right along the word, following the line of text even when the link wraps onto two lines, because it is painted as a background on the inline box with box-decoration-break clone. Visited links keep a dotted idle line. Arrow glyph optional for external links. States: idle, hover or focus (line draws), active (line thickens to 3px), leave (line retracts to the right edge, not back to the left).
motion: Hover draws the line by animating background-size from 0 to 100% width over 280ms cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1), anchored left. On leave, the anchor switches to right and the line retracts over 220ms, so it travels through the word rather than rewinding. Wrapped links draw each line fragment simultaneously.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. In any still, link text must be fully legible and distinguishable as a link by the idle hairline alone, without relying on hover. Idle, hover, and visited states differ visibly.
mobile: At 375px there is no hover, so links show a 1.5px idle underline at 50% ink; tapping draws the full line during the press as feedback before navigation, using the active state.
a11y: Links always have an underline, never colour only. Focus-visible gets the full line plus a 2px outline offset. Reduced motion shows the drawn line instantly. Contrast of the idle line versus text is noted but text itself meets 4.5:1.
avoid: Removing the idle underline, lines that skip descender gaps awkwardly, animation on block-level nav items where it feels slow, wrapped links where only the last line draws, or rewinding retract motion.

stack_notes.css: background-image linear-gradient currentColor, background-size 0 2px to 100% 2px, background-position left bottom switching to right bottom on leave, box-decoration-break clone for wraps; transitions only, no script.
stack_notes.js: None needed. For SVG hand-drawn variants, inject a path per link fragment using getClientRects and animate stroke-dashoffset with WAAPI, keeping the CSS underline as the base.

name: Add to bag flight
blueprint: On product cards and detail pages. Pressing Add to bag clones a small thumbnail of the product (4rem square, rounded) at the button location and flies it along an arc to the bag icon in the header. The bag icon is a tote outline with a count badge. On arrival, the tote dips 3px as if catching weight and the badge number rolls up. A short line under the button confirms Added, size M, with an Undo link. States: idle, adding (button shows spinner text Adding), flying, landed (badge updated), undone.
motion: The clone travels a quadratic arc from button to bag over 520ms: x uses ease-in-out, y uses ease-out then ease-in for a natural lob, scale goes from 1 to 0.35 and opacity holds until the final 80ms. On landing, the tote dips with a 220ms spring-like keyframe and the badge digit slides up over 180ms.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. Any frame must show the button label and the bag count as legible text; the flying clone never covers the header nav labels or the price. The landed state shows the new count and the confirmation line.
mobile: At 375px the header bag may be off-screen; the clone flies to a sticky bottom bag bar instead, which slides up showing item count and Checkout. Arc height reduces to keep the clone on screen.
a11y: The clone is aria-hidden. A live region announces Added to bag, 3 items. Reduced motion skips the flight and pulses the badge. Undo is a focusable button. The bag link label includes the count as text.
avoid: Flight ending at a stale position after scroll, updating the count before the server confirms, clones left in the DOM, covering the price during flight, or flights for bulk add that spawn dozens of clones.

stack_notes.css: CSS path: offset-path with a path() arc computed into a custom property, plus offset-distance animated from 0 to 100% via a keyframe; badge roll uses a translated stack of digits; position fixed clone.
stack_notes.js: Measure button and bag rects with getBoundingClientRect at click, create a fixed clone, animate with WAAPI using separate x and y keyframes for the arc, remove on finish, then update the badge after the cart request resolves.

name: Odometer number tick
blueprint: Any number that changes in response to input: a pricing total when switching monthly to yearly, a mortgage payment as a slider moves, a dashboard metric on refresh. Each digit sits in a fixed-width cell using tabular numerals, clipped to one line height, containing a vertical strip of 0 to 9. Currency symbol and separators are static cells. A small delta chip appears to the right (plus 12 or minus 40) in the direction's text. States: idle, changing (digits roll), settled, delta shown for 2s then fades to 50%.
motion: On change, each digit strip translates vertically to its new value over 360ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), with lower-order digits starting 20ms later than higher ones so the change reads left to right. Digits roll upward for increases and downward for decreases. Delta chip fades in over 150ms.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. Any frame must show a readable number; mid-roll frames show each digit at most half offset, and the settled state shows the exact value with its delta chip. Width never changes during the roll.
mobile: At 375px the same behaviour holds; for very large numbers, the roll applies only to the last four digits to avoid jitter, and slider-driven changes throttle the roll so it settles after input stops.
a11y: The digit strips are aria-hidden; a visually hidden span holds the full formatted value and updates via aria-live polite, debounced so sliders do not spam announcements. Reduced motion swaps values instantly with tabular numerals.
avoid: Width jumps from proportional digits, rolling through every intermediate value on large jumps, announcing every slider tick, formatting that drops currency, or a roll so long the value lags the input.

stack_notes.css: Register --d as an integer at-property per digit and transition it; translate the strip by calc(var(--d) * -1lh); font-variant-numeric tabular-nums; direction class picks up or down travel. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.
stack_notes.js: Format with Intl.NumberFormat, split into characters, set --d per digit cell, and update the hidden live text after a 400ms debounce. WAAPI can replace the transition for older engines.

name: Focus ring that travels
blueprint: One shared focus indicator per component group (a toolbar, a nav, a filter row, a pricing toggle). Instead of each control drawing its own ring, a single absolutely positioned ring element, 2px solid accent with a 3px offset and the control's radius, slides from the previously focused control to the newly focused one. The ring sits above controls in z-order but has pointer-events none. Outside groups, standard per-element focus-visible rings remain. States: no focus (ring hidden), focus enters group (ring fades in at target), focus moves (ring travels), focus leaves (ring fades out).
motion: When focus moves within a group, the ring animates position, width, height, and radius to the new target over 180ms cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1), fast enough that keyboard users never wait. Entering the group fades the ring in over 100ms at the target without travel. Leaving fades it out over 120ms.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. In any still where a control in the group has keyboard focus, the ring fully encloses that control with no part lagging over a neighbour; labels stay readable under the 3px offset.
mobile: At 375px touch input rarely shows focus-visible, so the ring appears only with a hardware keyboard; groups that wrap onto two rows still travel correctly because positions are measured or anchored each time.
a11y: Each control keeps a native fallback outline that is suppressed only when the shared ring is confirmed active. Reduced motion jumps the ring without travel. Ring colour meets 3:1 against adjacent colours as WCAG 2.2 focus appearance asks.
