avoid: Removing native outlines before the ring works, a ring that lags behind fast tabbing, rings clipped by overflow hidden parents, travel across the whole page between unrelated groups, or rings appearing on mouse clicks.

stack_notes.css: CSS anchor positioning: give the focused control anchor-name via :focus-visible, and position the ring with position-anchor and anchor() insets, with transitions on inset properties; fallback outlines under @supports not.
stack_notes.js: On focusin within the group, read getBoundingClientRect of the target relative to the group and animate the ring with WAAPI; reposition on resize via ResizeObserver; check matches(':focus-visible') to skip pointer focus.

name: Diagonal seam wipe
blueprint: Applied at the boundary between two contrasting sections, for example a light case study followed by a dark showreel. The incoming section overlaps the previous one by 40vh and is clipped by a polygon with a diagonal leading edge at 12 degrees. A thin accent rule 3px tall rides the diagonal edge, and a small label (Next: Showreel) travels on that rule in the section's mono face at clamp(0.75rem, 1vw, 0.9rem). States: before seam (incoming fully clipped), wiping (edge travels up), after seam (incoming fully revealed, rule fades).
motion: Over the 40vh overlap, 0-100% progress moves the diagonal edge from the bottom of the viewport to above the top, revealing the incoming section. The outgoing content scales down to 0.97 and dims 20% across the same range. The rule and label travel with the edge; the rule fades out over the last 10%.
still_check: At 50% of the seam, the diagonal splits the viewport with both sections' visible text legible on its own side and the label readable on the rule. At 25% the incoming wedge is small; at 75% it dominates.
mobile: At 375px the angle drops to 6 degrees and the overlap shortens to 25vh; the outgoing scale is skipped to avoid reflow, and the label shortens to the next section's name only.
a11y: Content order stays linear in the DOM; the overlap is purely visual through negative margin and clip. Reduced motion shows a hard horizontal seam. The label is aria-hidden as it repeats the next heading. No content is hidden while clipped once revealed.
avoid: Clipping text that should be readable at the seam, overlapping interactive elements that become unclickable, using it on every boundary, scroll velocity triggers, or a diagonal that crosses headlines at 50%.

stack_notes.css: clip-path polygon with a custom property for the edge offset animated on the incoming section's view() timeline with animation-range entry; outgoing section gets a matching scale animation on its exit range.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver with fine thresholds or rAF progress sets --edge on the incoming section; pointer-events none on the clipped part until revealed. Any existing scroll library can scrub the same variable.

name: Second-state image reveal
blueprint: Product, property, or dish images that have a meaningful second state: a garment on a model then flat, a room furnished then empty, a dish plated then sliced, a property by day then at dusk. Both images stack in one aspect-ratio frame (4 / 5). The second image reveals through a soft vertical blind of 6 slats that open one after another, not a crossfade. A small caption chip names the state (Worn, Flat lay). States: idle (first image), hover or focus (slats open to second), touch (tap toggles), loading (second image lazy-loaded on first hover intent).
motion: Hover opens six vertical slat masks in sequence from left to right, each scaling on the x axis from 0 to 1 over 260ms with a 35ms stagger, revealing the second image. The caption chip text swaps with a 120ms fade. Leaving closes slats right to left at the same speed.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. Idle shows the first image complete with chip; hovered still shows the second image complete with its chip; product name and price below the frame are always legible and never covered.
mobile: At 375px there is no hover; a small toggle chip on the image switches states on tap, and a swipe within the frame moves between the two images as a two-slide scroll-snap track.
a11y: Both images have alt text describing their state; the toggle is a button with aria-pressed. Reduced motion uses an instant swap. Hover-revealed information is also reachable by focus. The second state never carries the only copy of any detail.
avoid: Loading both images eagerly for every card, slats leaving gaps at fractional widths, hover-only state switches on touch, revealing a state that misleads such as staged furniture without saying so, or covering price text.

stack_notes.css: Second image with a mask-image built from six linear-gradient stops whose sizes transition per slat via custom properties and transition-delay; :hover and :focus-within on the card trigger; loading lazy on the second image.
stack_notes.js: On pointerenter intent, set the second image src from a data attribute so it loads only when needed; tap toggles a class on touch. WAAPI can animate slat masks if mask transitions are unsupported.

name: Cursor-tethered caption
blueprint: On a photo gallery or work index. Hovering an image shows a caption card tethered to the pointer by a thin 1px line, offset 2rem below-right: title, place and year, photographer credit, in a small label at clamp(0.75rem, 1vw, 0.9rem) on a solid chip. The card lags behind the pointer on a spring so the line stretches and relaxes. The card flips side when near a viewport edge. Static captions also exist under each image in the DOM. States: idle (no tether), hover (tether shown), moving (line stretches), edge (card flips), leave (card retracts to pointer and fades).
motion: While hovering, the card position lerps toward pointer plus offset at 0.18 per frame, so fast moves stretch the line up to about 8rem before it recovers. Line length and angle derive from card and pointer positions each frame. Enter fades the card in over 140ms; leave retracts it toward the pointer over 160ms.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. Any hover still shows a fully legible caption card not overlapping the hovered image's focal point, with the tether line visible. Without hover, images still show their DOM captions below.
mobile: At 375px there is no pointer tether; captions show under images as normal text, and tapping an image opens it in a lightbox with the caption pinned at the bottom.
a11y: The floating card is aria-hidden because the same caption is in the figcaption. Reduced motion places the card at a fixed offset without lag or line stretch. Keyboard focus on a figure shows its caption anchored to the image corner.
avoid: Captions that exist only in the floating card, cards covering the subject of the photo, rAF loops running when no gallery is hovered, cards clipped at screen edges, or the tether persisting after leaving.

stack_notes.css: CSS-only approximation: a caption chip positioned by anchor() to the hovered figure corner, revealed with :hover and :focus-within transitions; no tether line, but the same content and layering.
stack_notes.js: pointermove writes target coordinates; a single rAF loop runs only while a figure is hovered, lerps card position, and draws the tether as an SVG line or a rotated div. Loop stops on pointerleave and cleans up listeners on unmount.

name: Stitched progress thread
blueprint: A reading progress indicator for long articles or lessons: a 2px thread running down the left margin of the content column, positioned at 1.5rem from the text, drawn as a dashed stitch line. As the reader advances, the stitches fill solid from top. Each h2 in the article places a small knot (a 6px filled circle with a label of the section number) on the thread at its relative position. At the end, the thread ties off with a small bow mark beside the closing paragraph. States: unread (dashed), read (solid stitch), at knot (knot fills and its section number shows), complete (tie-off mark).
motion: Page scroll progress 0-100% through the article body maps to the thread fill height, linear with scroll. Knots fill as the fill reaches them, with a 140ms scale pop. At 100% the tie-off mark draws its two loops via stroke-dashoffset over 400ms once. No motion when idle.
still_check: At 50% of the article, the thread is solid to the midpoint knot with remaining stitches dashed, and article text is untouched. At 25% fewer knots are filled; at 75% most are filled with the tie-off still undrawn.
mobile: At 375px the margin is too narrow, so the thread becomes a horizontal stitch line 2px tall fixed at the top of the viewport under the header, with knots as small notches and no labels.
a11y: The thread is decorative and aria-hidden; the article keeps a regular table of contents. Reduced motion keeps the fill since it is position not animation, but removes pops and the tie-off draw. The thread never overlaps text.
avoid: Measuring the whole page instead of the article body, knot positions drifting as images load, thread overlapping pull quotes, a progress bar that also acts as a scrubber stealing drags, or duplicating the docs rail.

stack_notes.css: A fixed or sticky thread element with scale on the y axis animated on a named view-timeline on the article element; knots placed by their own view timelines; dashed stitches by repeating-linear-gradient.
stack_notes.js: Compute progress from the article's getBoundingClientRect in a passive scroll listener with rAF, position knots from h2 offsetTop relative to article height, and recompute with ResizeObserver after images load.

name: Disclosure with measured height
blueprint: A native details and summary pattern used for spec sheets, dosage notes, fee breakdowns, or code examples. Summary row 3rem tall with label at clamp(1rem, 1.4vw, 1.125rem) and a plus mark built from two bars, where the vertical bar rotates flat to form a minus. Content area animates its height from 0 to auto using interpolate-size, with a 1px top rule that draws across when open. Content padding block 1rem. States: closed, hover (summary background tint), opening, open, closing.
motion: Opening animates block-size from 0 to auto over 280ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) while content opacity goes from 0 to 1 starting 60ms in. The vertical bar of the plus rotates 90 degrees over the same duration. The top rule scales on the x axis from 0 to 1 over 220ms. Closing reverses in 220ms.
still_check: Not scroll-linked. Closed and open stills must both be complete: closed shows the summary label and plus mark; open shows all content with no clipped last line. Content is never shown half-height in a settled state.
mobile: At 375px summaries keep a 48px minimum tap height, the plus mark sits at the right edge with 1rem padding, and long content such as code blocks scroll horizontally inside the panel rather than widening the page.
a11y: Native details provides state and keyboard toggling; summary keeps a visible focus ring. Reduced motion opens instantly. Content inside is findable by in-page search because hidden until found is honoured by details. No ARIA overrides needed.
avoid: Fixed max-height hacks that clip content or delay closing, animating padding causing jitter, removing the default marker without a replacement, nesting interactive elements inside summary, or animating many panels open at once.

stack_notes.css: interpolate-size: allow-keywords on :root; transition on block-size and content-visibility with allow-discrete on the ::details-content pseudo-element; plus mark bars rotated via details[open] selectors, with no script and no fixed max-height values needed.
stack_notes.js: Fallback for engines without interpolate-size: on toggle, measure scrollHeight and run a WAAPI height animation from 0 to the measured value, then clear the inline height. Listeners removed on unmount.

name: Exploded Pipeline Stack
blueprint: Full-viewport hero, min-height 100svh, padding clamp(4rem, 9vw, 8rem) clamp(1rem, 5vw, 4rem). The tool's own pipeline is the object: 3-5 translucent planes stacked on one axis, one plane per real stage the product runs (input, each pass or check, output). Each plane carries a small DOM label at 0.875rem monospace (stage name plus what it changes) pinned to its edge by projected coordinates. The h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 8vw, 8rem) and a one-line deck sit on a plain text plate the planes never cross; the primary CTA (install or try) and a secondary docs link sit under the deck. A poster image of the assembled stack renders first. States: collapsed (planes touching, reads as one finished artefact), exploded (planes spread, stage labels readable), focused (one plane forward, its label expanded), replayed (Replay button resets to collapsed).
motion: Load: planes start collapsed and spread over 1100ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), each delayed 90ms after the one below. Pointer: the stack tilts up to 8deg toward the cursor with a damped spring. Scroll 0-50% of the hero range: the camera moves along the stack axis and each plane in turn comes forward and brightens while its label expands; 50-100%: the planes collapse back into the finished output plane and the CTA settles.
still_check: At 50% the headline and CTA are fully readable on their plate, at least three planes are separated with their labels legible, and one plane is clearly in front. 25% shows the first stage forward; 75% shows the stack partly collapsed toward the output.
mobile: At 375px the text plate sits above a 70vw-tall canvas, the stack shows 3 planes at most with labels below it as a numbered list, pointer tilt is off and the explode runs once on first view instead of scroll.
a11y: Stages exist as a real ordered list in the DOM; the canvas is aria-hidden. The Replay control is a real button. Reduced motion: the stack shows exploded and static with every label visible. Headline contrast is 4.5:1 or better against the plate, never against the canvas.
avoid: Stages that are not real steps of the product, labels that exist only inside the canvas, a blank canvas while WebGL starts (poster first), planes passing over the headline, pinning the hero longer than one viewport, generic glowing cubes standing in for the product.

stack_notes.css: No-WebGL path: the planes are absolutely positioned divs with transform-style: preserve-3d and translateZ per plane; animation-timeline: view() spreads them on scroll; a CSS transition handles the load spread. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: three.js PlaneGeometry per stage with MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission or a cheap alpha material; rAF reads hero progress from getBoundingClientRect. Project label anchors to screen for DOM labels. Pause off-screen, dispose geometries, materials, textures and the renderer on unmount. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Request Trace Scrub
blueprint: Section 300vh with a sticky 100vh stage inside max-width 80rem. The stage holds the product's real architecture as an SVG diagram (4-7 labelled nodes such as client, agent, server, rules, output, joined by paths at 2px) and under it a log panel 14rem tall in 0.875rem monospace. A single traced request (a dot plus a short payload chip) travels the paths. Section heading at clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem) and a one-line explanation sit above the stage. States: idle node at 50% ink, active node at full ink with its log lines appended, visited node keeps a small check, finished (whole path drawn, final output line highlighted).
motion: Scroll progress 0..1 maps to distance along the path: the dot moves with stroke-dashoffset drawing the path behind it; reaching a node lights it and appends that node's 2-3 log lines with a 120ms fade. 0-10% shows the diagram at rest, 10-90% runs the trace, 90-100% holds the finished path and output.
still_check: At 50% about half the path is drawn, the active node is obvious, and the log panel shows the earlier nodes' lines as readable text. 25% shows the first one or two nodes lit; 75% shows most of the path with only the output node left.
mobile: At 375px the diagram turns vertical (nodes stacked, paths straight down) without pinning; each node lights as it enters the viewport and its log lines appear beneath it.
a11y: Nodes and log lines are real DOM text in order (an ordered list of steps with their output); the moving dot is decorative and aria-hidden. Reduced motion shows the whole path drawn and every log line visible. Focus on a step scrolls the trace to it.
avoid: Invented nodes or log lines the product never prints, a diagram so small labels fall under 0.75rem, a dot that outruns the scroll, colour-only state, and log text that scrolls inside the panel faster than it can be read.

stack_notes.css: SVG path with stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset bound to animation-timeline: scroll() on the section; nodes and log groups use view() ranges. Sticky stage via position: sticky.
stack_notes.js: Read section progress in rAF, use SVGPathElement.getPointAtLength for the dot, toggle data-active on nodes at precomputed lengths. GSAP ScrollTrigger or a plain scroll listener both work; remove listeners and cancel rAF on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Benchmark Run Replay
blueprint: Section 250vh with a sticky stage inside max-width 76rem. One row per contender or per run (3-6 rows), each a horizontal track 3rem tall with its name at 1rem, a bar that grows, and its measured value in tabular-nums at 1.25rem. Beside the tracks a method card 18rem wide states what was measured, on what input, how many runs and the date, plus a link to the raw results. Heading at clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem). States: running (bars growing, values counting), settled (final values, best row marked with a text label not just colour), inspected (hovered or focused row shows its run details).
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% replays the runs: each bar grows to its real measured value in proportion to time, values count up with tabular-nums so width never jumps. 70-100% holds the settled result and fades in the method card's footnote. Rows start 80ms apart so the order of finish is readable.
still_check: At 50% every row shows a partly grown bar with a readable current value and the method card is visible; 25% shows short bars, 75% shows final values with the best row labelled. Values in any frame are real intermediate or final numbers, never placeholders.
mobile: At 375px rows stack full width with values under the names, the method card moves below the rows, and the replay runs once on view instead of scrubbing.
a11y: The data is a real table (caption, row headers, values with units) in the DOM; bars are visual only. Reduced motion shows final values at once. Best row is marked in text. Contrast of bar against track is 3:1 or better.
avoid: Numbers that were not measured, a missing method, axes that start above zero to exaggerate a gap, rivals named without their real results, and bars whose final width disagrees with the printed value.

stack_notes.css: Bar width via a registered @property --v animated with animation-timeline: view(); counter() with @property integers can show values without JS where supported.
stack_notes.js: Map scroll progress in rAF to each run's recorded timeline and set width plus textContent with Intl.NumberFormat; IntersectionObserver fallback runs it once. Cancel rAF and remove listeners on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Case Caption as the Headline
blueprint: Centred column, max 34ch, on a bond-paper ground. The h1 is set like a court caption: a small-caps line above ('In the matter of'), the firm's promise as the case name at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5.5rem), a hairline 'v.' rule, then the client's problem as the opposing party ('a contract that stopped being honoured'). Under the caption, inside the same centred block, a ruled docket box holds real facts: matter types, response time, the office address. Below, the primary action reads as the filing line: 'Book a first consultation' with a labelled date field. States: idle, field focused, date chosen.
motion: On load the caption rules draw outward from the centre over 500ms, then the two caption lines settle 6px upward with an 80ms stagger. The docket box fades in last. Nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the full caption, docket facts and the consultation action readable. 25%, 50% and 75% are identical after load; only the focus state of the date field changes.
mobile: At 375px the docket box is a full-width ruled list; the case name drops to clamp(2.25rem, 10vw, 3rem) and keeps max 14ch per line.
a11y: The caption is one h1 with the small-caps lines as spans; the docket box is a dl. Date field has a visible label and a native date input. Reduced motion shows everything settled. Hairlines meet 3:1 non-text contrast.
avoid: Scales, gavels or columns as art; Latin mottos; a caption that names a real case or party; navy-and-gold colouring; burying the consultation action below the fold.

stack_notes.css: Rules are border-top with transform: scaleX from 0 under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); caption lines use a one-time animation with animation-delay. Docket is a two-column grid of dt/dd.
stack_notes.js: Only the date field needs script: min date today, closed days from the firm's calendar, submit to the booking endpoint.

name: Exhibit Binder Tabs
blueprint: A pinned first screen holds a binder seen from above: a stack of 4 sheets with lettered exhibit tabs (A, B, C, D) down the right edge. Sheets are min(88vw, 760px) wide with 44px tabs. The h1 sits on the top sheet as the cover page at clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.5rem) ('Every matter, filed in order.'). Each tab names one stage of how the firm handles a matter: Intake, Strategy, Filing, Hearing. Scroll turns the sheets: each shows that stage's one true fact (who you speak to, how long it takes, what you sign) in a ruled exhibit layout. The last sheet carries 'Book a first consultation'.
motion: Scroll-scrubbed across 300vh: each sheet lifts from its tab edge and turns left over 25% of the range, revealing the next. Snap to whole sheets. The current sheet's tab stays highlighted. Unpin after the last sheet.
still_check: At 25%, 50% and 75% a complete sheet lies flat and readable with its tab highlighted; no sheet rests mid-turn because of snapping.
mobile: Below 900px wide or 620px tall: no pin. The 4 sheets stack vertically as ruled cards with their exhibit tab on the top edge.
a11y: Sheets are an ordered list; tabs are in-page links to each sheet. Reduced motion: no pin, the stacked layout. Tab colours always carry a letter, never colour alone.
avoid: Pinned area taller than the viewport, sheets resting half-turned, fake case numbers, tiny exhibit text, changing scroll speed.

stack_notes.css: Scroll-driven animation with view-timeline on a 300vh track and a position: sticky stage; rotateY on each sheet with transform-origin left.
stack_notes.js: GSAP ScrollTrigger pin with snap: 1 / (sheets - 1), inside gsap.matchMedia with the reduced-motion and size guards; kill on unmount. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Practice Areas as a Clause Index
blueprint: Practice areas set as numbered clauses of an agreement: '§ 1 Employment', '§ 2 Property', each a row with the clause number in mono, the area at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), a two-line plain-language description of who it is for, the fee basis (fixed, hourly, contingency) and the lead lawyer's name. Rows are separated by hairlines; sub-clauses (1.1, 1.2) list matter types as indented lines.
motion: Opening a clause expands its sub-clauses with a 200ms height transition; the clause number shifts to the accent colour. Nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every clause title, fee basis and lead name readable; open and closed states differ only in sub-clause visibility.
mobile: Clause number sits above the title; fee basis and lead name move to one line under the description.
a11y: Each clause is a details/summary so it works without JS; summary text includes the clause number. Visible focus ring on paper. Reduced motion: no height transition.
avoid: Icon cards for practice areas, jargon in descriptions, hiding fees, more than 8 top-level clauses.

stack_notes.css: details/summary with ::details-content transition where supported; CSS counters for clause numbers.
stack_notes.js: None needed; optional deep link opens the matching clause from the URL hash.

name: Matter Docket Timeline
blueprint: How a matter runs, set as a docket sheet: a ruled table at max 72rem wide, rows at least 56px tall, whose rows are entries in date order: 'Day 1 · First consultation', 'Week 1 · Engagement letter signed', 'Weeks 2–6 · Evidence and filings', 'Hearing'. Columns: entry number (mono), stage, what the client does, what the firm does, typical time. A seal-red rule marks the example current stage.
motion: Rows draw their bottom hairline left to right once as they enter view (300ms each, 60ms stagger). No scroll scrubbing.
still_check: Any screenshot shows complete rows with every column readable; before and after entry the content is identical, only the rules differ.
mobile: The table becomes a list of entries, each with the stage as heading and the two 'who does what' cells as labelled lines.
a11y: A real table with th scope=col; on mobile the list keeps the labels as text. Reduced motion: rules shown drawn.
avoid: Promising outcomes or durations the firm cannot stand behind, icon-step circles, carousels.

stack_notes.css: Rule draw via background-size with animation-timeline: view() under the reduced-motion guard; static fallback.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver adds a class once per row when scroll timelines are unsupported.

name: Engagement Letter Terms
blueprint: Proof as the firm's own engagement letter: one paper sheet at max 68ch with 3rem padding and a 14rem margin column with letterhead, then the real terms a client gets (who handles the matter, how fees are billed, response time, how to end the engagement), each a numbered paragraph. Margin notes in the accent colour gloss the plain meaning ('You can stop at any time'). A signature line and the bar admissions close the sheet. Client quotes, only if real and permitted, sit as margin notes, never as a carousel.
motion: Margin notes slide 8px in from the margin as their paragraph enters view, once. The sheet itself does not move.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the full letter text and every margin note readable; motion only shifts notes by 8px before entry.
mobile: Margin notes become indented callouts under their paragraph.
a11y: The letter is an article with an ordered list of terms; margin notes are aside elements linked by aria-describedby. Accent notes keep at least 4.5:1 contrast.
avoid: Invented testimonials, star ratings, award badges without the award, a script signature as the only name.

stack_notes.css: Grid with a margin column; notes use a one-time animation triggered by a view timeline or a class.
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver adds a class once per paragraph when scroll timelines are unsupported.

name: Bar Roll Register
blueprint: The team as a bar-roll register: a ruled list with each lawyer's name at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), admission year and jurisdiction in mono, practice areas, languages spoken and a direct line. A small square portrait sits in a fixed slot at the row's left, greyscale until hover or focus. Partners first, then associates, ordered by admission year.
motion: Hover or focus lifts the row background one step and restores the portrait's colour over 180ms. No scroll motion.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every name, admission, practice area and phone readable; hover changes only background and portrait colour.
mobile: Portrait sits left of the name; admission and practice areas wrap to two short lines; the direct line is a tel: link.
a11y: A list of articles with names as h3; portraits have alt text with the name; phone links have accessible names. The hover state also applies on :focus-within.
avoid: Arms-crossed stock portraits, contact details hidden behind hover, uneven portrait crops.

stack_notes.css: Grid rows with filter: grayscale(1) on the img and a transition on :hover and :focus-within.
stack_notes.js: None.

name: Floor Plan, You Are Here
blueprint: The first screen is the museum's own floor plan at min(92vw, 1200px), drawn as flat coloured rooms with real gallery names. A 'You are here' pin sits at the entrance; the h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) is printed inside the largest room like a wall sign ('Touch everything in Gallery 2.'). Each room shows today's hands-on station as a small label; the open hours and 'Buy tickets' sit in the ticket-desk room by the entrance. Rooms are links to their gallery section.
motion: On load the pin drops 12px and settles; hovering or focusing a room lifts it 4px and shows its station label at full strength. Nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every room name, the headline, the hours and the ticket action readable; hover only lifts one room by 4px.
mobile: At 375px the plan becomes a vertical strip of rooms in walking order with the entrance and ticket desk first; the headline sits above the strip at clamp(2.25rem, 10vw, 3rem).
a11y: The plan is a nav with a list of room links; the pin is decorative (aria-hidden). Room colours carry a text name, never colour alone; text on rooms meets 4.5:1. Reduced motion: no pin drop.
avoid: A generic stock floor plan, invented rooms, tiny room labels, hiding the hours and tickets behind the map, a mascot pointing at the pin.

stack_notes.css: CSS grid areas for the rooms; one-time keyframe for the pin under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; :hover and :focus-visible lift with transform.
stack_notes.js: None needed; optional: highlight the room whose station is running now from the day's programme.

name: Pull-Out Specimen Drawer
blueprint: A shallow wooden specimen drawer fills the first screen at min(90vw, 1100px), half pulled out. The headline at clamp(2.75rem, 7vw, 6rem) wraps around one real object from the collection lying in the drawer (a fossil, a gear, a shell) shot from above. A card label beside it gives the object's name and 'Find it in Gallery 3'. Dragging or pressing the drawer handle pulls it fully open to show 3 more objects, each with a label and a 'try it' station number. 'Plan your visit' sits under the drawer.
motion: Drag or press the handle: the drawer slides out up to 240px with a short ease-out and objects settle 4px. Keyboard: Enter on the handle toggles open and closed.
still_check: Closed and open states both show the headline, the first object label and 'Plan your visit' readable; the open state only adds 3 labelled objects.
mobile: At 375px the drawer is shown fully open as a 2-column grid of objects with labels; no drag.
a11y: The handle is a button with aria-expanded; objects are figures with figcaption labels; photos have alt text naming the object. Reduced motion: toggle without slide.
avoid: Clip-art fossils, dinosaur cartoons standing in for the real collection, drag as the only way to see objects, headline covered by the drawer.

stack_notes.css: Drawer translateY driven by a CSS variable; text wrap via shape-outside on the hero object; transition under the reduced-motion guard.
stack_notes.js: Pointer events set the drawer offset with a clamp and snap to open or closed on release; remove listeners on unmount.

name: Today at the Museum
blueprint: Today's programme as one horizontal day rail at max 72rem: hours from opening to closing across the top, each demo, workshop or show a coloured block at its real time with its room, age band ('4–7', '8+') and whether it needs booking. A vertical 'now' line marks the current time. Under the rail, the next 3 starting events repeat as large cards at clamp(1.25rem, 2.5vw, 1.75rem) so families can decide fast.
motion: The 'now' line moves once a minute; blocks that have ended fade to the muted colour. No scroll motion.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every block's title, time, room and age band readable; only the 'now' line position and ended-block colour change over time.
mobile: Below 700px the rail becomes a vertical list in time order with the next event pinned first.
a11y: The rail is an ordered list with times as time elements; age bands are text. The 'now' line is aria-hidden with the current time stated in text. Reduced motion: line jumps, no animation.
avoid: Invented events, a carousel of today's events, age bands shown only as colours, hiding which events need booking.

stack_notes.css: Grid columns per 15 minutes with grid-column spans; ended blocks get a class from the server or script.
stack_notes.js: A one-minute interval updates the 'now' line and ended state; clear it on unmount.

name: Wristband Tickets
blueprint: Ticket types set as coloured paper wristbands laid flat, each a long band at min(100%, 44rem) with the ticket name, age band, price in tabular figures at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem) and what it includes (galleries, planetarium show, workshop). A family-bundle band shows the real saving in money, not percent. A counter beside each band (−/+) builds the order and a running total sits in the last band with 'Book tickets'.
motion: Changing a count bumps the total figure 4px and back over 160ms. No scroll motion.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every ticket name, age band, price, inclusion and the total readable; counters change numbers only.
mobile: Bands stack full width; counters move under the price; the total band sticks to the bottom of the section while it is in view.
a11y: Each band is a fieldset with a legend; counters are labelled buttons around a number input; the total is aria-live polite. Reduced motion: no bump.
avoid: Fake 'limited tickets' urgency, hidden booking fees, prices only in a PDF, wristband colours as the only difference between tickets.

stack_notes.css: Bands are flex rows with a notched end via clip-path; tabular-nums for prices.
stack_notes.js: Counters update the total; submit goes to the real ticketing endpoint.

name: Exhibit Wall Labels
blueprint: Exhibits shown as museum wall labels: each card is a white label at least 18rem wide with the exhibit title at clamp(1.25rem, 2.5vw, 1.75rem), a one-line 'what you can do here' ('Build a bridge that holds you'), the age band, the gallery room and a 'hands-on' or 'look only' mark, next to one real photo of a child at the exhibit. A filter row above sorts by age band and by gallery.
motion: Filtering re-flows the labels with a short 180ms fade; nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every visible label's title, age band and room readable; filtering only changes which labels show.
mobile: Labels become a single column with the photo above the text.
a11y: Filters are a radio group per facet with visible labels; the result count is aria-live. Photos have alt text. Reduced motion: no fade.
avoid: Stock photos of children unrelated to the museum, cartoon icons instead of the exhibits, unlabelled age colours, a slideshow of exhibits.

stack_notes.css: CSS grid with auto-fill minmax(18rem, 1fr); :has() filtering where supported.
stack_notes.js: Small script filters by data attributes when :has() is unsupported and announces the count.

name: Operations Wall Board
blueprint: The first screen is the wall-mounted board the team would actually keep open, edge to edge: 4 to 6 live tiles in a 12-column grid at full viewport width, each tile one real number for this business today (orders due, items short, late deliveries) at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) with its unit and the time it last changed. The h1 at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.5rem) is the board's title bar ('Tuesday, 6:40 am — 3 orders need you'). One tile is flagged in the accent colour with its action ('Reassign driver'). The sign-up or 'Open the board' action sits in the title bar.
motion: When a value updates, the tile's number rolls to the new value over 300ms and its 'changed' time refreshes. No scroll motion.
still_check: Any screenshot shows every tile's label, value, unit and the flagged action readable; updates only change numbers.
mobile: At 375px tiles stack in priority order with the flagged tile first; numbers drop to clamp(2rem, 9vw, 2.75rem).
a11y: Tiles are a list of articles with headings; values are text, not canvas; the flagged state has a text label too. Updates use aria-live polite on the title bar only. Reduced motion: numbers swap without rolling.
avoid: Four generic KPI cards over a line chart, made-up growth percentages, sparklines in every tile, neon glow.

stack_notes.css: CSS grid with grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr); tabular-nums; the roll is a translateY on a digit column under the reduced-motion guard.
stack_notes.js: Optional polling or SSE updates values; clear timers on unmount.

name: Scrub the Day
blueprint: A pinned first screen holds one horizontal timeline of the business's day at min(94vw, 1280px): opening to closing across, with real events as blocks (batches, deliveries, shifts). The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem) sits above it ('See your whole day before it starts'). Scrolling moves a playhead across the day; the panel under the timeline shows what the product shows at that moment: the queue, the stock level, who is on shift. 4 snap points: open, morning rush, midday, close.
motion: Scroll-scrubbed across 260vh: the playhead moves left to right and the panel crossfades between 4 states, snapped to whole states. Unpin after close.
still_check: At 25%, 50% and 75% the playhead rests on a snap point and the panel shows one complete readable state.
mobile: Below 900px wide or 620px tall: no pin; the 4 states show as a vertical list of time-stamped panels.
a11y: States are an ordered list with time headings; the timeline is decorative for screen readers with each state's time in text. Reduced motion: no pin, the stacked list.
avoid: A playhead resting between states, fake activity data, more than 5 states, scroll-jacked speed.

stack_notes.css: position: sticky stage on a 260vh track; scroll-driven animation (view-timeline) for the playhead with a static fallback.
stack_notes.js: GSAP ScrollTrigger pin with snap: 1 / 3 inside gsap.matchMedia with reduced-motion and size guards; kill on unmount. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Command Bar First
blueprint: A centred column at max 46rem: the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem) states the job ('Ask your shop anything'), and right under it a real command bar at 56px tall, focused on load, with 3 example commands from this business as chips ('Reorder rye flour', 'Who is on Saturday?', 'Late orders'). Choosing a chip shows its result card below the bar from sample data (the bar itself is a real search form): a small table or one action button. 'Start free' sits under the result.
motion: Choosing a chip fades its result card up 8px over 200ms. Nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the headline, command bar, chips and either the empty prompt or one complete result readable.
mobile: At 375px chips wrap to two lines; the result card is full width; the bar stays 56px tall.
a11y: The bar is a labelled search input in a form; chips are a radio group with visible labels; the result region is aria-live polite. Reduced motion: the result appears without the fade.
avoid: A fake terminal, an AI sparkle icon as the only idea, results that do not match the command, autofocus that steals focus on later pages.

stack_notes.css: Chips are radio inputs; :has(#chip-n:checked) shows the matching pre-rendered result card. Centred grid, max-width in rem, visible focus rings.
stack_notes.js: Optional: submit the bar to the product's real search; the chip results need no script.

name: Question of the Day
blueprint: A centred column at max 40rem: the h1 is one real question the museum answers inside, at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) ('How heavy is a blue whale's heart?'). Under it, a large answer card that flips open on press to give the answer in one line and where to see it ('As heavy as a piano. See it life-size in Gallery 4.'). Below the card: today's hours, the next free entry slot and 'Plan your visit'. A small 'another question' link swaps to the next of 5 real questions.
motion: Pressing the card rotates it 180deg on Y over 400ms to the answer side. Nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the question, the card (either side complete), the hours and the visit action readable.
mobile: At 375px the question drops to clamp(2rem, 9vw, 2.75rem) and keeps max 16ch per line; the card stays full width.
a11y: The card is a button with aria-expanded controlling the answer, which is in the DOM as text. Reduced motion: answer replaces the question without rotation.
avoid: Trivia that is not in the collection, cartoon mascots, the answer hidden from screen readers, quiz scores or timers.

stack_notes.css: transform-style: preserve-3d with backface-visibility on both faces under the reduced-motion guard. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.
stack_notes.js: Toggles aria-expanded and rotates the next question from a short list; no network.

name: Pick Your Age, Get Your Path
blueprint: A stacked first screen: the h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 7vw, 6rem) across the full measure ('Bring them. We know where to start.'), then a full-width row of age bands as large tabs (Under 4, 4–7, 8–11, 12+). Choosing a band fills the band below with that age's path through the museum: 3 numbered stops with room names, a photo of the exhibit and how long it takes, ending in 'Book a time slot'. One band is open by default from the most visited age.
motion: Switching bands slides the path 12px and fades it over 220ms. Nothing moves on scroll.
still_check: Any screenshot shows the headline, all age tabs and one complete 3-stop path readable.
mobile: At 375px tabs become a 2x2 grid; the path stops stack vertically with photos above text.
a11y: Tabs follow the ARIA tabs pattern with arrow-key support; each path is a tabpanel with an ordered list. Reduced motion: no slide.
avoid: Generic 'fun for all ages' copy, stock photos, age bands only as colours, paths that list exhibits not in the museum.

stack_notes.css: Tabs as a grid of buttons; panels toggled with the hidden attribute; transition under the reduced-motion guard.
stack_notes.js: Small tabs script with roving tabindex; remember the last band in the URL hash.

name: Weight-axis poster headline
blueprint: Poster hero, min-height 100svh, padding clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 3rem). One h1 of 2 to 4 words naming what the business does with its own noun (Boilers fixed tonight, Ink that heals clean, Water you can trust), set in a variable font at clamp(4rem, 16vw, 15rem), line-height 0.86, tracking -0.03em, flush left and allowed to run to the right edge. The font's wght axis sits on a registered custom property --w. A thin rule runs under the last line; below it a 3-column fact row at 0.9375rem: where, when open, how to reach (phone as a tel: link). One primary action sits at the right end of the fact row, 3rem tall. Corners: square everywhere (radius 0) so the heavy type carries the shape; the action is a 2px-ruled rectangle. h1 uses text-wrap: balance; the fact row uses text-wrap: pretty.
motion: Scroll progress 0-60% of the hero's exit drives --w from 300 to 900 so the words thicken as the visitor commits; letter widths stay inside the measured line because the font's wdth axis compensates from 100 to 88. 60-100%: the fact row slides up 2rem and the rule extends from 40% to 100% width. On load nothing animates: the headline renders at weight 300.
still_check: At 50% the headline is mid-weight (around 600), every word on its line, the rule two-thirds across and the fact row fully readable. 25% looks visibly lighter, 75% visibly heavier.
mobile: At 375px the h1 drops to clamp(3rem, 15vw, 4.5rem) on 3 to 4 lines; the weight scrub keeps running but over a shorter range (0-40%). Fact row stacks into 3 rows with 44px tap targets.
a11y: The h1 is plain text, never an image. Reduced motion: weight fixed at 700, rule full width, no slide. Fact links keep a 3px focus-visible outline in the ink colour.
avoid: A font without a wght axis (fakes bold and jumps), lines that rewrap mid-scrub (lock wdth compensation), weight tied to scroll speed, or a headline about the brand instead of the trade's own noun.

stack_notes.css: @property --w registered as number; h1 uses font-variation-settings driven by --w; animation-timeline: view() with animation-range exit 0% exit 60% on the hero. Where unsupported the h1 simply renders at weight 700. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.
stack_notes.js: Optional rAF reader of hero progress writing --w for engines without scroll timelines; one passive scroll listener, removed on unmount.

name: Ruled ledger poster
blueprint: Poster on a paper ground, max width 80rem, padding clamp(2rem, 6vw, 5rem). The page is ruled with 1px horizontal lines every 2rem (a repeating-linear-gradient), and every text line sits exactly on a rule: h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 7vw, 6rem) spans 2 rule pairs per line. A narrow right margin column, 14rem wide and separated by a red 1px margin line, holds facts in ledger form with right-aligned tabular figures: established year, licence or registration number, hours, phone. Under the h1 one sentence at 1.25rem names who it is for. One text link action, underlined 2px, sits on the last rule. Corners: radius 0, a ledger has no rounded edges. h1 uses text-wrap: balance so no single word hangs on the last rule.
motion: Entering view only: the rules draw in from left to right over 600ms, one 30ms after another, then stop. The margin line draws top to bottom over 400ms. No scroll-linked motion afterwards; links underline-grow on hover in 160ms.
still_check: Any still shows every rule, the headline sitting on its baselines, and all four ledger facts readable in the margin column. The composition is complete with no motion at all.
mobile: At 375px the margin column moves below the headline as a 2-column fact list (label, value), the rules tighten to 1.75rem, h1 to clamp(2.25rem, 10vw, 3rem).
a11y: Ruled lines are a background, never text decoration that confuses readers. Ledger facts are a dl. Reduced motion: rules and margin line render complete at once. Focus ring 3px offset 3px.
avoid: Text drifting off the baseline grid (set line-height in multiples of 2rem), fake registration numbers, more than 4 margin facts, or ruling so dark it competes with the words.

stack_notes.css: Rules via background-image repeating-linear-gradient sized 100% 2rem; draw-in via a pseudo-element with scaleX keyed to animation-timeline: view() entry range; margin line likewise on scaleY. RTL: rules draw from the inline-start edge (transform-origin: inline-start equivalent via logical left/right swap under :dir(rtl)); the margin column sits at inline-end with border-inline-start.
stack_notes.js: None required. Optionally compute the rule rhythm from the loaded font metrics with document.fonts.ready and set --rule so baselines align exactly.

name: Zoom through the letter
blueprint: Pinned poster, 220vh tall section with a 100svh sticky stage. One giant glyph, the first letter of the business or its key noun, set at clamp(28rem, 90vw, 70rem) and cropped by all four viewport edges. The glyph is filled with a photograph of the trade's real object (a coiled hose, an inked forearm, a vineyard row) via background-clip text. The full h1 sits in DOM at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) bottom-left on a solid ink band, always readable. The next section's opening image waits behind, framed by the glyph's counter (the hole in an O, D, A or P). Corners: the h1 band is square (radius 0); nothing else has corners. The h1 uses text-wrap: balance.
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% scales the glyph from 1 to 18 with transform-origin set on the centre of its counter, so the camera flies through the hole into the photograph behind; 70-100% the glyph has left the frame and the next image is full bleed. The h1 band stays fixed until 60% then slides down and out over 15%.
still_check: At 50% the glyph is about 8x, its counter filling most of the frame with the next image clearly visible through it, and the h1 band still fully readable. 25% shows the whole glyph cropped large; 75% shows almost only the next image.
mobile: At 375px the pinned range shortens to 150vh, the glyph picks a letter with a wide counter, and the photo fill swaps to a solid brand colour if the image is under 50KB budget. h1 band grows to two lines.
a11y: The giant glyph is aria-hidden; the h1 is real text and is never scaled. Reduced motion: no pin and no zoom; the glyph renders once at 1x beside the h1 and the section scrolls normally.
avoid: Choosing a glyph with no counter (I, L, T), transform-origin off-centre so the fly-through misses the hole, pinning beyond 2.2 viewports, or the h1 placed on the photo fill where contrast varies.

stack_notes.css: Sticky stage plus animation-timeline: view() on the glyph's scale; transform-origin set from a custom property. Without scroll timelines the glyph stays at 1x and the section is not pinned. RTL: the h1 band anchors to inset-inline-start and slides on the block axis, so it needs no mirroring.
stack_notes.js: Measure the counter's centre with a hidden SVG of the glyph (getBBox) and write it to --ox/--oy; rAF maps progress to scale. Disconnect observers on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: grow type with font-size or CSS zoom, not transform: scale, so glyphs stay sharp at the large end.

name: Stamped numeral poster
blueprint: Poster whose hero is one meaningful number from the brief (the year founded, minutes to reach a call-out, the date of the next open day, litres treated per day): numerals at clamp(9rem, 32vw, 26rem) with tabular lining figures, weight 300, in a muted ink, set top-left. Over its lower third, the h1 at clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 3.75rem) explains the number in a sentence on a solid ground strip. A small caption at 0.875rem below the number states its source and date. Right column, 18rem: 2 actions as text links with arrows. Corners: square strip, radius 0; text-link actions have no box. The explaining h1 uses text-wrap: balance.
motion: Entering view: the numeral settles from letter-spacing 0.08em to 0 and opacity 0.6 to 1 over 700ms; the h1 strip draws its ground from left in 400ms after. No scroll scrubbing; the number never counts up.
still_check: Any still shows the number, its sentence and its source caption complete, with the strip fully behind the h1.
mobile: At 375px the numeral becomes clamp(6rem, 38vw, 9rem) on its own row, the h1 strip sits under it full width, actions stack as 48px rows.
a11y: The number is part of the reading order before the sentence that explains it; give the numeral an aria-describedby to the caption. Reduced motion: final spacing, no draw. Strip text 4.5:1 minimum.
avoid: A vanity number with no source, numbers that count up from zero (reads as a gimmick and lies mid-count), or a numeral so pale it fails 3:1 as large text.

stack_notes.css: font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums; settle via @starting-style or view() entry keyed animation; strip via a scaleX pseudo-element. RTL: the strip ground draws from inline-start (scaleX with transform-origin flipped under :dir(rtl)); the numeral stays left-to-right as digits always are. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.
stack_notes.js: None. Content teams can swap the number from CMS; no script needed.

name: Tear-off tabs flyer
blueprint: Hero styled as a notice pinned to a cork or plaster wall: a paper sheet max width 44rem, rotated -1.5deg, with a pin or tape at top. Sheet holds the h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 5.5rem) in a condensed grotesk, a 2-line pitch, and one photo of the trade's object at 4:3. Along the bottom edge, 5 to 7 vertical tear-off tabs 3.25rem wide by 9rem tall, separated by dashed cut lines, each printing one way to act sideways (Call 0161 555 0100, Book online, Prices, Find us, WhatsApp). Each tab is a real link. Corners: paper sheet radius 2px, tabs square with dashed cut lines; never round chips. h1 and pitch use text-wrap: balance and pretty.
motion: Load: the sheet drops 1.5rem and settles to its rotation over 500ms with a slight overshoot. Hover or focus on a tab lifts it 6px and rotates it 4deg from the top, as if half torn. Activating a tab plays a 250ms tear (the tab detaches and falls 2rem fading) before navigation; back navigation restores it. Scroll 0-100%: the sheet parallaxes 4vh slower than the page.
still_check: At 50% of the hero scroll the sheet is complete with every tab attached and legible; the parallax offset is small enough that nothing is cut off.
mobile: At 375px the sheet loses its rotation, tabs become a horizontal scroll-snap row of 6.5rem by 3rem chips under the sheet, each still a link, and the tear animation is skipped.
a11y: Tabs are links with full text, not rotated images; rotated text has aria-label equal to its visible string. Reduced motion: no drop, lift or tear; tabs get a colour change on focus. Focus rings drawn outside the rotated box.
avoid: Tabs so narrow the vertical text is unreadable, tearing that delays navigation over 300ms, fake handwritten phone numbers that cannot be tapped, or cork textures that crush contrast.

stack_notes.css: writing-mode: vertical-rl for tab text; transforms on :hover and :focus-visible; tear via a class-free :active transition; parallax via animation-timeline: scroll() on the sheet. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: Intercept tab clicks to run a 250ms WAAPI tear then navigate; respect modifier-clicks and middle-clicks by not intercepting them.

name: Split-flap departure board
blueprint: Poster hero on a near-black ground. A split-flap board of 3 rows by 14 to 18 cells, each cell 3.25rem by 4.5rem (scales to clamp(1.75rem, 5vw, 3.25rem) wide), shows the h1 as a sentence whose last word cycles through the trade's real nouns (We fix LEAKS / FUSE BOARDS / BOILERS; Now pouring PINOT / RIESLING). The DOM h1 holds the full sentence with all nouns listed in visually hidden text. Beneath the board, a status row in monospace 0.9375rem names the live or next item (next open slot, today's pour, next departure) and one action button. Corners: each flap cell has a 3px radius like real hardware; the action is a square-cornered 3rem button. The DOM h1 uses text-wrap: balance.
motion: On load the board flips from blanks into the first word, each cell running 4 to 9 character flips of 60ms with a 25ms stagger left to right. Every 4s the cycling row flips to the next noun; scroll progress 30-80% of the hero adds one extra flip per noun so scrolling never shows a half word at rest. Each flip is a two-half rotateX of 60ms with a darker shadow on the falling half.
still_check: At 50% every cell shows a complete character, the sentence reads cleanly, and the status row is readable. A screenshot never catches more than one row mid-flip.
mobile: At 375px the board shrinks to 2 rows of 10 cells, nouns are capped at 10 characters, and cycling slows to 6s. The status row wraps under the board.
a11y: Board cells are aria-hidden; the h1 reads the full sentence once. Cycling pauses on hover, focus and when the tab is hidden, with a visible pause control. Reduced motion: no flips; the board shows the first noun statically and the others are listed below.
avoid: Cycling faster than 3s, flipping every cell on every change (only changed cells flip), noun lists longer than 6, or a fake departures look for a business that has no schedule to show.

stack_notes.css: Cells are inline-grid with two half spans; the flip uses rotateX keyframes and backface-visibility hidden. A pure CSS version can cycle via @keyframes steps for one noun list. RTL: cells stagger from inline-start; for Arabic or Hebrew nouns use a font with the script and run the stagger from the right; the board grid uses direction from the document.
stack_notes.js: A small controller diffs old and new strings and only animates changed cells, schedules flips with setTimeout tied to document.visibilityState, and clears timers on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.

name: Debossed paper under moving light
blueprint: Poster on an uncoated paper ground (a subtle grain image under 30KB). The h1 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 8rem) is set as if debossed: same colour as the paper with an inner dark top-left shadow and a light bottom-right highlight, plus a solid ink duplicate exposed for contrast (see a11y). Above the h1, a small blind-embossed mark of the business; below, one line of copy at 1.125rem in ink and a single outlined action. Generous margins: the content block is max 52rem and sits on the lower-left third. Corners: the outlined action has a 2px radius, the emblem is circular because it is a seal. h1 uses text-wrap: balance.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% of the hero moves an imaginary light from upper-left to upper-right: text-shadow offsets travel from (-2px,-2px) to (2px,-2px) and the highlight swaps side, linear with scroll. On view entry the ink layer fades from 0 to its final opacity over 500ms.
still_check: At 50% the light is overhead: shadows short and even, the h1 clearly legible through its ink layer, copy and action fully readable.
mobile: At 375px the h1 is clamp(2.4rem, 11vw, 3.25rem); the light motion is kept but range halves. The emblem drops to 2.5rem.
a11y: Deboss alone fails contrast, so the h1 always carries an ink fill at 4.5:1 with the deboss as an extra effect. Reduced motion: light fixed overhead. Focus ring is solid ink, 2px, offset 4px.
avoid: Same-colour text with no ink fill (unreadable), heavy grain that makes the page look dirty, shadows above 3px that turn the effect into a cheap bevel, or applying deboss to body copy.

stack_notes.css: Registered @property --lx for the shadow offset, animated on animation-timeline: view(); text-shadow composed from var(--lx). Grain as a background-image with background-blend-mode multiply. RTL: the light travels from inline-start to inline-end, so mirror --lx sign under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: Not needed. Optionally tie --lx to device orientation on phones behind a permission-free sensor check, removed on unmount.

name: Headline that is the menu
blueprint: Poster hero where the h1 doubles as the site's navigation: a sentence at clamp(2.5rem, 7.5vw, 6.5rem) such as We plan the service, care for your person and stay with you after, in which 3 to 4 nouns are links to their sections (plan, care, after). Linked nouns carry a 0.08em underline in the accent colour and a superscript section number at 0.35em. No separate nav row in the hero; a small top bar holds only the logo and phone. Below, a 2-column row: one paragraph at 1.125rem and the primary action. Corners: radius 0 on the preview frame; links are bare words. The sentence uses text-wrap: balance so link nouns never strand alone.
motion: Scroll progress through the whole page drives a fill on each linked noun: the underline thickens from 0.08em to 0.5em as its section approaches and reads as a highlight while the section is on screen (scroll-driven, anchored to each section's view timeline via timeline-scope). Hovering a noun previews its section's opening image in a 16rem fixed frame bottom-right, crossfading in 180ms.
still_check: At hero 50% the sentence is complete, underlines on all link nouns are visible, and the preview frame is empty or showing a complete image. The sentence never reflows when underlines thicken.
mobile: At 375px the sentence drops to clamp(2rem, 9vw, 2.75rem); hover previews are dropped; underline fills still track sections. A compact menu button appears in the top bar for the rest of the nav.
a11y: The h1 remains a single heading containing links; linked words must make sense out of context (aria-describedby on the number). Reduced motion: underlines stay thin; active section shown by bold weight. Visible focus on each link.
avoid: More than 4 links in one heading, links whose text is meaningless alone, underline fills that change line height, or hiding the real navigation entirely for sections not in the sentence.

stack_notes.css: timeline-scope on body names each section's view timeline; link pseudo-elements animate background-size against it. Preview frame uses :has(a:hover) on the hero. RTL: the preview frame sits at inset-inline-end and underline fills grow from inline-start via background-position-x set per :dir().
stack_notes.js: IntersectionObserver fallback sets an is-active attribute on the matching link; preview images are preloaded on idle. Observers disconnected on unmount.

name: Ink diffusing under the type
blueprint: Full-viewport poster with the h1 at clamp(3.5rem, 11vw, 10rem) in DOM, ink-coloured on a paper ground. Behind the type, a WebGL fluid simulation seeded from the letterforms: at load the letter shapes are rendered to a mask texture and pigment in the brand's spot colour (or the trade's material colour: tattoo black, red wine, slate blue water) blooms outward from beneath each letter like ink into wet paper. A 40rem column of copy and the action sit below the h1 on solid paper, outside the simulation area. Corners: radius 0, the paper edge is the frame; the action is a square 3rem button with a 1.5px ink border. h1 uses text-wrap: balance.
motion: Load: pigment diffuses from the letter mask for 2.5s and then freezes as a stain. Scroll progress 0-100% advects the stain slowly downward and dilutes it to 40% so the next section starts clean. Pointer movement over the stage adds a small amount of clear water that pushes pigment (capped force); the effect sleeps after 4s idle.
still_check: At 50% the stain is mid-dilution, settled behind the letters, never covering the copy column; the h1 reads at full contrast because it sits on top as DOM.
mobile: At 375px the simulation runs at quarter resolution or falls back to a pre-rendered stain PNG under 80KB when WebGL2 is absent; pointer interaction is off.
a11y: Canvas aria-hidden. Reduced motion: show the frozen final stain image, no simulation. The h1 colour is chosen to keep 4.5:1 against the darkest pigment it overlaps.
avoid: Pigment drifting over body copy, simulations that never sleep and drain battery, colour pools so dark the ink h1 vanishes, or a generic rainbow fluid that has nothing to do with the trade's material.

stack_notes.css: Fallback poster: a static PNG stain behind the h1 with mask-image fade. Sizes reserved so the canvas swap causes no layout shift.
stack_notes.js: WebGL2 stable-fluids at 256x256 sim resolution, letter mask from a 2D canvas fillText of the h1; stop rAF when off-screen or idle; dispose framebuffers and textures on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Iris aperture opening
blueprint: Pinned centred hero: 200vh section, 100svh sticky stage on an ink ground. Centre stage: a circular clip-path window starting at 14vmin radius shows a photograph of the trade's real place or object (the chapel, the taproom, the workshop bench). The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits centred above the window on the ink ground, with a one-line deck under the window. Corners: none, the circle is the only shape; the action is a square 3rem button with 2px radius anchored at the stage's block-end.
motion: Scroll progress 0-75% grows the clip circle from 14vmin to 150vmax, so the photograph floods the stage; the h1 moves up 20vh and stays on its own ink band. 75-100%: the photo's scale eases from 1.15 to 1 and the deck fades in over the bottom band.
still_check: At 50% the circle fills roughly half the stage with the photo clearly recognisable, the h1 fully on ink above it and never over the photo.
mobile: At 375px the pin shortens to 140vh, the circle starts at 24vmin, and the photo uses a portrait crop chosen for the subject.
a11y: Photo has descriptive alt. Reduced motion: no pin; the photo shows full frame under the h1. Focus ring 3px light on ink.
avoid: A circle that opens onto a generic stock image, the h1 placed over the expanding photo, a pin longer than 2 viewports, or opening tied to scroll velocity.

stack_notes.css: clip-path: circle(var(--r) at 50% 55%) with --r registered and animated on a view() timeline over the sticky stage. Without scroll timelines the circle renders fully open.
stack_notes.js: Optional rAF progress mapper for older engines; one passive listener removed on unmount.

name: Centred page with marginalia
blueprint: Centred hero laid out like a book page: a central 36rem text block holding the h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 5.5vw, 4.5rem) in a serif with text-wrap: balance, and a 3-sentence paragraph with text-wrap: pretty. In the margins on both sides, 3 to 4 marginal notes at 0.875rem italic, each tied to a word in the paragraph by a 1px hairline: a price, an hour, a name, a small detail about the trade's object (the oak is local, the kiln runs Thursdays). Notes sit in a 12rem column each side. Corners: radius 0 everywhere; the action is a text link with a 1.5px underline.
motion: Entering view: hairlines draw from the anchor word out to the note over 450ms, staggered 120ms, then notes fade in. No scroll scrubbing after that; hovering an anchor word thickens its hairline and tints its note.
still_check: Any still shows the full text block, all notes and all hairlines complete.
mobile: At 375px notes move inline as footnote-style numbered asides under the paragraph, each with a superscript link back; hairlines are dropped.
a11y: Notes are aside elements linked by aria-describedby from their anchor spans. Reduced motion: hairlines and notes show complete. Focus visible on the action link.
avoid: More than 4 notes, notes that repeat the paragraph, hairlines crossing text, or decorative script fonts in the margins.

stack_notes.css: Hairlines as absolutely positioned SVG lines; draw-in via stroke-dashoffset on animation-timeline: view(). Margins via a 3-column grid 12rem 36rem 12rem. RTL: the grid uses logical columns, so notes mirror automatically; hairline SVGs are flipped with scale(-1, 1) under :dir(rtl). Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: Compute hairline endpoints from getBoundingClientRect of anchor spans and notes after fonts load; recompute on ResizeObserver; disconnect on unmount.

name: Open-now status line
blueprint: Centred hero, min-height 80svh, max width 46rem. Above the h1 a single status line at 1rem in tabular figures that says what is true right now: Open now until 18:00, On call tonight, Next tour 14:30, Supply normal in all areas. A small analogue dial 2.5rem wide sits before it with its hand at the real local time. h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance; one sentence below with text-wrap: pretty; two actions side by side, the first being the thing the status implies (Call now when on call, Book when open). Corners: actions square with 2px radius.
motion: The dial hand moves once a minute with a 300ms ease; the status line crossfades in 200ms when the state changes (open to closing soon). Entering view the status line underline draws in 300ms. Nothing scroll-linked.
still_check: Any still shows a complete true status, the dial, the h1 and both actions.
mobile: At 375px the status line sits as a full-width band above the h1 with the dial at its start; actions stack as 48px rows.
a11y: Status is plain text in a polite live region; colour is never the only signal (words always say open or closed). Reduced motion: hand jumps without easing. Server-render a status so it is correct before script runs.
avoid: Status computed only client-side (wrong at first paint), green dots without words, time zones ignored, or claiming open during a holiday closure.

stack_notes.css: Server-rendered status string; dial hand rotation set from a --minutes variable at render time; underline via @starting-style. RTL: the dial sits at inline-start and the status text follows document direction; the hand still turns clockwise.
stack_notes.js: A small script refreshes status and dial every 60s from opening-hours JSON including exceptions; clears its interval on unmount and on visibilitychange hidden.

name: The visitor's own question
blueprint: Centred hero whose h1 is the question the visitor arrives with, in their words: Someone has died. What do I do now?, Water coming through the ceiling?, Booking your first tattoo?, set at clamp(2.25rem, 5.5vw, 4.25rem) with text-wrap: balance in a 40rem measure. Beneath, 3 to 4 answer routes as full-width rows 4rem tall, each a link with a bold label and a one-line plain answer (Call us now, day or night; See what happens in the first 24 hours; Check prices). Rows have a 1px top rule and a trailing arrow. Corners: rows square, radius 0.
motion: Hover or focus on a row slides its arrow 6px toward inline-end and fills the row ground from inline-start over 200ms. Entering view rows rise 12px in a 70ms stagger, already readable.
still_check: Any still shows the question and every route complete with label and answer.
mobile: At 375px rows keep full width, labels at 1.125rem and answers at 0.9375rem; the question drops to clamp(1.9rem, 8vw, 2.4rem).
a11y: Rows are a nav with a list of links; the arrow is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: no rise or fill sweep, only a colour change on focus. Focus ring 3px inside the row.
avoid: A question in marketing voice instead of the visitor's, more than 4 routes, routes that lead to the same page, or burying the phone number behind a form.

stack_notes.css: Row fill via background-size transition with background-position set by logical direction. RTL: fill and arrow motion mirror with :dir(rtl) swapping background-position and translate sign.
stack_notes.js: None required. Optionally log which route is chosen to tune the order; no third-party trackers.

name: Torchlight over the workbench
blueprint: Centred hero on a near-black stage, min-height 100svh. Behind everything, a large photograph of the trade's working surface (the bench, the bar, the embalming-free arrangement room, the tattoo station) dimmed to 8% brightness. A soft circular torch radius clamp(10rem, 22vw, 18rem) follows the pointer and shows the photo at full brightness inside it. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6.5vw, 5.5rem), text-wrap: balance, is always lit, on its own solid band, centred. Corners: square band, radius 0; action square 2px radius.
motion: Pointer moves the torch with a 120ms lerp. Without a pointer (touch, keyboard), the torch tours 4 preset points of interest every 3.5s, each labelled with a one-line caption at its spot. Scroll 0-100% widens the torch radius to cover the whole photo by the hero's end.
still_check: At 50% scroll the torch already covers about half the photo, a caption is readable at its point, and the h1 band is crisp.
mobile: At 375px the torch tours preset points only, radius 40vw, and the photo uses a portrait crop.
a11y: Photo described in alt; captions are real text listed in DOM order. Reduced motion: no torch, photo shows at 60% brightness with all captions visible. The h1 never depends on the torch for contrast.
avoid: Putting the h1 in the dark area, captions only visible inside the torch, a torch that lags more than 150ms, or a photo of nothing in particular.

stack_notes.css: Static fallback: mask-image radial-gradient at a fixed point plus captions. The scroll widening uses a registered --torch on a view() timeline.
stack_notes.js: Pointermove updates --x/--y via rAF with lerp; tour mode timer pauses on visibilitychange; listeners removed on unmount.

name: Concentric rings of reach
blueprint: Centred hero where concentric rings mark real reach from the business: service radius in miles, minutes of response, years of a family firm, generations of a vineyard. 5 rings, from 8rem to 90vmin diameter, 1px strokes, each labelled at its inline-end edge with a value at 0.8125rem tabular (10 min, 20 min, 30 min). At the centre a 4rem marker for the premises. The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, sits in the upper third, the deck and a postcode check field below the rings. Corners: field and button share a 2px radius; no rounded panels.
motion: Entering view rings expand from the centre to their radius over 900ms, staggered 90ms, then hold. Scroll progress 0-100% gently compresses the rings to 85% so their labels slide closer, a calm depth cue. A postcode entered in the field highlights the ring that contains it.
still_check: At 50% every ring and label is complete and readable, the centre marker visible, the h1 and field crisp.
mobile: At 375px rings become 4, max diameter 92vw, labels move to a legend list under them.
a11y: Rings are an SVG with a title and a legend table as the accessible source. Reduced motion: rings render at final size. Field has a visible label and inline error text.
avoid: Rings that imply a precise radius the business does not serve, labels on top of each other, or decoration rings with no values.

stack_notes.css: SVG circles with r animated via CSS transitions on @starting-style and a view() timeline for compression. RTL: labels sit at inline-end, so place them with text-anchor end and mirror x under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: Postcode check calls the project's own coverage endpoint and returns ring index; debounce 300ms; abort pending fetch on unmount.

name: Point cloud of the object
blueprint: Centred hero, 100svh, on a dark ground. A WebGL point cloud of 30k to 60k points forms the silhouette of the trade's real object (a tap and pipe run, a guitar, a grape cluster, a lantern, a coding robot kit), sampled from a 3D model or a depth photo. The h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, is DOM text centred over a quiet zone the cloud avoids by sampling a mask of the h1's box. Under it a 1.125rem deck and one action. Corners: action square 2px radius.
motion: Load: points start scattered as a loose field and fall into the silhouette over 1.6s with curl-noise easing. Scroll progress 0-100% rotates the silhouette 0 to 90deg on Y and lets the outer 30% of points drift toward the next section's position, leading the eye down. Pointer nearby pushes points away within a 6rem radius.
still_check: At 50% the silhouette is formed and turned about 45deg, recognisable, never covering the h1 quiet zone.
mobile: At 375px point count drops to 12k and pointer push is off; if WebGL2 is unavailable a dotted PNG of the silhouette is shown.
a11y: Canvas aria-hidden; a visually hidden sentence names the object. Reduced motion: static dotted image, no fall or rotation.
avoid: Points that never form a recognisable object, clouds that cover the h1, 100k+ points on phones, or generic galaxy particles unrelated to the trade.

stack_notes.css: Static poster: dotted silhouette PNG behind the h1, sized to its final box to avoid layout shift.
stack_notes.js: three.js Points with a custom shader; positions baked to a Float32Array; pause when off-screen; dispose geometry, material and renderer on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Copy hugging the object's contour
blueprint: Object-wrap hero, max width 76rem, padding clamp(2rem, 6vw, 5rem). A cut-out photo of the trade's object with transparent background (a loaf, an urn, a boot, a bottle, a toolbox) floats at inline-end, height clamp(22rem, 60vh, 40rem). The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) with text-wrap: balance and a 120 to 160 word paragraph with text-wrap: pretty flow around the object's actual silhouette using shape-outside from the image alpha, with shape-margin 1.25rem. The paragraph names real particulars. Corner radius: 0 throughout, the object silhouette supplies the curves; the action is a text link.
motion: Entering view the object rotates from -3deg to 0 and rises 1rem over 700ms; text does not move. No scroll motion afterwards.
still_check: Any still shows the object and the text tightly following its edge with no line shorter than 3 words.
mobile: At 375px shape-outside is dropped; the object sits above the text at 60vw wide, centred, and the paragraph runs full width.
a11y: The object image has meaningful alt. Reduced motion: no rotate or rise. Text order is unaffected by the float.
avoid: Objects with spiky alpha that make ragged one-word lines, shape-margin under 1rem so text touches the object, or wrapping a generic product shot instead of the trade's own thing.

stack_notes.css: float: inline-end; shape-outside: url(object.png) with shape-image-threshold 0.4; entry motion via @starting-style. RTL: float inline-end mirrors automatically; rotation sign flips under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Seal ring around the object
blueprint: Object-wrap hero centred on a round photo of the object seen from above (a wine cork, a tattoo machine coil, a pie, a water meter face), diameter clamp(16rem, 38vw, 30rem). Around it a text ring on an SVG textPath reads the business name and a true claim (Family run since 1962, Licensed by the Water Services Regulation Authority). The ring text is decorative; the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, sits under the seal with a short deck and two actions. Corners: actions 2px radius; the seal is the only round element.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% rotates the ring text 0 to 120deg while the photo counter-rotates 0 to -20deg, a slow mechanical feel. Entering view the ring draws its text along the path from start to end over 800ms.
still_check: At 50% the ring is turned about 60deg with all of its words readable on the visible arc, the photo sharp, the h1 complete.
mobile: At 375px the seal is 70vw, ring text shortens to the name only, rotation range halves.
