a11y: Ring SVG aria-hidden because the h1 and deck carry the same facts. Reduced motion: ring static at 0deg. Focus ring on actions.
avoid: Ring text claims that are not true, rotation so fast it reads as a loading spinner, or a seal that looks like a fake award badge.

stack_notes.css: SVG textPath on a circle path; rotation via animation-timeline: view(); draw-in via stroke-dasharray on a text clip. RTL: the ring text follows its script direction on the path; for RTL scripts set the path direction anticlockwise.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Object nested in the letter
blueprint: Object-wrap hero, 100svh. The h1 at clamp(4rem, 14vw, 13rem), text-wrap: balance, contains a word with a large counter (the O in Wood, the o in Tattoo, the a in Camp) and a WebGL render of the trade's object sits exactly inside that counter, sized to it, as if the letter were holding it. The letter's stroke passes in front of the object at the top and behind it at the bottom (two DOM copies of the letter with clip masks), so it reads as truly interlocked. Deck and one action below. Corners: action square 2px radius.
motion: Load: the object drops into the counter from 20vh above with a damped bounce over 900ms. Scroll progress 0-100% spins the object 0 to 360deg on Y while the headline tracking widens from -0.04em to 0.02em, giving the object air to leave toward the next section at the end.
still_check: At 50% the object sits in the counter turned 180deg, the letter clearly in front at the top and behind at the bottom, every word legible.
mobile: At 375px a pre-rendered transparent PNG replaces the render; the h1 is clamp(3rem, 16vw, 4.5rem) and the nest still holds.
a11y: The h1 reads as normal text; the duplicated letter copy is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: no drop or spin; static three-quarter view.
avoid: Measuring the counter once and missing on font swap (re-measure after fonts load), objects larger than the counter, or a word chosen only for its O.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: transparent PNG placed with anchor positioning to the letter span; front and back masks via clip-path inset.
stack_notes.js: Measure the counter from a canvas text-metrics pass; three.js renderer sized to it; ResizeObserver re-measures; dispose renderer and textures on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: measure split or fitted text only after document.fonts.ready, or line breaks shift once the web font lands.

name: Anatomy with leader lines
blueprint: Object-wrap hero showing one cut-out photo of the trade's object at clamp(18rem, 44vw, 36rem) (a combi boiler, a casket handle detail, a camp backpack, a wine barrel), with 4 to 6 leader lines from real parts to labels around it: each label is a 2-line note at 0.9375rem, a bold part name and a plain sentence about why it matters to the visitor. Labels sit in two side columns of 14rem; leader lines are 1px with a 6px dot at the part. The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, sits above the object. Corners: labels have no boxes; action 2px radius.
motion: Scroll progress 10-70% draws the leader lines one by one from part to label with stroke-dashoffset, each label fading in as its line arrives; 70-100% the object turns slightly (rotateY 0 to 8deg).
still_check: At 50% at least 3 lines and labels are complete and the rest have not started; nothing is half-faded. At 75% all are drawn.
mobile: At 375px labels become a numbered list under the object; the photo carries small numbered markers instead of lines.
a11y: Labels are an ordered list matching markers; the image alt names the object. Reduced motion: all lines and labels shown complete. Hover or focus on a label highlights its part.
avoid: Lines that cross each other, labels that state specs instead of benefits to the visitor, more than 6 callouts, or parts that do not exist on the real object.

stack_notes.css: SVG overlay with path lines; draw via animation-timeline: view() and animation-range per line. RTL: label columns are logical, mirror the SVG x coordinates under :dir(rtl) with a scale(-1,1) wrapper and counter-flip text. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.
stack_notes.js: Compute line endpoints from label boxes with ResizeObserver; disconnect on unmount.

name: Object on the headline's shelf
blueprint: Object-wrap hero, padding clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem). A single 2px shelf line runs across the full content width at about 60% of the hero height. The h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 7vw, 6rem), text-wrap: balance, sits with its last line's baseline exactly on the shelf, flush to inline-start. At inline-end, 2 or 3 cut-out photos of the trade's objects at real relative scale stand on the same shelf (a jar, a bag of flour, a whisk; or a helmet, a lamp, a map). Below the shelf: a 2-column row with the deck and the action. Corners: radius 0; the shelf is the design.
motion: Entering view the objects slide onto the shelf from 1rem above with a soft settle, 100ms apart; the shelf line draws from inline-start in 500ms. Static after.
still_check: Any still shows the shelf, objects standing on it with contact shadows, and the headline's baseline on the same line.
mobile: At 375px the shelf moves under the objects, which sit in a row of 3 at 28vw each, and the h1 sits above them with its own short rule.
a11y: Objects have alt text; shelf is decorative. Reduced motion: no slide, shelf drawn.
avoid: Objects floating above the shelf (missing contact shadow), wrong relative scale, or baselines that drift off the shelf when fonts swap.

stack_notes.css: Grid with align-items: last baseline; the shelf is a border-block-end on the row. Draw-in via scaleX keyed to view(). RTL: the shelf draws from inline-start with transform-origin swapped under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Knolled tools snapping to grid
blueprint: Object-wrap hero, top-down. 8 to 14 cut-out photos of the trade's real tools and materials (needles, ink caps, stencil paper; or pipe cutter, PTFE tape, spanner) lie around a central h1 block at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance. Items start in a loose, slightly rotated pile and end knolled: aligned at 90 degrees on an invisible 2rem grid, parallel to each other, framing the h1. Each item has a small caption at 0.75rem. Corners: the h1 block is a square ground with radius 0; captions plain.
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% moves each item from its pile position and rotation to its grid slot with a slight overshoot; 70-100% captions fade in beside each item. Hovering an item lifts it 4px with a sharper shadow.
still_check: At 50% items are halfway between pile and grid, every one distinct, none covering the h1.
mobile: At 375px items are cut to 6 and arranged in a 2-column grid under the h1; the motion is a short entry snap.
a11y: Items are a list with captions; images have empty alt when captions name them. Reduced motion: items rendered knolled with captions. Keyboard focus on items shows their caption.
avoid: Items overlapping the headline, using vector icons instead of real photos, items that are not the trade's own, or more than 14 pieces.

stack_notes.css: Final grid positions in CSS; pile offsets as custom properties per item animated by view() timeline. RTL: grid columns mirror; pile offsets on the x axis are multiplied by -1 under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: rAF progress mapper writes per-item interpolation; ResizeObserver recomputes the grid; cleanup on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Exterior to cutaway scrub
blueprint: Object-wrap hero, pinned 180vh with a 100svh stage. Two registered images of the same object: its exterior and a cutaway or inside view (a wall and the pipes inside it; a skin surface and the ink layer; a barrel and its contents; a casket and its lining). The cutaway sits under the exterior; a vertical divider line 2px wide sweeps across. The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, sits at inline-start on a solid panel 28rem wide, the images fill the remainder. 3 notes appear on the cutaway side as it is revealed. Corners: panel radius 0, notes 2px radius.
motion: Scroll progress 0-80% moves the divider from inline-start to inline-end, revealing the cutaway; each note appears when the divider passes it. 80-100% hold.
still_check: At 50% half of the object shows exterior and half cutaway, the divider sharp, at least one note readable, h1 panel complete.
mobile: At 375px images stack vertically and the divider sweeps top to bottom over a 140vh pin; the h1 panel sits above.
a11y: Both images have alt text describing what each shows; notes are a list in DOM order. Reduced motion: no pin; the two images show side by side with notes.
avoid: Images not registered to the same frame, notes that cover the divider, a pin beyond 2 viewports, or a cutaway that shows nothing the visitor cares about.

stack_notes.css: clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - var(--p)) 0 0) on the exterior with --p on a view() timeline. RTL: use inset on the opposite side under :dir(rtl) so the sweep runs from inline-start. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: Optional drag handle for desktop that writes --p from pointer x; keyboard arrows move it 5%; listeners removed on unmount.

name: Sticker peeling off the headline
blueprint: Object-wrap hero, 100svh. The h1 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 8rem), text-wrap: balance, is set on a bold ground. Stuck over one word is a die-cut sticker of the trade's object (a flash tattoo design, a camp patch, a beer label, a council recycling sticker) at clamp(10rem, 22vw, 18rem). The sticker is a WebGL plane with a page-curl shader. Under the h1 the deck and an action. Corners: sticker has a 1.5rem die-cut white border following its shape; action square 2px radius.
motion: Scroll progress 0-60% peels the sticker from its bottom inline-end corner, curling it back to reveal the covered word; 60-100% the sticker lifts away and settles stuck at the hero's corner at 60% size. Pointer hover on the sticker previews a small 10deg peel.
still_check: At 50% the sticker is curled back about 80%, its underside visible, and the covered word fully readable.
mobile: At 375px a CSS-only version: the sticker rotates and slides off the word with a shadow, no curl; sizes halve.
a11y: The covered word is always in the DOM h1; the sticker canvas is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: the sticker starts in its corner position and nothing covers the word.
avoid: Covering the word with no fallback (word unreadable until scroll), curl shaders that tear at the edge, or clip-art stickers unrelated to the trade.

stack_notes.css: Fallback via transform rotate and translate on a view() timeline. RTL: peel from the bottom inline-end corner; mirror the curl axis under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: three.js plane with a curl vertex shader parameterised by progress; texture from the sticker PNG; dispose on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Strata of facts
blueprint: Stacked hero made of 4 to 5 full-width horizontal bands like rock strata, each a different tint of one earthy hue, each band 1 fact tall: the h1 band first at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) with text-wrap: balance, then bands for where, when, how much and who, each a single line at clamp(1.125rem, 2vw, 1.5rem) with its label in small caps at inline-start and its value at inline-end. Band heights vary (clamp(4rem, 9vh, 7rem) to clamp(9rem, 22vh, 14rem)) to reflect importance. Corner radius 0; bands meet edge to edge with a 1px darker seam.
motion: Entering view, bands settle from 0.5rem offsets into place from the top band down, 80ms apart, 400ms each. Scroll progress 0-100% shifts each band's tint 4% darker so the stack reads deeper as you leave. No horizontal motion.
still_check: Any still shows every band with label and value readable and the seams aligned.
mobile: At 375px label and value stack inside each band, bands grow to fit, h1 band at clamp(2rem, 9vw, 2.75rem).
a11y: Bands are a dl after the h1. Reduced motion: no settle, tints fixed. Each tint pair passes 4.5:1 for its text.
avoid: Too many bands (keep 5 max), tints so close the seams vanish, or facts that are slogans.

stack_notes.css: Flex column; tints via color-mix(in oklch) from one base; darken via animation-timeline: view(). Logical properties for label and value placement so RTL mirrors automatically. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Counter-running noun rows
blueprint: Stacked hero, min-height 100svh, 3 full-bleed rows. Row 1 and row 3 are marquees of the trade's real nouns at clamp(2rem, 6vw, 5rem) in outline type (rye, spelt, sourdough or boilers, radiators, showers), separated by a small glyph. Row 2, between them, is the static h1 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 8rem), text-wrap: balance, solid ink on a contrasting band. Under the rows: deck and two actions in a 2-column row. Corner radius 0 on bands; actions square-cornered with 2px radius.
motion: Rows 1 and 3 move in opposite directions; their translate is driven by scroll progress through the page top (0 to -30% and 0 to +30%) plus a slow idle drift of 1 loop per 40s. The h1 row is static.
still_check: At 50% both marquee rows show complete words (no half word at the viewport edge matters, but at least 3 whole nouns are visible per row) and the h1 is untouched.
mobile: At 375px marquee type drops to clamp(1.5rem, 8vw, 2rem); idle drift stops, only scroll offset remains.
a11y: Marquee rows aria-hidden with the noun list given once as visible text further down. Pause control for the idle drift. Reduced motion: marquees static.
avoid: Marquees on the h1 itself, rows moving with scroll velocity, slogans instead of nouns, or drift speed above 1 loop per 20s.

stack_notes.css: Duplicated row content with translate via animation-timeline: scroll(root); idle drift via @keyframes. RTL: direction of travel is defined relative to inline-start; swap translate signs under :dir(rtl). Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: Optional: pause idle drift on visibilitychange; no other script.

name: Photos in the gaps between lines
blueprint: Stacked hero, 3 to 4 line h1 at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 8.5rem), line-height 0.95, text-wrap: balance, each line its own block. Between lines, gap strips start at 0 height and open to clamp(5rem, 14vh, 9rem), each strip holding a wide photo crop of the trade at work (hands kneading, a van at dawn, a ceremony aisle). Photos are cropped to a 6:1 band. Deck and action follow the last line. Corner radius 0; the strips are hard-edged like film.
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% opens the strips one after another from top to bottom; photos inside move at 0.6x so they appear to slide behind the type. 70-100% hold.
still_check: At 50% the first two strips are open with readable photos and the h1 lines are all intact and in order.
mobile: At 375px only 2 strips open, each clamp(4rem, 22vw, 6rem), and the h1 is clamp(2.4rem, 12vw, 3.25rem).
a11y: h1 is a single heading; photos have empty alt when decorative or short alt when meaningful. Reduced motion: strips open from the start.
avoid: Strips opening so far the headline separates into unrelated words, photos with faces cut at the brow, or layout shift (reserve final strip heights in a container).

stack_notes.css: Strip height via a registered --open on view() timelines with per-strip animation-range; the h1 container has a fixed total height. Vertical motion only, so RTL needs no mirroring.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Today's printed sheet
blueprint: Stacked hero styled as the day's typed sheet pinned by the door: a 48rem column on paper with a date line at top (Tuesday 14 October in tabular small caps), the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem) with text-wrap: balance, then a stacked list of today's real items: what's on, who's in, what's ready, what's booked out (Sourdough ready 7:30, Tour at 14:00 has 3 places, Emergency line staffed until 22:00). Each item a row with time at inline-start in tabular figures. One action at the end. Corner radius 2px on the paper sheet, rows square.
motion: Entering view, rows type in as whole rows (no character typing), 60ms apart. A row whose time has passed is struck through with a line that draws in 300ms.
still_check: Any still shows the date, h1 and all rows complete; past rows already struck.
mobile: At 375px time moves above each item; sheet goes full width with 1rem gutters.
a11y: List is an ol; struck rows add visually hidden text Finished. Reduced motion: rows present, strikes static. Server-render the day so it is right at first paint.
avoid: A stale sheet (no CMS hook), invented busy-ness, or typewriter character effects that delay reading.

stack_notes.css: Rows via @starting-style opacity and translate; strike via a pseudo-element scaleX. RTL: strike draws from inline-start by swapping transform-origin under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: A small script re-evaluates past rows each minute; interval cleared on unmount.

name: Fit-to-width word stack
blueprint: Stacked hero whose h1 is one sentence broken into 4 to 6 lines, each line fitted to the full content width (each line gets its own font size so its ink spans edge to edge: short words huge, long words smaller, from clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem) up to clamp(5rem, 22vw, 20rem)). The words are the trade's promise in plain speech (WE / COME OUT / AT NIGHT / FOR LEAKS). A thin rule between lines. Deck and action below in normal type with text-wrap: pretty. Corner radius 0; brutal flat ground.
motion: Scroll progress 0-80% reveals lines one by one: each line slides up out of its own overflow mask, completes, then the next begins; lines already set never move again. 80-100% the rules extend full width.
still_check: At 50% the first 3 lines are fully set and readable, later lines not started (masked, not half-shown).
mobile: At 375px the fitted sizes recompute for the width; reveal shortens to a load-time sequence of 120ms per line.
a11y: The h1 is one sentence in DOM, line spans are presentational. Text is visible without JS: lines start set, and JS only adds the masked reveal class. Reduced motion: no reveal.
avoid: Lines fitted with letter-spacing hacks instead of font size, hiding text until JS runs, or over 6 lines.

stack_notes.css: CSS fallback: each line sized with a precomputed clamp() per line and container query units (cqi). Vertical slides only, no RTL mirroring needed; fitting works for any script.
stack_notes.js: Fit lines with a measure pass after document.fonts.ready and on ResizeObserver; reveal via IntersectionObserver plus WAAPI; cleanup on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Stacked folder tabs
blueprint: Stacked hero shaped like a set of manila folders seen from the front: 4 to 5 folder tabs at the top edge, offset across the width, each labelled with a service area (Arrangements, Prices, Pre-planning, After a death). The front folder is open and holds the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, a short paragraph and two actions. Clicking a tab brings that folder to the front with its own h2 content. Folders are 52rem wide on desktop. Corner radius: 6px on tab tops only, folder bodies square.
motion: Switching folders: the outgoing folder drops 0.75rem and darkens, the incoming rises to the front in 260ms. Entering view, folders fan up from a single stack, 60ms apart.
still_check: Any still shows one complete front folder and all tab labels legible.
mobile: At 375px tabs become a horizontal scroll-snap row above a single folder body.
a11y: Tabs follow the ARIA tabs pattern with arrow-key navigation. Reduced motion: instant swap. The default folder content is server-rendered.
avoid: More than 5 folders, tabs labelled by internal jargon, or hiding the phone number inside a back folder.

stack_notes.css: Radio inputs plus :has(:checked) to raise a folder with z-index and transform; logical inset for tab offsets so RTL mirrors. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: Optional: upgrade to a proper tablist with roving tabindex; sync to URL hash.

name: Contact sheet with grease pencil
blueprint: Stacked hero: h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, above a black contact-sheet strip of 6 frames of real work (each frame 3:2, clamp(8rem, 15vw, 13rem) wide) with frame numbers and sprocket marks in the film border. One frame is circled in red grease pencil; its caption sits under the strip. Deck and action below. Corner radius 0; frames are hard-edged like a real print.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% moves the grease-pencil circle from frame 1 to frame 6, redrawing (stroke-dashoffset) at each frame, and swaps the caption to that frame's line in a 180ms crossfade.
still_check: At 50% the circle is fully drawn around frame 3 or 4 and its caption matches.
mobile: At 375px the strip becomes a 2 by 3 grid; the circle jumps frame to frame on a tap.
a11y: Frames are figures with figcaptions; the circled state also adds aria-current. Reduced motion: circle stays on frame 1, all captions listed below.
avoid: Stock photos, circling frames out of order, or a strip that scrolls sideways with no visible cue.

stack_notes.css: SVG circle per frame drawn via animation-timeline: view() with staggered animation-range. RTL: the circle travels from inline-start, so reverse the frame order range under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Signpost blades to tasks
blueprint: Stacked hero with a vertical post 1.25rem wide at the centre-left and 4 sign blades stacked down it, each blade a pointed sign 22rem to 30rem long pointing toward its task: Book a visit, Emergency, Prices, Find us. Blades point alternately to inline-start and inline-end. Each blade is a link, text at clamp(1.125rem, 2vw, 1.5rem). The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits above the post. Corner radius 2px on blade corners except the pointed end.
motion: Entering view each blade swings into place from rotateY(70deg) around the post, 100ms apart, 450ms each. Hover lifts a blade 4px and nudges it 6px toward its point.
still_check: Any still shows all blades readable and pointing in their direction.
mobile: At 375px blades all point to inline-end, full width minus the post, 3.5rem tall.
a11y: Blades are a nav list of links. Reduced motion: no swing. Blade text 4.5:1 on its colour.
avoid: More than 5 blades, decorative signs that are not links, or blade text rotated.

stack_notes.css: clip-path polygon for the pointed blade; swing via @starting-style rotateY. RTL: blade direction set with logical classes; mirror the polygon under :dir(rtl). Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Slow pan with a solid band
blueprint: Full-bleed hero, 100svh, a single wide photograph of the trade's place (a chapel garden, a reservoir, a cellar, a workshop) at 2:1 crop scaled to 112% so it can pan. At the bottom a solid band, full width, clamp(9rem, 22vh, 13rem) tall in the brand ink, holds the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem) with text-wrap: balance at inline-start and one action at inline-end. Text never sits on the photo. Corner radius 0; action square 2px radius.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% pans the photo 6% toward inline-end and 3% up, linear; nothing else moves.
still_check: At 50% the photo is mid-pan and the band text crisp.
mobile: At 375px use a portrait crop and pan vertically only; band text wraps to 3 lines.
a11y: Photo alt describes the place. Reduced motion: no pan.
avoid: Text over the photo, pans over 8%, autoplaying Ken Burns on a loop.

stack_notes.css: object-position animated on animation-timeline: view(). RTL: pan direction toward inline-end, swap the object-position keyframes under :dir(rtl). Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Scroll-scrubbed process film
blueprint: Full-bleed pinned hero, 300vh with 100svh sticky stage. A 4 to 6 second film of the trade's real process (dough rising, a pipe being soldered, a tattoo line pulled, a glass poured) shot locked-off, exported as 90 to 120 WebP frames or an all-keyframe MP4. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid panel at block-start inline-start, 30rem wide; 3 captions take turns on a panel at block-end as the process passes key moments. Corner radius 0 on panels.
motion: Scroll progress 0-90% maps to the film's frames 0 to N, drawn to a canvas; captions switch at 25%, 50%, 75%. 90-100% the last frame holds and the panel slides out.
still_check: At 50% a sharp mid-process frame shows with caption 2 readable and the h1 panel intact.
mobile: At 375px the frame set halves and uses a 4:5 crop; pin is 200vh.
a11y: Canvas has a text description; captions are real text in order. Reduced motion: no pin; show a still of the finished result with all captions as a list.
avoid: Loading 30MB of frames upfront (stream frames, start with every 4th), motion blur in frames that makes stills ugly, or a film of nothing.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: a poster image with the captions in a list; sticky stage only when JS confirms frames loaded.
stack_notes.js: Preload frames in idle batches as ImageBitmaps; rAF draws the frame for current progress; release bitmaps and observers on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.

name: Duotone from night to day
blueprint: Full-bleed hero: one photograph of the trade's place rendered as a duotone via an SVG feColorMatrix filter, starting as a night pair (navy and amber) and ending as a day pair (cream and the brand ink). The h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid ink block 36rem wide anchored to block-end inline-start. Hours or a time of day appears as small text in the block (We work 7am to 10pm). Corner radius 0.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% interpolates the duotone pair from night to day. Text block colours swap at 50% so contrast is never mid-blend.
still_check: At 50% the photo sits at a dusk mix, recognisable, and the block text is at full contrast in its post-swap colours.
mobile: At 375px the photo uses a portrait crop; block spans full width.
a11y: Reduced motion: the day duotone, static. Photo alt describes the place.
avoid: Duotones that make faces grey and ill, text on the photo, or colour pairs with no tie to the trade.

stack_notes.css: Two duotone images stacked, crossfading via opacity on a view() timeline, as a robust alternative to animating the filter. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: Optional live SVG filter whose matrix values are set from progress in rAF.

name: Venetian blinds opening
blueprint: Full-bleed hero, 100svh. A photograph of the trade's interior sits behind 14 to 20 horizontal slats, each clamp(2.5rem, 6vh, 4rem) tall, in the brand ink colour. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem), text-wrap: balance, is printed across the closed slats as if painted on the blind, in a light colour, centred-left. Under the blind, after the hero, deck and action. Corner radius 0.
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% rotates the slats open (scaleY from 1 to 0.08 per slat, from the slat's centre), revealing the interior; the h1 fades out between 40% and 55% and reappears as a DOM h1 on a solid band at block-end at 55%.
still_check: At 50% slats are half open, the interior readable through them, and the h1 is fully readable on its band (the swap already done), never mid-fade on stripes.
mobile: At 375px slats are 10, h1 band always shown from the start.
a11y: One DOM h1; the painted copy is aria-hidden. Reduced motion: slats open, h1 on band.
avoid: Text on half-open slats (unreadable), slats too thin to read as blinds, or an interior photo that does not reward the reveal.

stack_notes.css: Slats from one repeating-linear-gradient mask with animated mask-size on a view() timeline, cheaper than 20 elements. Vertical motion; no RTL change.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Tilt-shift focus band
blueprint: Full-bleed hero photograph of a wide scene (a village with the shop, a water treatment works, a camp field), with a tilt-shift effect: a sharp horizontal band 28% of the height across the subject, blurred above and below via two backdrop-filter layers. The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5.5vw, 4.5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid paper panel 34rem wide floating above the blurred top area, never on the sharp band. Corner radius 2px on the panel.
motion: Entering view only: blur rises from 0 to 6px over 600ms, focusing attention on the band. Nothing scroll-linked.
still_check: Any still shows the band sharp, the rest softly blurred, panel text crisp.
mobile: At 375px the band covers 36% and the panel moves under the photo.
a11y: Photo alt names the subject in the band. Reduced motion: final blur, no transition.
avoid: Blur over 10px that looks broken, a band that misses the subject, or placing text on the blur without a panel.

stack_notes.css: Two absolutely positioned layers with backdrop-filter: blur() and a linear-gradient mask; entry via @starting-style. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Atmosphere of the place
blueprint: Full-bleed hero with a real photograph of the place and a WebGL shader that adds the atmosphere the trade lives in: rain on the chapel window glass, steam over a bakery bench, caustics on a pool floor, heat haze over a forge, mist in vine rows. The shader samples the photo and a hand-painted mask of where the effect belongs. The h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid block at block-end. Corner radius 0 on the block.
motion: Effect runs at a slow constant rate; scroll progress 0-100% eases the effect strength from 1 to 0.3 so the page calms as you read on. Pointer movement over the glass (rain) wipes a clear streak that refills in 2s.
still_check: At 50% the effect is visible but softer, the photo subject clear, the h1 block crisp.
mobile: At 375px half resolution and no pointer interaction; static still with effect baked when WebGL2 is absent.
a11y: Canvas aria-hidden; the photo's alt is on a fallback img. Reduced motion: baked still with effect frozen.
avoid: Generic effects with no tie to the place, effects over faces, battery-draining 60fps when off-screen.

stack_notes.css: Fallback img with the effect baked; block text on solid ground.
stack_notes.js: Fragment shader with photo and mask textures; render at device pixel ratio capped at 1.5; stop on IntersectionObserver exit; dispose on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Mosaic that flips into the photo
blueprint: Full-bleed hero: a grid of 8 by 5 square tiles (each about 12.5vw) that together form one photograph of the trade's place. Initially each tile shows a solid colour sampled from the photo's region (a coarse pixel mosaic). The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid block spanning 4 by 2 tiles at block-end inline-start, part of the grid. Corner radius 0; tiles meet with a 2px gap showing the ground.
motion: On load and as the hero enters view, tiles flip (rotateY 180deg, 420ms) to their photo fragment in a diagonal wave from the h1 block outward, 30ms between diagonals. Scroll back above reverses once. Hover flips a single tile to show its solid colour back.
still_check: At 50% of the wave (or any later still), most tiles show photo fragments and the picture is recognisable; the h1 block is never flipped.
mobile: At 375px the grid is 4 by 6 and the wave is quicker (15ms).
a11y: Grid is aria-hidden; the photo alt is on a hidden img. Reduced motion: tiles show the photo, no flips.
avoid: Tiles smaller than 5vw (too many elements), flips that block reading, a mosaic of a stock image.

stack_notes.css: Each tile uses the photo as background with background-position per tile; flip via transform and backface-visibility. RTL: the wave starts from the h1 block at inline-start, mirrored under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: Generate tiles from the grid size; trigger with IntersectionObserver; WAAPI per tile with delays; cancel animations on unmount. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Dusk to lit windows
blueprint: Full-bleed hero of the trade's building at dusk, shot twice from a locked-off tripod: once with lights off at blue hour, once with every window and lamp lit. The lit exposure sits on top with a mask that starts empty. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid block at block-start inline-start with one line of hours under it (Open late on Fridays). Corner radius 0 on the block.
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% expands the lit mask window by window (a hand-made mask PNG whose grey levels order the windows), so lights come on one by one; 70-100% a warm glow layer grows 20%.
still_check: At 50% about half the windows are lit, the building clearly readable, h1 block complete.
mobile: At 375px use a portrait crop of the doorway; same relight.
a11y: Reduced motion: lit exposure shown. Alt text describes the building lit at dusk.
avoid: Exposures not registered, a mask that lights windows randomly, or text on the photo.

stack_notes.css: mask-image with a luminance mask PNG and an animated threshold via mask-size or a registered --t driving a CSS filter on the mask layer; view() timeline. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: Optional canvas compositor that thresholds the grey mask by progress for older engines; cleanup on unmount.

name: Measured gutter split
blueprint: Split hero, 7:5 columns, divided by a vertical ruler gutter 3rem wide with tick marks every 0.5rem and a number every 4rem, printed in the muted ink. Start column: h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, deck with text-wrap: pretty, one action. End column: one measured object of the trade (a frame, a bottle, a radiator, a plot plan) photographed square-on, with its real dimensions noted against the ruler. Corner radius 0 everywhere; ruler ticks are 1px hairlines.
motion: Entering view, ticks draw down the gutter in 500ms; the dimension leader lines extend from the ruler to the object in 300ms after.
still_check: Any still shows the full ruler, the object and its labelled dimensions.
mobile: At 375px the ruler turns horizontal between h1 and object, 2rem tall.
a11y: Ruler aria-hidden; dimensions are real text beside the object. Reduced motion: static drawing.
avoid: Fake dimensions, decorative rulers with no measured object, or ticks heavier than the text.

stack_notes.css: Ticks via repeating-linear-gradient; leaders via scaleX on pseudo-elements anchored at inline-start. RTL: leaders grow from inline-start using logical transform-origin under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Promise left, proof right
blueprint: Split hero, 1:1 columns that are not equal in weight: the start column holds one promise as the h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 7vw, 6rem), text-wrap: balance; the end column holds the evidence for that exact promise as a short typed record (3 to 5 dated lines from real jobs or records: arrival times, inspection grades, hours kept), each line a real data point in tabular figures. A key word of the h1 is underlined and a hairline connects it to the record. Corner radius 0 on columns; record lines square.
motion: Entering view, the hairline draws from the underlined word to the record (400ms), then record lines appear one at a time, 70ms apart.
still_check: Any still shows the promise, the connecting hairline and every record line.
mobile: At 375px the record moves under the h1 and the hairline becomes a short vertical tick.
a11y: Record is a list with dates in time elements. Reduced motion: hairline and lines static.
avoid: A promise with no checkable proof, invented numbers, or proof shown as star ratings.

stack_notes.css: Hairline via an SVG path between anchor points set with CSS anchor positioning where supported, else a fixed vertical rule. RTL: the hairline runs inline-start to inline-end and mirrors with logical anchors.
stack_notes.js: Optional ResizeObserver to recompute the hairline path where anchor positioning is missing.

name: Columns that scroll against each other
blueprint: Split hero, pinned 220vh with 100svh stage, two tall columns of photographs of the trade (each photo 4:5, 2 columns of 6 photos) moving in opposite directions as you scroll, with the h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, sitting on a solid band across the middle of both columns. Under the band a deck and action. Corner radius 2px on photos, 0 on the band.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% moves column A up by 60% of its height and column B down by 60%; the band never moves. Velocity is not used.
still_check: At 50% both columns show whole photos aligned to the band edges, and the band text is crisp.
mobile: At 375px one column only, moving up at 0.5x, no pin.
a11y: Photos meaningful get short alt; columns are a list. Reduced motion: no pin, columns static.
avoid: Photos of nothing, moving the band, or pins longer than 250vh.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: static grid of the 12 photos under the band; pin applies only after JS init.
stack_notes.js: Translate via scroll progress in rAF or a scroll-driven animation; IntersectionObserver to idle off-screen; cleanup on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Do the task in the hero
blueprint: Split hero, 5:7 columns. Start column: a short h1 at clamp(2rem, 4.5vw, 3.5rem), text-wrap: balance, naming the task (Book a viewing, Check your bin day, Get a fixed quote) and one sentence with text-wrap: pretty. End column: the real first step of that task as a working form, 2 to 3 fields at 3rem tall with visible labels (postcode, date, job type), and a submit button 3rem tall with 4px corners. Below the form, what happens next in one line. Corner radius 4px on fields and button; card square with a 1px border.
motion: Focus moves the field label up 0.25rem and darkens the border in 150ms. On a valid entry a small check draws in the field's inline-end.
still_check: Any still shows labels, fields and button complete and readable.
mobile: At 375px form sits under the h1; fields full width.
a11y: Real labels (no placeholder-only), errors announced with aria-live, autocomplete attributes set. Reduced motion: no label move.
avoid: Asking for email before the task, more than 3 fields in the hero, or a form that does not work without JS.

stack_notes.css: Native form with constraint validation styles via :user-invalid; logical padding so the check icon mirrors in RTL. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: Optional progressive enhancement: postcode lookup fetch with abort on unmount.

name: Headline split across depth planes
blueprint: Layered hero, 100svh: a cut-out photograph of the trade's object (a cake, a boiler, a casket spray, a bike) sits between two planes of the h1. The h1 at clamp(4rem, 14vw, 12rem), text-wrap: balance, is set twice in the same position: the back copy is full, the front copy is clipped by the object's silhouette mask so letters pass behind the object and come in front of it at chosen points. Deck and action on a plain area at block-end. Corner radius 0.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% moves the back type plane up 6%, the object 3% and the front plane 0%, so depth reads through parallax without breaking the word.
still_check: At 50% the word reads whole through and around the object; the object is sharp.
mobile: At 375px the object scales to 80vw, h1 to clamp(3rem, 16vw, 4.5rem), parallax off.
a11y: One DOM h1, duplicate copy aria-hidden. Reduced motion: no parallax.
avoid: Object hiding letters so the word cannot be read, a cut-out with halo edges, or depth planes moving over 8%.

stack_notes.css: Front copy with mask-image of the object's PNG silhouette; parallax via view() timelines on translate. Vertical motion only; RTL unaffected. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Layered panes over the place
blueprint: Layered hero, 100svh, over one full-bleed photograph of the place or product. Two panes only, offset in a 12-column grid (not floating at random): pane 1 spans columns 1 to 6 at block-end, a near-solid surface (92% opaque in the ground colour, backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.1) only behind it) holding the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4.25rem) with text-wrap: balance, one sentence and the primary button 3rem tall with 4px corners plus a text link; pane 2 spans columns 9 to 12 higher up, smaller, holding one hard fact (a figure in tabular numerals with its label) or a 4:5 detail photo. Panes have a 1px inner hairline at 12% white and 4px corners, no glow. States: idle, button hover (fill darkens 8%), focus (2px ring offset 2px).
motion: Load: photo scales 1.04 to 1 over 1.2s; pane 1 rises 16px and fades in at 200ms, pane 2 at 320ms. Scroll 0-100%: pane 2 drifts 4vh slower than pane 1. No pointer tilt.
still_check: Any still shows all 3 plates legible; the h1 plate frost is opaque enough for 4.5:1.
mobile: At 375px plates stack vertically, no tilt, blur reduced to 8px.
a11y: Plates are a list of regions in reading order. Reduced motion: no tilt or separation.
avoid: More than two panes, thin frost that fails 4.5:1, glow edges, rounded corners above 6px, pointer-tilt stacks, or glass panes with no content.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: plates with solid 94% backgrounds where backdrop-filter is absent; transforms from custom properties. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: Pointer tilt via pointermove throttled to rAF; disable on coarse pointers; remove listeners on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Tracing paper over the photo
blueprint: Layered hero: a documentary photograph of the trade's place or object, with a sheet of tracing paper laid over its start half (translucent white at 70%) on which the subject is redrawn as a hand-inked line drawing aligned to the photo. The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4.25rem), text-wrap: balance, is lettered on the tracing paper in the ink colour, with small inked labels on parts. Corner radius 0; the paper has a soft torn edge on its inline-end side.
motion: Entering view, the line drawing draws itself in 900ms (stroke-dashoffset), labels fade in after.
still_check: Any still shows photo, paper, completed drawing and h1 legible.
mobile: At 375px the paper covers the top 55% and the drawing simplifies.
a11y: Drawing aria-hidden, labels repeated in a caption. Reduced motion: drawing complete.
avoid: A drawing that does not register to the photo, filter-generated sketches, or labels too small to read.

stack_notes.css: Paper via a semi-transparent background and an SVG mask edge; draw via @starting-style on stroke-dashoffset. Logical inset puts the paper at inline-start so RTL mirrors.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Dolly through the doorway
blueprint: Layered hero built as 4 to 5 depth layers cut from photographs of the trade's real space (the street front, the door, the counter, the back room), arranged in a 3D scene so scroll dollies the camera forward through them. The h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, is set on a solid panel fixed to the viewport at block-end inline-start; layer captions change as each layer passes. Corner radius 0 on the panel.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% moves the camera z from layer 1 to layer 5 with ease-in-out; each layer fades to 0 as the camera passes through it. Pinned 300vh.
still_check: At 50% the camera sits between layers 2 and 3 with both recognisable and the panel crisp.
mobile: At 375px use a CSS 3D fallback with 3 layers and 180vh pin.
a11y: Canvas aria-hidden; captions are real text in a list. Reduced motion: show layer 3 still, no pin.
avoid: Layers cut so roughly they read as paper puppets, fast dollies, or text inside the 3D scene.

stack_notes.css: CSS fallback: preserve-3d stack with translateZ driven by a view() timeline; poster still with no support. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: three.js planes with alpha textures; camera z from scroll progress; dispose textures and geometry on unmount; stop on IntersectionObserver exit. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Annotated by hand
blueprint: Layered hero: a clean typeset h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, with a second layer of hand-drawn ink annotations on top by the owner: one word circled, an arrow to a small photo, a crossed-out word replaced by a better one above it, a margin note with a real fact (yes, even Sundays). The photo is 18rem wide, tilted 2deg, taped. Corner radius 0 on photo; tape strips square.
motion: Entering view, annotations draw one after another (circle 400ms, arrow 300ms, strike 200ms, note fades in), total under 1.6s.
still_check: Any still shows typeset h1 plus every annotation complete.
mobile: At 375px keep only the circle and the margin note; photo goes under the h1.
a11y: Annotations as SVG aria-hidden; the replaced word and the note are also real text for screen readers. Reduced motion: drawn state.
avoid: Font-based fake handwriting, more than 4 annotations, or notes that are jokes about nothing.

stack_notes.css: SVG strokes from real scans; draw via @starting-style; positions in em so they track the type. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Type casting a long shadow
blueprint: Layered hero on a plain warm ground: the h1 at clamp(3.5rem, 10vw, 9rem), text-wrap: balance, set in the brand ink, casting a long soft shadow across the ground as if lit by a low sun, with a single real object (a vase, a stone, a key) on the same ground casting a matching shadow. The deck sits in the shadow's cool tone area with 4.5:1 contrast. Corner radius 0.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% lengthens both shadows 20% and shifts their angle 6deg, as if afternoon passes.
still_check: At 50% shadows are mid-length and the headline is crisp; the object shadow matches the type's angle.
mobile: At 375px shadows fixed, shorter.
a11y: Shadows decorative. Reduced motion: fixed shadow.
avoid: Mismatched shadow angles between type and object, hard black shadows, or shadows that cover the deck.

stack_notes.css: Type shadow via layered text-shadow from a registered --len; object shadow is a separate blurred, skewed element; both read --len on a view() timeline. RTL: the sun stays on the same physical side; no mirroring needed.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Detail zooms out to the whole
blueprint: Layered hero that starts on one extreme detail of the trade (a pastry's lamination, a thread on a gown, a tool's worn grip) filling the viewport, and pulls back to reveal the whole scene, with each step framed by a thin printed crop mark set. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, is on a solid strip at block-start that stays still. Corner radius 0; crop marks 1px.
motion: Scroll progress 0-80% scales the image from 4x to 1x around the detail's focal point, crop marks retreating to the final frame; 80-100% caption fades in.
still_check: At 50% the image sits at about 2x, sharp (source large enough), and the h1 strip is untouched.
mobile: At 375px scale from 2.5x; no pin, uses a view() timeline over 150vh.
a11y: Image alt describes the whole scene. Reduced motion: whole scene, no zoom.
avoid: Upscaled blur at 4x (supply a 4000px source or a separate detail crop), focal points off subject, or zooms that reverse direction.

stack_notes.css: transform: scale with transform-origin at the focal point, driven by animation-timeline: view(); sticky container 200vh.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Misregistered print plates
blueprint: Layered hero printed like a 3-colour risograph: the h1 at clamp(3.5rem, 10vw, 9rem), text-wrap: balance, and one illustration of the trade's object are split into 3 colour plates (e.g. fluorescent pink, blue, yellow) with multiply blend. At rest the plates register perfectly. Paper grain texture on the ground. Corner radius 0.
motion: Pointer position knocks the plates out of register up to 6px each in different directions; scroll velocity adds a brief extra offset that settles back within 400ms. Every still frame settles to registered within 0.4s.
still_check: Any still taken after 0.4s idle shows plates registered and the h1 sharp.
mobile: At 375px no pointer effect; plates offset 2px permanently as a printed look.
a11y: One DOM h1; plate copies aria-hidden. Reduced motion: registered, no movement.
avoid: Offsets so big the word blurs, more than 3 plates, or offsets on body text.

stack_notes.css: Plates as stacked copies with mix-blend-mode: multiply and translate from custom properties; static registered fallback. Pitfall: give the overlay stack an explicit positioning context (a shared grid cell or position: relative parent) so layers align at every size.
stack_notes.js: Pointermove sets offsets via rAF with spring decay; disable for coarse pointers; remove listeners on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Photo with depth-map parallax
blueprint: Layered hero: one photograph of the trade's place paired with a hand-cleaned depth map, rendered in WebGL so pointer and scroll shift near pixels more than far ones (a 2.5D look). The h1 at clamp(2.75rem, 7vw, 6rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid block at block-end, outside the image. Corner radius 0 on block and image.
motion: Pointer movement shifts the view up to 1.5% horizontally; scroll progress 0-100% shifts it 2% vertically. Displacement is clamped to avoid tearing.
still_check: At 50% the photo is undistorted to the eye and the block text crisp.
mobile: At 375px no pointer effect; tiny scroll-only shift; image fallback on low memory devices.
a11y: Canvas aria-hidden with the photo alt on fallback img. Reduced motion: flat photo.
avoid: Auto-generated depth maps with tearing around hair and edges, shifts over 2%, or effects on portraits.

stack_notes.css: Fallback img; block on solid ground.
stack_notes.js: Fragment shader offsets UVs by depth times pointer vector; cap DPR at 1.5; dispose textures on unmount; pause off-screen. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: One part lit per chapter
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 300vh. A single dark photograph of the trade's whole object (a boiler, an espresso machine, a church organ, a printing press) holds the sticky stage. As chapters scroll by in a 26rem text column at inline-end, one part of the object lights up at a time (a light mask over that part) and its chapter heading at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), text-wrap: balance, explains it. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem) is chapter 0. Corner radius 0.
motion: Each chapter's view() range fades its part's light mask from 0 to 1 and the previous one back to 0.2, 300ms cross-ease.
still_check: At any chapter midpoint one part is clearly lit, the matching chapter text readable.
mobile: At 375px the photo pins at the top 45svh and chapters scroll below.
a11y: Chapters are real sections with h2s. Reduced motion: no pin; all parts at 0.6 light with numbered labels.
avoid: Lighting parts that do not match chapters, more than 5 chapters, or text over the dark photo.

stack_notes.css: Light masks are pre-cut PNGs stacked over the dark photo; opacity via named view timelines with timeline-scope on the stage. Logical placement of the text column so RTL mirrors.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Exploded assembly
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 280vh: a 3D model of the trade's product or system (a bike, a valve, a speaker, a cabinet joint) assembled at first, then exploding along its axes into labelled parts as you scroll, then reassembling. Labels are HTML callouts anchored to parts with 1px leaders. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid panel at block-start inline-start. Corner radius 2px on callouts, 0 on panel.
motion: Scroll progress 0-50% explodes parts outward along predefined vectors with 60ms stagger, 50-70% hold with labels, 70-100% reassemble.
still_check: At 60% parts are separated with every label legible and leaders touching their parts.
mobile: At 375px a pre-rendered 3-frame image sequence (assembled, exploded, assembled) swapped by progress.
a11y: Labels are a real list of parts in order. Reduced motion: exploded still with labels, no pin.
avoid: Heavy models over 3MB, labels inside the WebGL canvas, or parts flying off-screen.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: exploded still image with an HTML parts list.
stack_notes.js: three.js with GLTF and Draco; project part anchors to screen each frame; dispose on unmount; stop off-screen. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps. Pitfall: keep transform-style: preserve-3d on every wrapper between the perspective root and the moving planes; one flat wrapper collapses the depth.

name: Slot word for each customer
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 240vh. The h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, has one slot word inside it that changes as you scroll (Cakes for weddings / birthdays / Tuesdays). The slot is a fixed-width box sized to the longest option, with the current word on a ruled window. Beside the stage at inline-end a photo changes to match each word. Corner radius 0 on the slot window, 2px on the photo.
motion: Scroll progress through 4 to 5 stops rolls the slot word vertically to the next option (300ms ease) and crossfades the matching photo.
still_check: At any stop the full sentence reads correctly with one word in the slot and the matching photo.
mobile: At 375px the photo sits under the h1; slot rolls on view() steps.
a11y: The h1 accessible name is the first sentence; all options listed in a visually hidden list. Reduced motion: first option, all options shown as a short list below.
avoid: Options that change the grammar, a slot so narrow words clip, or more than 5 options.

stack_notes.css: Slot as an overflow-hidden inline-block with a column of words translated by steps on a view() timeline. Vertical roll only, RTL unaffected.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Zoom from place to the one detail
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 220vh. A wide photograph of the place (a shopfront, a hall, a garden) pins at 100svh. Three captions in a 24rem column at inline-start each zoom the photo toward a detail (the door, the counter, the bench by the window). The h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, is the first caption. Corner radius 0; caption cards 2px.
motion: Each caption's view() range eases the photo scale and translate toward its detail's focal point (up to 1.8x), 600ms equivalent ease.
still_check: At each caption midpoint the photo is sharp at the zoom level and caption readable.
mobile: At 375px the photo pins in the top 50svh; zoom capped at 1.5x.
a11y: Captions are paragraphs in order. Reduced motion: wide photo, captions listed.
avoid: Zooming into blur (source must be large), more than 3 stops, or captions over the photo without a card.

stack_notes.css: transform on the img with keyframes per stop via named view timelines and timeline-scope. Logical placement of the column so RTL mirrors; zoom targets are physical photo points.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: A day in one pinned frame
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 300vh, telling the trade's day from opening to close: one locked-off frame of the place in 5 timed photographs (6am, 9am, 1pm, 5pm, 10pm) crossfading as you scroll, with a clock face 8rem across at block-start inline-end whose hand advances with progress. Each time has a short line with text-wrap: pretty (6am: dough out of the fridge). The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid strip at block-end. Corner radius 0 on strip; clock is a circle (full radius is right for a clock face).
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% advances the clock hand 16 hours and crossfades photos at each time over 10% of progress; lines swap with the photos.
still_check: At 50% a single sharp photo (not mid-crossfade at stop midpoints) and its time line are shown, the clock hand at the matching hour.
mobile: At 375px photos stack as a vertical list with times, no pin.
a11y: Clock aria-hidden; times are real text in a list. Reduced motion: no pin, list of photos with times.
avoid: Photos from different angles, fake times, or a clock that runs backwards when scrolling up quickly.

stack_notes.css: Fallback list of 5 photos with time labels; pin only after JS init.
stack_notes.js: Progress from a scroll listener throttled to rAF; set hand rotation and photo opacity; cleanup on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Checklist that ticks itself
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 200vh. The start column pins the h1 at clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4rem), text-wrap: balance, and a 4 to 6 item checklist of what the customer actually gets or must do (Survey within 48 hours, Fixed written price, Tidy-up on the day, 12-month guarantee); the end column scrolls a matching photo per item. Each item gets a square tick box 1.5rem. Corner radius 2px on tick boxes; photos 0.
motion: Each photo's view() range ticks its item: the check stroke draws in 250ms and the item text darkens from muted to full ink.
still_check: Any still shows all items readable; ticked items show completed checks.
mobile: At 375px no pin: each item sits above its photo in sequence.
a11y: Checklist is a ul; ticks aria-hidden. Muted text still passes 4.5:1. Reduced motion: all ticked.
avoid: Items that are vague (Great service), more than 6 items, or ticking on a timer instead of scroll.

stack_notes.css: Stroke-dashoffset per tick on named view timelines with timeline-scope on the section. Logical columns so RTL mirrors. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Walk up to the door
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 200vh: a street photograph of the trade's front pins full-bleed, and scrolling walks you up to the door until the door frame fills the viewport and becomes the frame of the next section. The h1 at clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 5rem), text-wrap: balance, sits on a solid sign board at block-start inline-start with the address and hours. Corner radius 0 on the sign; the door opening is a rectangle.
motion: Scroll progress 0-100% scales the photo toward the door's centre up to 3x; the door's opening is a transparent mask through which the next section's interior photo shows at 1x from 70%.
still_check: At 50% the street and door are clear at 2x and the sign board is untouched.
mobile: At 375px a portrait street crop and 2x max zoom.
a11y: Photo alt describes the front and door. Reduced motion: street photo, no zoom; next section starts normally.
avoid: Doors that are not the trade's door, low-res photos, or a door opening that never aligns with the next section.

stack_notes.css: Scale via view() timeline on transform; door opening via mask-image of the door shape. Zoom target is physical; RTL needs no change.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Curtain rises on the room
blueprint: Sticky-stage hero, 180vh: a heavy fabric curtain (real photographed texture, not a gradient) covers the viewport with the h1 at clamp(3rem, 8vw, 7rem), text-wrap: balance, in a solid panel hung on it. As you scroll the curtain rises in gathered folds, revealing the room set for the trade (a dining room, a ballroom, a stage, a chapel). The panel lifts with the curtain and the h1 re-renders on a solid strip at block-end. Corner radius 0.
motion: Scroll progress 0-70% lifts the curtain via a scaleY plus a fold displacement map, 70-100% the room photo settles 1.02 to 1.
still_check: At 50% the curtain is half up, the room partly visible, and the h1 strip is already shown in full.
mobile: At 375px curtain rises without folds, simple translateY.
a11y: One DOM h1. Reduced motion: room shown, no curtain.
avoid: Velvet red for every trade, curtains that never fully rise, or text on the fabric under 4.5:1.

stack_notes.css: Fallback: translateY curtain driven by a view() timeline; vertical only.
stack_notes.js: SVG feDisplacementMap fold scale set from progress in rAF; cleanup on unmount. Pitfall: render each frame as a pure function of progress or time so seeking and scrolling back land on the same state; never chain setTimeout steps.

name: Services as a counter ledger
blueprint: Services as a ruled ledger the way a counter would list them: one row per service, 4.5rem tall, columns for the service name at clamp(1.25rem, 2.2vw, 1.75rem) with text-wrap: balance, what is included in one line with text-wrap: pretty, how long it takes and the from-price in tabular figures at inline-end. Rows are grouped under 2 to 3 small-caps group headings. A row expands in place to 3 to 5 lines of detail. Max width 64rem. Corner radius 0; rows divided by 1px rules.
motion: Row expansion animates height via interpolate-size in 220ms; the plus mark rotates to a minus. Hover tints the row 3%.
still_check: Any still shows every row's name, duration and price aligned in columns.
mobile: At 375px duration and price drop under the name on one line.
a11y: Rows are details/summary; prices are text. Reduced motion: instant open.
avoid: Services listed as icon cards, prices hidden behind contact us, or more than 12 rows without grouping.

stack_notes.css: details with ::details-content and interpolate-size: allow-keywords; grid columns via subgrid so prices align. Logical alignment so RTL mirrors. Pitfall: colours inside the scene come from tokens, never hard-coded values, so a dark or inverted theme recolours the whole scene.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Pick your situation
blueprint: Services organised by the customer's situation rather than the trade's menu: a row of 3 to 5 situation buttons at the top (Moving house, Something is broken, Planning ahead, Just browsing) each 3rem tall with 4px corners, and below them the matching services panel with 2 to 4 services that fit, each with one line of why and a next step. The section h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem) with text-wrap: balance. Panel max 56rem. Corner radius 4px on buttons, 0 on panel.
motion: Choosing a situation crossfades the panel content in 200ms and slides the active underline under the chosen button.
still_check: Any still shows one situation active and its complete panel.
mobile: At 375px situations become a vertical list of buttons above the panel.
a11y: Buttons use aria-pressed or tabs semantics; panel is a live region labelled by the choice. Reduced motion: instant swap. All panels rendered in HTML so they work without JS via :has().
avoid: Situations that are just service names reworded, or more than 5 situations.

stack_notes.css: Radio inputs with :has(:checked) to show panels; underline via anchor positioning or a translated pseudo-element. RTL: the underline slide follows inline direction using logical inset. Pitfall: over-scan each moving layer by its full travel plus a margin so its edges never enter the frame.
stack_notes.js: Optional URL hash sync.

name: Steps along the workbench
blueprint: Process shown as the actual objects at each step laid along a long workbench photo strip 100vw wide and clamp(14rem, 30vw, 22rem) tall: raw material, first cut, assembly, finish, handover. Each step has a numeral at clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4rem) in tabular figures, a title with text-wrap: balance and two lines of text under its object. The strip scrolls horizontally inside the page with snap points. Corner radius 0 on the strip; step markers are 2px squares.
motion: Vertical scroll drives horizontal travel along the strip through a sticky container of 250vh; snap to each step at rest.
still_check: Any still shows at least one full step with its object, numeral and text.
mobile: At 375px the strip becomes a vertical list, one object per step.
a11y: Steps are an ol in reading order. Reduced motion: vertical list. Keyboard: steps are focusable to scroll into view.
avoid: Steps with no object to show, more than 6 steps, or horizontal scroll with no visible progress.

stack_notes.css: Sticky container plus translate on a view() timeline. RTL: the strip travels toward inline-end; invert the translate sign under :dir(rtl) so the first step is at inline-start.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: What happens, and when
blueprint: A two-column table of the customer's journey: when (Today, Within 2 days, On the day, After) in the start column at clamp(1rem, 1.6vw, 1.25rem) small caps, and what happens with who does it in the end column, each row 2 to 3 lines with text-wrap: pretty. One row is marked You do this so the customer sees their own part. The section h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.5rem), text-wrap: balance. Max width 48rem. Corner radius 0; rows ruled.
motion: Entering view, rows appear in order 70ms apart; the You do this marker draws its underline.
still_check: Any still shows all rows complete.
mobile: At 375px the when label sits above each row.
a11y: It is a real table or dl. Reduced motion: static.
avoid: Vague times (Soon), marketing-flavoured steps, or hiding the customer's responsibilities.

stack_notes.css: CSS grid with subgrid for alignment; @starting-style entry. Logical properties so the when column sits at inline-start in RTL.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Before and after, with the record
blueprint: Proof as 3 to 4 real jobs, each a pair of photos (before, after) at 4:3, clamp(14rem, 28vw, 22rem) wide, with a drag divider, plus the job's record beside the pair: date, location area, time taken, what was replaced, the price band. The h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem), text-wrap: balance. Job records in tabular figures. Corner radius 2px on photo pairs; divider handle is a 2.5rem square with 4px corners.
motion: Dragging the divider reveals the after image; keyboard arrows move it 5%. On entering view the divider sweeps from 0 to 50% once in 600ms.
still_check: Any still shows each pair at 50% with the record readable.
mobile: At 375px pairs go full width; records under each pair.
a11y: Divider is an input type range labelled by the job. Reduced motion: no initial sweep.
avoid: Staged befores, photos from different angles, or jobs without dates.

stack_notes.css: Native range input over two stacked images with clip-path inset from a custom property. RTL: the sweep follows inline direction; flip the inset side under :dir(rtl).
stack_notes.js: None required; optional pointer capture refinements.

name: Proof from public records
blueprint: Proof made only of things a stranger can check: registration numbers, inspection grades, licences, insurance cover, years trading, each a row with the authority's name, the value, and a link to look it up. Values at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem) in tabular figures; labels in small text with text-wrap: pretty. The h2 at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), text-wrap: balance. Max 52rem. Corner radius 0; 1px rules.
motion: Entering view, each verification link shows a small check that draws after the row appears, 80ms apart.
still_check: Any still shows every value and its authority.
mobile: At 375px label and value stack.
a11y: Links say where they go (Check on the Food Standards register). Reduced motion: static.
avoid: Invented badges, award logos with no link, or star ratings with no source.

stack_notes.css: Plain grid; check via stroke-dashoffset on @starting-style.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: People at their stations
blueprint: Team as environmental portraits of each person at their own station, doing their part (at the oven, at the desk with the plans, on the van ladder), each 4:5 at clamp(14rem, 24vw, 20rem) wide, laid in an uneven row where heights differ by role. Each portrait carries name, what they do here in one sentence with text-wrap: pretty, and one specific detail (Has fitted 1,200 boilers). The h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem), text-wrap: balance. Corner radius 0 on portraits.
motion: Hover on a portrait swaps to a second photo of their hands at work (crossfade 250ms). Entering view, portraits rise 1rem, 80ms apart.
still_check: Any still shows each person, name and sentence.
mobile: At 375px portraits stack in a single column, 4:5.
a11y: Each portrait figure has alt naming the person and the task. Reduced motion: no swap animation, still swaps on focus.
avoid: Headshots on grey, job titles like Ninja, or team grids of 12 identical squares.

stack_notes.css: Flex row with align-items: end; swap via :hover and :focus-within opacity.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Who you will meet
blueprint: Team arranged by the order a customer meets them (who answers the phone, who visits, who does the work, who follows up), as a vertical sequence with a portrait 7rem square, name, role in the customer's words, and how to reach them directly. A thin line joins the sequence. The h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.5rem), text-wrap: balance. Max 44rem. Corner radius 4px on portraits, never circles.
motion: Entering view, the joining line draws downward through each person, 120ms per person.
still_check: Any still shows every person in order with contact details.
mobile: At 375px portrait sits beside name; line remains.
a11y: An ol of people; contact links labelled. Reduced motion: line static.
avoid: Org charts, people the customer never meets, or contacts that all go to one inbox.

stack_notes.css: Line via a pseudo-element with scaleY on a view() timeline. Logical inline-start placement so RTL mirrors.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Build your receipt
blueprint: Pricing as a receipt the customer builds: options on the start side as checkboxes and steppers (rooms, extras, delivery), each 3rem tall with 4px corners, and on the end side a till receipt 22rem wide in monospace with each chosen line and its price, subtotal, tax and total in tabular figures. The h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem), text-wrap: balance. A print and an email-me link under the receipt. Corner radius 4px on controls; receipt has a zigzag torn bottom edge.
motion: Each change prints a new line onto the receipt (line slides down from the top 180ms) and the total ticks to its new value.
still_check: Any still shows a complete receipt matching the controls.
mobile: At 375px the receipt is sticky at the bottom as a summary bar that expands.
a11y: Total announced via aria-live polite. Works without JS: a default receipt is server-rendered for a common set. Reduced motion: no slide, no tick.
avoid: Hidden fees after the receipt, prices that disagree with the receipt, or fake discount strike-throughs.

stack_notes.css: Receipt via monospace grid; zigzag via mask-image repeating-conic-gradient.
stack_notes.js: Form state to receipt in plain JS or framework state; Intl.NumberFormat for currency; no listeners leak.

name: Three real jobs, priced
blueprint: Pricing explained through 3 real recent jobs of different sizes rather than tiers: each job is a stacked block, not a card in a row, with what the customer asked for, what it involved (hours, materials), and the final price at clamp(1.75rem, 3vw, 2.5rem) in tabular figures. Under them, the pricing rule in one paragraph with text-wrap: pretty (We charge 65 an hour plus parts at cost). Stacked vertically, max 48rem. Corner radius 0; separated by full-width rules.
motion: None beyond a 200ms fade on entry.
still_check: Any still shows each job and its price.
mobile: Same layout at 375px with smaller price type.
a11y: Prices are text with currency spelled for screen readers when ambiguous. Reduced motion: no fade.
avoid: Tier names like Gold, three equal cards side by side, or jobs with no price.

stack_notes.css: Plain flow layout.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: The object it started with
blueprint: About told through one founding object (the first oven, the first van, the founder's grandmother's ledger) photographed large at 3:2, clamp(20rem, 50vw, 40rem) wide, beside a short story of 3 paragraphs with text-wrap: pretty and the h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 3rem), text-wrap: balance. Numbered callouts on the object point to marks that tell the story (burn mark from 1998, the dent from the first delivery). Corner radius 0; callout markers 1.5rem squares with 2px corners.
motion: Entering view, callout markers pop in one by one 100ms apart; hovering a marker highlights its story sentence.
still_check: Any still shows object, markers and full story.
mobile: At 375px object on top, callouts listed under it.
a11y: Markers are buttons linked to sentences via aria-describedby. Reduced motion: no pop.
avoid: Generic origin stories with no object, stock vintage photos, or more than 5 callouts.

stack_notes.css: Markers absolutely positioned in percentages; @starting-style for entry; logical positioning for the story column.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: This week, counted
blueprint: About section as a plain-sentence paragraph of this week's real counts set at clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2.25rem), text-wrap: pretty, where each number is set in tabular figures and slightly heavier weight: This week we baked 1,140 loaves, answered 86 calls and drove 412 miles. A small updated-on date beneath. Max 44rem. Corner radius 0; no boxes.
motion: Numbers count up once on entry in 700ms, ending on the true value; sentence remains readable throughout because numbers are fixed-width.
still_check: Any still shows the sentence with every number (final values in the HTML).
mobile: Same at 375px with smaller type.
a11y: Real numbers in the DOM; count-up only in visuals. Reduced motion: no count.
avoid: Stats tiles in a row, round fake numbers, or numbers never updated.

stack_notes.css: Count via a registered integer custom property and counter(); tabular-nums prevents reflow.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Asked this week
blueprint: FAQ built from the questions customers actually asked recently, each with how many times it came up and the date last asked in small tabular text; questions at clamp(1.125rem, 1.8vw, 1.375rem) with text-wrap: balance, answers with text-wrap: pretty, max 3 sentences, ending with a link to the full policy where relevant. Grouped under before, during and after. Max 46rem. Corner radius 0; 1px rules between questions.
motion: Opening a question grows its height via interpolate-size in 200ms.
still_check: Any still shows every question readable; at least one open.
mobile: Same at 375px.
a11y: details/summary; group headings are h3. Reduced motion: instant.
avoid: Marketing questions nobody asks (Why are you so great?), answers longer than 3 sentences, or hiding cancellation terms.

stack_notes.css: details with ::details-content transitions; logical padding.
stack_notes.js: None required.

name: Reach us by how urgent it is
blueprint: Contact sorted by urgency, 3 stacked bands: Right now (phone number at clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem) in tabular figures, with who answers and until when), Today (message or callback form of 2 fields), This week (email and the reply time you keep). The h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.5rem), text-wrap: balance. Bands full width, stacked, the urgent one in the strongest ink. Corner radius 0 on bands; form fields 4px.
motion: The Right now band shows a live open or closed state with a dot that pulses once per 4s only while open.
still_check: Any still shows all three bands and their contact routes.
mobile: At 375px the phone number is a tap-to-call link 3rem tall.
a11y: tel: and mailto: links; open state as text, not colour only. Reduced motion: no pulse.
avoid: A single contact form for everything, phone numbers as images, or reply times you do not keep.

stack_notes.css: Server-rendered open state with a small script refresh; plain stacked bands.
stack_notes.js: Optional: recompute open state each minute; clear interval on unmount.

name: Light table of real work
blueprint: Gallery laid out as prints on a back-lit light table: photographs at mixed real aspect ratios (3:2, 4:5, 1:1) arranged in a loose grid with 1.5rem gaps on a pale glowing ground, each print slightly rotated (-1.5 to 1.5deg) with a small handwritten-style label in the margin printed as real text. The h2 at clamp(1.75rem, 3.5vw, 2.75rem), text-wrap: balance. Clicking a print lifts it into a dialog view. Corner radius 0 on prints; dialog 2px.
motion: Hover straightens a print to 0deg and lifts it 6px with a softer shadow in 200ms. Opening uses a view transition from the print to the dialog image.
still_check: Any still shows every print with its label legible.
mobile: At 375px prints become a 2-column grid without rotation.
a11y: Each print is a button opening a dialog with focus trap; images have alt. Reduced motion: no rotation, no lift, instant dialog.
avoid: Masonry of stock, autoplaying carousels, or rotation on body text.
